questions.stem: About how much alcohol can the liver oxidize in an hour?

options.text: About one drink
About three drinks
It depends entirely on body weight

questions.correctOption: About one drink
questions.explanation: The liver works at a fixed rate of roughly one drink an hour. Body weight changes how high your BAC climbs, but not how fast it falls.

citations.quote: the liver can only oxidize about one drink per hour. Contrary to popular belief, this rate cannot be increased by drinking coffee, exercising, taking a cold shower or anything else. Only time can sober a person who's been drinking.

questions.stem: Coffee, a cold shower or exercise will:

options.text: Lower blood alcohol concentration by about half
Speed up the rate at which alcohol leaves the body
Do nothing to speed up sobering — only time will

questions.correctOption: Do nothing to speed up sobering — only time will
questions.explanation: These tricks may make a drinker feel more awake, but the alcohol is still in the blood. Only time sobers someone up.

citations.quote: the liver can only oxidize about one drink per hour. Contrary to popular belief, this rate cannot be increased by drinking coffee, exercising, taking a cold shower or anything else. Only time can sober a person who's been drinking.

questions.stem: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures:

options.text: The percentage of alcohol in the blood
How long it has been since the last drink
The number of drinks consumed in the last hour

questions.correctOption: The percentage of alcohol in the blood
questions.explanation: BAC is a percentage of alcohol in the blood, and impairment climbs as that number climbs.

citations.quote: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is a measurement of the percentage of alcohol in the blood. The higher the BAC number, the more impaired a person is.

questions.stem: In Tennessee, the blood alcohol concentration that is always illegal for a driver 21 or older is:
questions.explanation: Point-oh-eight is the line above which intoxication is illegal in Tennessee and most other states — but a driver can be convicted below it.

citations.quote: In most states, including Tennessee, .08 is the level of intoxication which is always illegal.

questions.stem: The first ability alcohol affects is:

options.text: Hearing
Muscle strength
Judgment

questions.correctOption: Judgment
questions.explanation: Judgment goes first, which is exactly why an impaired driver is a poor judge of whether they are impaired.

citations.quote: The first thing affected after drinking alcohol is a person's judgment.

questions.stem: Alcohol, in any concentration, is:

options.text: A stimulant
A depressant
A stimulant at low doses and a depressant at high doses

questions.correctOption: A depressant
questions.explanation: It is a depressant at every concentration. Feeling lively after a drink is loss of inhibition, not stimulation.

citations.quote: Alcohol, in any concentration, is a depressant, not a stimulant.

questions.stem: Alcohol reduces the ability to see clearly at night by:

options.text: More than half
Less than a tenth
About a quarter

questions.correctOption: More than half
questions.explanation: Night vision is more than halved, and glare recovery slows too — which is why drinking and night driving is such a bad combination.

citations.quote: It reduces the ability to see clearly at night by more than half

questions.stem: At a BAC of .05 percent, side vision is reduced by about:

options.text: 5 percent
30 percent
60 percent

questions.correctOption: 30 percent
questions.explanation: Losing roughly a third of your side vision means missing the cross traffic, the cyclist and the child at the curb.

citations.quote: Side vision is reduced by about 30 percent at .05 percent BAC.

questions.stem: Reaction time and coordination begin to be impaired at a BAC as low as:

options.text: .15 percent
.02 percent
.08 percent

questions.correctOption: .02 percent
questions.explanation: Impairment starts far below the legal limit — about one drink's worth for many people.

citations.quote: Reaction and coordination are impaired by alcohol consumption as low as .02 percent BAC.

questions.stem: According to the manual, driving skills, judgment and vision are already greatly impaired at BAC levels as low as:

options.text: .03 and .04 percent
.08 and .09 percent
.12 and .13 percent

questions.correctOption: .03 and .04 percent
questions.explanation: Well under the legal limit. The manual also states flatly that everyone at .10 percent is too impaired to drive safely.

citations.quote: ALL people at the .10 percent level are definitely too impaired to drive safely. Research has proven that driving skills, good judgment and vision are greatly impaired at BAC levels as low as .03 and .04 percent

questions.stem: At a BAC of .10 percent, a driver is about how much more likely to cause a crash than a sober driver?

options.text: Seven times as likely
Fifty times as likely
Twice as likely

questions.correctOption: Seven times as likely
questions.explanation: Seven times at .10, twenty-five times at .15, and fifty times at .17 — the risk does not rise gently, it explodes.

citations.quote: With a BAC of .10 percent, you are seven times more likely to cause a crash than if you were sober. As your BAC increases to .15 percent, your chances of causing a traffic crash increase to 25 times. At .17 percent BAC, you are 50 times more likely to cause a crash.

questions.stem: The alcohol in one 12-ounce bottle of beer is about the same as the alcohol in:

options.text: Three shots of whiskey
A 1-ounce shot of whiskey
A half-gallon of wine

questions.correctOption: A 1-ounce shot of whiskey
questions.explanation: Beer, wine and spirits are served in different sizes precisely because their strength differs. A drink is a drink.

citations.quote: The amount of alcohol in one (12 ounce) bottle of beer is about equal to that in a (1 ounce) shot of whiskey.

questions.stem: About how long does it take to cancel the intoxicating effects of one drink?

options.text: Fifteen minutes
About one hour
About four hours

questions.correctOption: About one hour
questions.explanation: One hour per drink. Three drinks, three hours — and no shortcut shortens it.

citations.quote: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink. It takes about three hours to cancel the intoxicating effects of three drinks.

questions.stem: About what share of the information a driver uses comes from the eyes?

options.text: Almost 90 percent
About 25 percent
Almost half

questions.correctOption: Almost 90 percent
questions.explanation: Nearly everything you use to drive comes in through your eyes, so anything that degrades vision — alcohol, glare, fog — degrades driving.

citations.quote: Because the eyes provide almost 90 percent of the information used in driving, any restriction in vision can cause disastrous results.

questions.stem: A driver who has been drinking takes unnecessary risks such as speeding around curves or passing without enough clear distance. This is mainly a failure of:

options.text: Grip strength
Night vision
Judgment

questions.correctOption: Judgment
questions.explanation: Alcohol lowers concern for physical wellbeing, so risks that would look obviously stupid sober start to look fine.

citations.quote: Good judgment decreases with the use of alcohol. The concern for physical well being also lessens. People under the influence of alcohol take unnecessary and dangerous risks.

questions.stem: The two abilities most important to driving, and most affected by small amounts of alcohol, are:

options.text: Judgment and vision
Hearing and balance
Strength and stamina

questions.correctOption: Judgment and vision
questions.explanation: Both are affected after a single drink, and both are the abilities driving depends on most.

citations.quote: The two abilities most important to the driving task are judgment and vision, both of which are affected by small amounts of alcohol.

questions.stem: Alcohol affects a driver's ability to judge:

options.text: Only distance
Only the passage of time
Speed, time and distance

questions.correctOption: Speed, time and distance
questions.explanation: All three go together, and all three are altered after a single drink — which is why gaps look bigger and closing speeds look slower.

citations.quote: Your ability to judge speed, time and distance are altered after only one drink.

questions.stem: Glare vision and glare recovery in a drinking driver are:

options.text: Unaffected by alcohol
Improved, because the pupils widen
Made worse, because eye muscles relax and recovery slows

questions.correctOption: Made worse, because eye muscles relax and recovery slows
questions.explanation: Relaxed eye muscles cannot focus properly, and the eyes take longer to recover after oncoming headlights — a longer stretch of driving effectively blind.

citations.quote: Glare vision is poor because of relaxed eye muscles. Glare recovery is also slowed by alcohol.

questions.stem: In Tennessee it is unlawful to drive or be in physical control of a vehicle while under the influence of:

options.text: Alcohol only
Any intoxicant, marijuana, narcotic drug or stimulant drug
Only substances that are illegal to possess

questions.correctOption: Any intoxicant, marijuana, narcotic drug or stimulant drug
questions.explanation: The DUI statute covers any intoxicant that impairs you, whether it came from a bar, a dealer or a pharmacy.

citations.quote: 1. Under the influence of any intoxicant, marijuana, narcotic drug or drugs producing stimulating effects on the central nervous system; or 2. While the alcohol concentration of the operator's blood or breath is .08 percent or higher.

questions.stem: A driver who registers a BAC of .00 percent:

options.text: Can still be convicted of DUI
Can only be charged with reckless driving
Cannot be convicted of DUI

questions.correctOption: Can still be convicted of DUI
questions.explanation: DUI is about impairment, not just about a number. Drugs — including prescription drugs — impair without registering any alcohol at all.

citations.quote: A driver can register a BAC of .00 percent and still be convicted of a DUI. The level of BAC does not clear a driver when it is below .08 percent.

questions.stem: A BAC reading below .08 percent means the driver:

options.text: Is automatically cleared of DUI
Is not cleared — a driver can still be convicted
Will be charged only if there was a crash

questions.correctOption: Is not cleared — a driver can still be convicted
questions.explanation: The manual says it plainly: a level below .08 does not clear a driver.

citations.quote: A driver can register a BAC of .00 percent and still be convicted of a DUI. The level of BAC does not clear a driver when it is below .08 percent.

questions.stem: Having a valid prescription for a drug that impairs your driving is:

options.text: A complete defense to a DUI charge
No defense to driving under the influence of it
A defense only for a first offense

questions.correctOption: No defense to driving under the influence of it
questions.explanation: A prescription makes possession legal. It does not make impaired driving legal.

citations.quote: Just because a drug is prescribed, by law, this is NO defense for driving under the influence of it.

questions.stem: Tennessee's Implied Consent Law means that by driving in this state you have already agreed to:

options.text: Carry collision insurance
Be tested for alcohol or drug content when an officer has reasonable grounds
Waive your right to a hearing

questions.correctOption: Be tested for alcohol or drug content when an officer has reasonable grounds
questions.explanation: Your consent came with the driving privilege. The officer still needs reasonable grounds to believe you were driving impaired.

citations.quote: By law, when you drive in Tennessee, you have given your consent to be tested to determine the alcohol or drug content of your blood. This test must be administered at the request of a law enforcement officer who has reasonable grounds to believe you have been driving under the influence of an intoxicant or drug.

questions.stem: A driver who is placed under arrest and refuses the officer's request for a blood alcohol test will likely:

options.text: Have driving privileges suspended by the court for twelve months
Face no consequence, since the test is voluntary
Receive a written warning for a first refusal

questions.correctOption: Have driving privileges suspended by the court for twelve months
questions.explanation: Refusal is its own violation of the implied consent law, and the likely penalty is a twelve-month suspension — separate from anything the DUI charge brings.

citations.quote: If you are placed under arrest and a law enforcement officer asks you to take the test and you refuse, it will likely result in the suspension by the court of your driving privileges for twelve (12) months.

questions.stem: Tennessee's "No Refusal" law allows law enforcement to:

options.text: Suspend a license at the roadside without a court
Arrest a driver without probable cause
Seek a search warrant for a blood sample from a suspected impaired driver

questions.correctOption: Seek a search warrant for a blood sample from a suspected impaired driver
questions.explanation: Refusing the test does not end the matter — officers can go to a judge for a warrant and take the sample anyway.

citations.quote: The No Refusal law was passed in 2012 and allows law enforcement officials to seek search warrants for blood samples in cases involving suspected impaired drivers.

questions.stem: The implied consent test is administered at the request of:

options.text: The driver's insurance company
Any citizen who witnessed the driving
A law enforcement officer with reasonable grounds to believe you were driving under the influence

questions.correctOption: A law enforcement officer with reasonable grounds to believe you were driving under the influence
questions.explanation: Reasonable grounds are the trigger — an officer cannot demand a test of a driver at random.

citations.quote: By law, when you drive in Tennessee, you have given your consent to be tested to determine the alcohol or drug content of your blood. This test must be administered at the request of a law enforcement officer who has reasonable grounds to believe you have been driving under the influence of an intoxicant or drug.

questions.stem: Tennessee's DUI law applies on public streets and highways, and also:

options.text: On shopping center, trailer park and apartment complex premises and other places frequented by the public
Only where a speed limit is posted
Only on interstates

questions.correctOption: On shopping center, trailer park and apartment complex premises and other places frequented by the public
questions.explanation: Private parking lots that the public uses are covered. "I never left the parking lot" is not a defense.

citations.quote: on the premises of any shopping center, trailer park, apartment house complex, or any place frequented by the public

questions.stem: Under Tennessee law you can be charged with DUI when you are:

options.text: Only when the vehicle is moving in traffic
Driving the vehicle only
Driving or in physical control of the vehicle

questions.correctOption: Driving or in physical control of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Physical control counts. Sitting behind the wheel of a running car while impaired can be enough.

citations.quote: it is unlawful for any person to drive or be in physical control of an automobile or other motor-driven vehicle on any public street, highway, road or alley

questions.stem: A person whose license is revoked for DUI and who then applies for a photo identification license will find that the ID:

options.text: Must indicate that the person is a DUI offender
Cannot be issued at all
Looks exactly like any other state ID

questions.correctOption: Must indicate that the person is a DUI offender
questions.explanation: The department is required to mark the ID. The credential itself carries the record.

citations.quote: the department is required to indicate on the ID that the person is a DUI offender.

questions.stem: As a condition of probation, a DUI conviction in Tennessee requires the offender to:

options.text: Perform litter pick-up for three eight-hour shifts wearing a vest identifying them as a drunk driver
Serve as a volunteer driving instructor
Attend one victim-impact lecture

questions.correctOption: Perform litter pick-up for three eight-hour shifts wearing a vest identifying them as a drunk driver
questions.explanation: Three eight-hour shifts of roadside litter removal, wearing a vest that says "I am a DRUNK DRIVER."

citations.quote: A DUI conviction also requires as a condition of probation, litter pick-up for three eight-hour shifts. While removing litter, the offender has to wear a vest or other clothing displaying the message, "I am a DRUNK DRIVER."

questions.stem: The manual states that alcohol-related questions make up what share of the knowledge test?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 50 percent
At least 25 percent

questions.correctOption: At least 25 percent
questions.explanation: A quarter of the test comes from the alcohol and drugs chapter — by law, not by custom.

citations.quote: by law, at least 25 percent of the questions on the knowledge test must consist of questions dealing with this topic.

questions.stem: A driver who has been drinking and is stopped by an officer with reasonable grounds may be asked for a test of:

options.text: Fingerprints
Vision only
Blood or breath

questions.correctOption: Blood or breath
questions.explanation: The DUI statute is written around the alcohol concentration of blood or breath, and implied consent covers testing for alcohol or drug content.

citations.quote: 1. Under the influence of any intoxicant, marijuana, narcotic drug or drugs producing stimulating effects on the central nervous system; or 2. While the alcohol concentration of the operator's blood or breath is .08 percent or higher.

questions.stem: Restricted driving privileges after a conviction are NOT available to a driver whose latest offense is:

options.text: Failure to display insurance
A first speeding conviction
Vehicular assault or aggravated vehicular homicide

questions.correctOption: Vehicular assault or aggravated vehicular homicide
questions.explanation: The most serious impaired-driving offenses close the restricted-license door entirely, as does a prior DUI within ten years.

citations.quote: DUI or adult driving while impaired within 10 years; • Vehicular Homicide as the latest result of intoxication; • Aggravated Vehicular Homicide; • Vehicular Assault.

questions.stem: After the first year of a two-year revocation, a driver may apply for a restricted license if they:

options.text: Simply pay the reinstatement fee
Move to another county
Install an ignition interlock device for the remaining period of revocation

questions.correctOption: Install an ignition interlock device for the remaining period of revocation
questions.explanation: The interlock buys back part of the revocation: it must stay on the vehicle for the rest of the revocation period.

citations.quote: After the first year of a two-year revocation, drivers may apply for a restricted driver license if they install an ignition interlock device on the motor vehicle for the remaining period of revocation.

questions.stem: The minimum jail time for a first DUI conviction in Tennessee is:

options.text: There is no minimum
48 hours
30 days

questions.correctOption: 48 hours
questions.explanation: Forty-eight hours is the floor for a first conviction, and the table sets a longer minimum where the BAC was very high.

citations.quote: 48 hours (7 days if BAC is 0.20% or more)

questions.stem: The fine range for a first DUI conviction in Tennessee is:
questions.explanation: And that is only the fine — court costs, bond, attorney fees, treatment and insurance increases come on top.

citations.quote: 1st Conviction 2nd Conviction 3rd Conviction 4th or subsequent Conviction (is a Class E felony)
Jail Time Fines License Revocation Period Vehicle Seizure

questions.stem: The license revocation period for a first DUI conviction is:

options.text: 30 days
1 year
5 years

questions.correctOption: 1 year
questions.explanation: One year for a first conviction, two for a second, three to ten for a third.

citations.quote: 1st Conviction 2nd Conviction 3rd Conviction 4th or subsequent Conviction (is a Class E felony)
1 year 2 years 3 -10 years 5 years [to indefinite]
Jail Time Fines License Revocation Period Vehicle Seizure

questions.stem: On a second DUI conviction, the vehicle:

options.text: Is impounded for exactly 48 hours
Cannot be touched by the state
Is subject to seizure and forfeiture

questions.correctOption: Is subject to seizure and forfeiture
questions.explanation: From the second conviction on, the car itself is on the line.

citations.quote: Vehicle is subject to seizure and forfeiture

questions.stem: A fourth or subsequent DUI conviction in Tennessee is:

options.text: Still a misdemeanor, with a larger fine
A Class C misdemeanor
A Class E felony

questions.correctOption: A Class E felony
questions.explanation: It stops being a misdemeanor. A felony conviction carries consequences that outlast any driving penalty.

citations.quote: 4th or subsequent Conviction (is a Class E felony)

questions.stem: A driver's vehicle will be seized if the driver has:

options.text: Any single DUI conviction
Three moving violations in a year
Two DUI convictions within five years, both after January 1997

questions.correctOption: Two DUI convictions within five years, both after January 1997
questions.explanation: Two convictions inside five years triggers seizure, provided both offenses happened after January 1997.

citations.quote: The driver's vehicle will be seized if he/she has two DUI convictions within five years AND both events happened after January 1997.

questions.stem: An ignition interlock device keeps a vehicle from starting when:

options.text: The driver's BAC is too high
The driver is not wearing a seat belt
The vehicle is overdue for inspection

questions.correctOption: The driver's BAC is too high
questions.explanation: The driver blows into the device before the engine will start, and again at intervals while driving.

citations.quote: Only a motor vehicle equipped with a functioning ignition interlock device (which keeps a car from starting if the driver's BAC is too high).

questions.stem: The ignition interlock restriction for a first DUI offense can last:

options.text: Thirty days
Six months to one year
Ten years

questions.correctOption: Six months to one year
questions.explanation: Six months to a year for a first offense, up to three years for a second, and up to ten years for a third or later.

citations.quote: The restriction can be from six months to one year for a first offense, up to three years for a second offense and up to 10 years for third and subsequent offenses

questions.stem: A person with two DUIs in a five-year period must use an ignition interlock device for how long after reinstatement?

options.text: Two weeks
There is no such requirement
Six months

questions.correctOption: Six months
questions.explanation: The interlock stays on for six months after you get your privileges back — the restriction outlives the revocation.

citations.quote: a person with 2 DUIs in a five year period MUST operate a motor vehicle with the ignition interlock device for six months after reinstatement of driving privileges.

questions.stem: Driving under the influence and causing a crash that kills another person may be charged as:

options.text: Vehicular homicide
Reckless driving only
A non-moving violation

questions.correctOption: Vehicular homicide
questions.explanation: Vehicular homicide carries fines and prison, and it is a permanent bar to a restricted license.

citations.quote: you may be charged with vehicular homicide. If convicted, you may be fined and sentenced to prison.

questions.stem: Driving under the influence and causing a crash that injures another person may be charged as:

options.text: A parking offense
Aggravated assault
Simple trespass

questions.correctOption: Aggravated assault
questions.explanation: An injury crash turns an impaired-driving charge into a violent felony charge carrying fines and prison.

citations.quote: you may be charged with aggravated assault. If convicted, you may be fined and sentenced to prison.

questions.stem: Under the Drunk Driving Child Protection Act, violating the DUI laws while a child under 18 is in the vehicle adds a mandatory minimum of:

options.text: A written warning
One day of community service
30 days in jail and a $1,000 fine

questions.correctOption: 30 days in jail and a $1,000 fine
questions.explanation: Both penalties are mandatory minimums, and both are added on top of everything else the DUI carries.

citations.quote: There is a mandatory minimum jail sentence of 30 days, and a mandatory minimum fine of $1,000. Both of these child-related penalties are added onto any other incarceration, penalty and fines.

questions.stem: If a child suffers serious bodily injury in a DUI crash, the violation is:

options.text: A Class D felony
A Class C misdemeanor
An infraction

questions.correctOption: A Class D felony
questions.explanation: A Class D felony for serious injury, and a Class C felony — especially aggravated child endangerment — if the child dies.

citations.quote: If the child suffers serious bodily injury, the violation is a Class D felony, and if the child dies, it is a Class C felony of especially aggravated child endangerment.

questions.stem: A driver whose privileges are already revoked for DUI and who is caught driving on that revoked license may have the vehicle:

options.text: Re-registered automatically
Seized
Returned with a warning

questions.correctOption: Seized
questions.explanation: Driving on a DUI revocation puts the car itself at risk of seizure, first offense or not.

citations.quote: A vehicle can be seized if a driver is charged with driving on a revoked license when his/her driving privileges are already revoked as a result of a DUI conviction

questions.stem: In addition to jail and fines, a judge will require a DUI offender who had a prior DUI in the previous five years to:

options.text: Retake the road test only
Surrender their vehicle registration permanently
Undergo a drug and alcohol treatment assessment and receive treatment as appropriate

questions.correctOption: Undergo a drug and alcohol treatment assessment and receive treatment as appropriate
questions.explanation: Repeat offenders are assessed and treated, not just punished — the court treats the drinking as the underlying problem.

citations.quote: To undergo a drug and alcohol treatment assessment and receive treatment, as appropriate, for those who have had a prior DUI in the five years prior to the current DUI.

questions.stem: Besides fines and court costs, the manual lists which of these as a real cost of a DUI?

options.text: Increased insurance premiums
A mandatory vehicle upgrade
A higher speed limit allowance

questions.correctOption: Increased insurance premiums
questions.explanation: Bond, attorney fees, lost work, treatment fees and higher premiums add up to thousands of dollars beyond the fine.

citations.quote: increased insurance premiums, and other expenses. This can add up to several thousand dollars.

questions.stem: A DUI offender ordered into a restricted license must, in most cases, submit:

options.text: A letter from an employer only
Nothing beyond the application
Two copies of the court order and proof of SR-22 insurance

questions.correctOption: Two copies of the court order and proof of SR-22 insurance
questions.explanation: Two copies of the court order, proof of financial responsibility, the required tests and the fees.

citations.quote: these applicants must submit two (2) copies of the court order and proof of car insurance/financial responsibility (SR-22 from their insurance company) and pass appropriate tests and pay the required fees.

questions.stem: A restricted license issued after a DUI conviction may permit driving:

options.text: Only between midnight and 6 a.m.
Anywhere, at any time
To and from work, full-time college and religious services

questions.correctOption: To and from work, full-time college and religious services
questions.explanation: The trial judge's order names the permitted trips — work, full-time college, worship and driving that is part of the job.

citations.quote: The restricted license permits the driver to operate a motor vehicle for very specific purposes that are spelled out when the license is issued.

DUI: After conviction for DUI, the trial judge may issue an order for a restricted license to go to and from work, attend college full time, attend religious services at their place of worship, drive as part of employment

questions.stem: A driver who is at least 16 but not yet 21 commits underage driving while impaired at a BAC of:

options.text: .02 percent
.08 percent
.05 percent

questions.correctOption: .02 percent
questions.explanation: Two hundredths of a percent — roughly one drink. Tennessee sets a much lower line for drivers under 21.

citations.quote: A person who is at least 16, but is not yet 21 years old, and who is found: (1) driving with a BAC of .02 percent

questions.stem: The penalty for underage driving while impaired includes:

options.text: A three-month permit restriction
Loss of license for one year and a $250 fine
A warning letter

questions.correctOption: Loss of license for one year and a $250 fine
questions.explanation: A year without a license and a $250 fine, sometimes with public service work attached.

citations.quote: Penalties for this conviction are: losing your license for one year, a fine of $250 and sometimes, includes public service work.

questions.stem: A person 18, 19 or 20 years old who is convicted of purchasing or possessing alcohol loses the privilege to drive for:

options.text: One year
Thirty days
Only until the fine is paid

questions.correctOption: One year
questions.explanation: One year for a first conviction, two for a second — and it applies whether or not a vehicle was involved at all.

citations.quote: you will lose your privilege to drive for one year. If it happens a second time you will lose your license for two years. The law applies to any alcohol-related conviction, whether or not you were driving or even in a vehicle.

questions.stem: The alcohol-conviction suspension for an 18 to 20-year-old applies:

options.text: Whether or not the person was driving or even in a vehicle
Only if the person was in a parking lot
Only if the person was driving at the time

questions.correctOption: Whether or not the person was driving or even in a vehicle
questions.explanation: It is a driving penalty attached to an alcohol conviction, not a driving offense. Buying a beer at 19 can cost a license.

citations.quote: you will lose your privilege to drive for one year. If it happens a second time you will lose your license for two years. The law applies to any alcohol-related conviction, whether or not you were driving or even in a vehicle.

questions.stem: A person between 13 and 17 found to have possessed, consumed or sold alcohol or drugs has driving privileges suspended for:

options.text: Until the next birthday
One year or until age 17, whichever is longer
Thirty days

questions.correctOption: One year or until age 17, whichever is longer
questions.explanation: A second conviction stretches it to two years or until age 18, whichever is longer.

citations.quote: your driving privilege will be suspended for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer

questions.stem: A second juvenile drug or alcohol conviction suspends driving privileges for:

options.text: Six months
Ninety days
Two years or until age 18, whichever is longer

questions.correctOption: Two years or until age 18, whichever is longer
questions.explanation: The suspensions stack toward adulthood — the second one runs to at least age 18.

citations.quote: If you have a second conviction, the suspension is for two years or until age 18, whichever is longer.

questions.stem: A person under 18 may lose driving privileges for a drug or alcohol offense:

options.text: Only for a second offense
Only if it happened while driving
Whether or not the offense occurred while driving

questions.correctOption: Whether or not the offense occurred while driving
questions.explanation: For drivers under 18 the offense does not have to touch a car at all.

citations.quote: In addition, persons under the age of 18 may lose their driving privileges for:
Convictions of any drug or alcohol offense, whether or not the offense occurred while driving; • Dropping out of school

questions.stem: Everyday over-the-counter medicines such as cold remedies and antihistamines:

options.text: Cancel out the effects of alcohol
Never affect driving
Can affect driving ability and should be checked before driving

questions.correctOption: Can affect driving ability and should be checked before driving
questions.explanation: The manual treats "every day" drugs as a real hazard. Read the label, and never mix them with alcohol.

citations.quote: Even some over-the-counter medicines can affect driving.
If you have questions about a particular drug or combination of drugs, check with your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.stem: Combining a prescription or over-the-counter drug with alcohol:

options.text: Can multiply the effect of both
Neutralizes the alcohol
Is safe as long as the dose is small

questions.correctOption: Can multiply the effect of both
questions.explanation: Mixing is where people get caught out: the combined effect is far larger than either substance alone.

citations.quote: when alcohol is combined with another depressant, like tranquilizers or sedatives, the results are not just added together; they are multiplied

questions.stem: Driving under the influence of an illegal drug in Tennessee carries:

options.text: A lesser penalty than alcohol
Only a fine
The same penalties as driving under the influence of alcohol

questions.correctOption: The same penalties as driving under the influence of alcohol
questions.explanation: Same law, same penalties — and prescription drugs are treated the same way.

citations.quote: driving while under the influence of drugs—even prescription drugs—carries the same penalties as for alcohol.

questions.stem: Possession by a driver of five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle is:

options.text: A ground for revoking or suspending a Tennessee driver license
A parking violation
Not connected to driving privileges

questions.correctOption: A ground for revoking or suspending a Tennessee driver license
questions.explanation: It is item 17 on the manual's list of grounds for losing your license.

citations.quote: In Tennessee, a driver license may be revoked or suspended for the following situations:
17. Possession by a driver of five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle.

questions.stem: The best plan for a driver who intends to drink is to:

options.text: Decide in advance not to drive and arrange another way home
Drink only beer
Wait fifteen minutes after the last drink

questions.correctOption: Decide in advance not to drive and arrange another way home
questions.explanation: The manual's prevention advice is to plan before the first drink, because judgment is the first thing you lose.

citations.quote: If you are planning a night on the town, decide before you start drinking that you are not going to drive.

questions.stem: Riding as a passenger with a driver who has been drinking is:

options.text: Only a problem at night
Safe as long as you wear a belt
A serious danger the manual warns young people about specifically

questions.correctOption: A serious danger the manual warns young people about specifically
questions.explanation: The manual singles this out: young people are endangered not only by their own impaired driving but by getting into a car with someone else who is impaired.

citations.quote: Young people remain especially vulnerable to the threat of alcohol and other drugs.
This is not only from their own impaired driving, but also from getting in the car with other drivers who are not sober.

questions.stem: Compared with older drivers, a young driver with a BAC between .01 and .08 percent has:

options.text: A lower chance, because of faster reflexes
A much greater chance of a crash
About the same chance of a crash

questions.correctOption: A much greater chance of a crash
questions.explanation: Low tolerance and limited driving experience combine, so young drivers are in trouble at alcohol levels that would be under the adult limit.

citations.quote: The young driver's chance of a crash is much greater with BAC between .01-.08 percent than older drivers.

questions.stem: Properly adjusted seat head restraints:

options.text: Are designed to prevent whiplash if hit from behind.
Both A and C
Should always be at a level even with the back of head.

questions.correctOption: Both A and C
questions.explanation: The manual makes both statements in one sentence: the restraint sits level with the back of the head, and its job is to stop your head snapping backward in a rear-end crash. Because A and C are both true, the combination answer is the only complete one.

citations.quote: Properly adjust seat head restraints to a level even with the back of the head. Head restraints are designed to prevent whiplash if hit from behind.

questions.stem: The driver should drive with both hands on the steering wheel approximately in the:

options.text: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions
11 o'clock and 6 o'clock positions
7 o'clock and 5 o'clock positions

questions.correctOption: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions
questions.explanation: Hands at 9 and 3 keep your arms clear of the air bag as it deploys. The old 10-and-2 grip puts your forearms directly over the bag.

citations.quote: drivers should place the left hand at the 9 o'clock position and the right hand at 3 o'clock position on the steering wheel. This position helps avoid injury from air bag deployment during an accident.

questions.stem: When adjusting the driver's seat for best driving posture, set the seat in an upright position where your body is about how far from the steering wheel?

options.text: 6 to 8 inches
10 to 12 inches
18 to 24 inches

questions.correctOption: 10 to 12 inches
questions.explanation: Ten to twelve inches gives the air bag room to inflate before it reaches you, and still lets you reach the pedals and wheel comfortably.

citations.quote: Your body should be about 10 to 12 inches back from the steering wheel with or without an air bag.

questions.stem: A child in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) should:

options.text: be facing the rear of the car if weighing less than 20 pounds and under 1 year old.
be facing forward if the child is one through three years old, and weighs more than 20 pounds,
A & B

questions.correctOption: A & B
questions.explanation: Tennessee sets both rules: rear-facing under one year old or under 20 pounds, forward-facing from one through three years old at over 20 pounds. Both statements are law, so the combination is correct.

citations.quote: A child under one year old, or any child weighing less than 20 pounds, must be in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) that is facing the rear of the car.
Children who are one through three years old, and who weigh more than 20 pounds, must be in a child passenger restraint system that is facing forward.

questions.stem: The lap belt should be worn:

options.text: at the abdomen for extra comfort .
above the pelvis so it doesn't touch the top of the thighs.
by pregnant women below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.

questions.correctOption: by pregnant women below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.
questions.explanation: A lap belt belongs low, across the hip bones — never across the soft abdomen. For a pregnant driver that means the lap belt under the belly and the shoulder belt above it.

citations.quote: Pregnant women should wear the lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.
The lap belt should be worn low over the pelvis with the bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs snugly.

questions.stem: The safest place for children 12 and under to ride in a vehicle equipped with air bags is:

options.text: The front seat
The back seat
The bed of a pick-up truck

questions.correctOption: The back seat
questions.explanation: A deploying passenger air bag can seriously injure a child. The manual's rule is simple: children 12 and under ride in the back seat.

citations.quote: CHILDREN ages 12 and under are safer in the back seat of a vehicle.

questions.stem: The sign at the right means:

options.text: Slow down and yield to traffic on main road when merging.
Always come to a complete stop.
Give your turn signal and proceed into traffic at regular speed.

questions.correctOption: Slow down and yield to traffic on main road when merging.
questions.explanation: A yield sign is not a stop sign. You slow down, and you stop only if traffic on the other roadway requires it — but you must give way either way.

citations.quote: Triangular Shape - Yield This three-sided sign means that you are approaching an intersection and must stop and wait when other vehicles are approaching from the right or left on the other roadway. If you are sure no other cars are coming you need not come to a complete stop but you must slow down and enter the intersection with caution.

questions.artworkNote: The manual prints this question beside a picture of the sign, and the picture is not in the PDF's text layer. The manual's own answer pointer sends the reader to printed page 36 (PDF 50), where the only sign matching answer A is the YIELD sign, and the keyed answer restates the manual's yield rule almost word for word. The app therefore renders its own YIELD sign (registry id r1-2-yield) next to the stem rather than dropping the question or guessing at unseen artwork.

questions.stem: What does a traffic signal with a yellow left arrow indicate to the driver?

options.text: Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
Protected left turn is about to end.
Both of the above.

questions.correctOption: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: The green arrow gave you a protected turn. When it changes to yellow that protection is ending, and oncoming traffic is about to get its own green — so both statements describe the same moment.

citations.quote: PROTECTED ARROWS: At many intersections, you may see what is called a "protected turn arrow." When the arrow is green, you have the right-of-way and may drive the vehicle only in the direction of the arrow, after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
When the arrow changes to yellow, prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.stem: The center of the roadway is marked with one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken yellow line is on the right of the solid yellow line (your side) it means:

options.text: You are not allowed to pass in this area.
You are in a "passing zone" and it is safe to pass other vehicles if no oncoming traffic is present.
You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.

questions.correctOption: You are in a "passing zone" and it is safe to pass other vehicles if no oncoming traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Read the line on your own side of the center. Broken on your side means passing is permitted when the way is clear; solid on your side means it is not.

citations.quote: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in the "passing zone" and may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.stem: It is illegal to park:

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctOption: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Both distances are on the manual's no-parking list, so neither single answer is complete.

citations.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant • Within a fire lane • Within 20 feet of a crosswalk or in the crosswalk marked area • Within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street or on the other side of the street within 75 feet of the fire station driveway • Within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or any other traffic control device • Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing

questions.stem: The two-second rule for following at a safe distance will hold true at:

options.text: Speeds up to 30 m.p.h.
Any speed.
Speeds up to 55 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: Any speed.
questions.explanation: The rule measures time, not distance, so it scales with speed automatically. In bad weather, at interstate speeds, at night, or behind a motorcycle, the manual asks for four seconds instead.

citations.quote: This principle will hold true at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits.
A minimum of four seconds should allow for better reaction time and a safer space cushion under these conditions including following a motorcycle.

questions.stem: Which lane must you be in before making a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctOption: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: On a one-way street the whole width is yours to choose from, so the left turn starts from the lane closest to the left curb and finishes in the first lane on the left of the new street.

citations.quote: Make your approach in the traffic lane furthermost to the left curb of the street. • Turn sharply into the first lane on the left side of the one-way street. DO NOT TURN WIDE.

questions.stem: Motorists are required by law when passing a bicycle traveling in the same direction to allow a minimum distance of:

options.text: 1 foot
3 feet
Safely away from the bicycle.

questions.correctOption: 3 feet
questions.explanation: Three feet is the legal minimum, and you have to hold that clearance until you are safely past — not just at the moment you draw level.

citations.quote: leave at least a distance between you and the bicycle of not less than 3 feet. It's the law! Also be sure to maintain this clearance until safely past the overtaken bicycle.

questions.stem: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars and enter when safe.
Check for cars, reduce speed to 25 MPH before entering traffic lane.
Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic and merge when the way is clear.

questions.correctOption: Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic and merge when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Entering an interstate reverses the usual habit: you use the acceleration lane to get up to the speed of traffic, then merge. Stopping on a ramp invites a rear-end collision.

citations.quote: You must use the merging or acceleration lane to speed up and merge with fast-moving traffic already on the interstate.

questions.stem: Emergency crossovers on the interstate are legal in Tennessee for:

options.text: Making a U-Turn when you missed your exit.
Turning around when no others are present.
Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

questions.correctOption: Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.
questions.explanation: U-turns on the interstate are illegal for ordinary drivers, crossover or not. If you miss your exit, go on to the next one.

citations.quote: It is illegal in Tennessee for any driver to make a U-turn on an interstate highway. Emergency crossovers are for the use of emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

questions.stem: Interstate driving demands require the driver to:

options.text: Have a complete awareness of higher speed driving
Constant alertness by the driver
Both of the above.

questions.correctOption: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: The manual names both demands in the same sentence, so neither one alone answers the question.

citations.quote: Safe use of the interstates demands a complete awareness of a higher speed type of driving and constant alertness by the driver.

questions.stem: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels causing the loss of steering control.
Keeps the brakes hot and prevents them from freezing.

questions.correctOption: Locks the front wheels causing the loss of steering control.
questions.explanation: Locked front wheels cannot steer — the car goes wherever its momentum takes it. Use steady pressure instead of stamping on the pedal.

citations.quote: Continuous hard braking on snow and ice can result in the locking of the front brakes causing a loss of steering.

questions.stem: When driving in foggy conditions, do not put your headlights on high beam because:

options.text: The light from the fog creates blurry vision on your eyes.
Approaching vehicles won't be able to see your oncoming vehicle.
Low beams provide greater visibility and you can be better seen by other vehicles.

questions.correctOption: Low beams provide greater visibility and you can be better seen by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: High beams bounce off the water droplets straight back at you. Low beams put the light on the road and still let other drivers see you coming.

citations.quote: In fog or mist, never put your headlights on high beam because the light will be reflected back into your eyes.

WHEN DRIVING THROUGH DENSE FOG, HEAVY RAIN OR SNOW DURING THE DAYTIME, TURN ON YOU LOW BEAM HEADLIGHTS. This gives you better visibility and alerts oncoming cars to your presence, it is also a requirement of Tennessee law.

questions.stem: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer because of less traffic and less distractions.
More hazardous because your range of visibility is limited by your headlights.
Safer and allows you to increase your speed while adjusting to road conditions.

questions.correctOption: More hazardous because your range of visibility is limited by your headlights.
questions.explanation: At night you can only see as far as your headlights reach, so your stopping distance has to stay inside that. The manual's phrase for it is: never outrun your headlights.

citations.quote: Driving at night is considerably more hazardous and difficult than daytime driving because your range of visibility is limited by your headlights.
The basic rule for safe night driving is this: NEVER OUTRUN YOUR HEADLIGHTS.

questions.stem: Driving while under the influence of drugs carries:

options.text: The same penalty as for alcohol
A lesser penalty than for alcohol.
Absolutely no penalty at all.

questions.correctOption: The same penalty as for alcohol
questions.explanation: Tennessee treats drug impairment exactly like alcohol impairment — and a valid prescription is not a defense.

citations.quote: driving while under the influence of drugs—even prescription drugs—carries the same penalties as for alcohol.
Just because a drug is prescribed, by law, this is NO defense for driving under the influence of it.

questions.stem: If you have had three beers in the past hour, about how long will it take for all the alcohol to leave your blood stream?

options.text: One hour
Two hours
Three hours

questions.correctOption: Three hours
questions.explanation: The liver clears roughly one drink per hour and nothing speeds it up — not coffee, not a shower, not food. Three drinks means about three hours.

citations.quote: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink. It takes about three hours to cancel the intoxicating effects of three drinks.

the liver can only oxidize about one drink per hour. Contrary to popular belief, this rate cannot be increased by drinking coffee, exercising, taking a cold shower or anything else. Only time can sober a person who's been drinking.

questions.stem: As the percentage of alcohol (BAC) in your blood increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated
More sober
More coordinated

questions.correctOption: More intoxicated
questions.explanation: BAC is a direct measure of how much alcohol is in your blood, and impairment rises with it. Alcohol is a depressant at every concentration.

citations.quote: As the percentage of alcohol in your blood increases, you become more intoxicated.
Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is a measurement of the percentage of alcohol in the blood. The higher the BAC number, the more impaired a person is.
Alcohol, in any concentration, is a depressant, not a stimulant.

questions.stem: Implied Consent Law means:

options.text: If asked, you will take a test to determine alcohol or drug content in the blood.
The laws apply even without any signs, markings or signals present at an intersection.
The owner of the vehicle will carry proper insurance.

questions.correctOption: If asked, you will take a test to determine alcohol or drug content in the blood.
questions.explanation: By driving in Tennessee you have already consented to testing when an officer has reasonable grounds. Refusing after arrest is itself punished — a likely twelve-month suspension.

citations.quote: By law, when you drive in Tennessee, you have given your consent to be tested to determine the alcohol or drug content of your blood. This test must be administered at the request of a law enforcement officer who has reasonable grounds to believe you have been driving under the influence of an intoxicant or drug.

If you are placed under arrest and a law enforcement officer asks you to take the test and you refuse, it will likely result in the suspension by the court of your driving privileges for twelve (12) months.

questions.stem: Which of the following driving skills are affected by the use of alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration
Reaction time and coordination
All of the above are affected.

questions.correctOption: All of the above are affected.
questions.explanation: The manual lists judgment, vision, reaction time, coordination, alertness and concentration — every one of them degrades, which is why no single option is complete.

citations.quote: In addition, your reaction time and coordination begin to deteriorate, while your alertness and concentration fade.

questions.stem: If involved in a reportable accident, the operator of the vehicle must file an accident report to the Department of Safety within:

options.text: 10 Days
20 Days
48 Hours

questions.correctOption: 20 Days
questions.explanation: Twenty days, and it applies regardless of who was at fault. Missing the deadline can cost you your driving and registration privileges.

citations.quote: Regardless of who is to blame, the operator and/or owner of a vehicle involved in a reportable crash in this state must file an Owner/Driver Report of the crash to the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security within 20 days.
Failure to report a crash may result in suspension of driving and registration privileges.

questions.pointerNote: The manual's pointer says printed page 88, but the 20-day rule is printed on page 89 (PDF 103). The citation below points at the rule's real location.

questions.stem: If you are not the first at the scene of accident and your help is not needed, what should you do:

options.text: Slow down to calm your nerves.
Stop and look for your own curiosity.
Drive on and do not interfere with procedures.

questions.correctOption: Drive on and do not interfere with procedures.
questions.explanation: Unless you are trained to give aid, the most useful thing you can do is keep moving and leave the road clear for police, fire and ambulance crews.

citations.quote: If you are not professionally trained to render aid, slowly continue on in your vehicle so not to interfere with the arrival of police and emergency medical and fire/rescue services.

questions.stem: A driver license may be revoked or suspended for:

options.text: Frequent convictions of traffic law violations resulting in 12 or more "points" within a 12 month period
Fraudulently altering a driver license
Both of the above

questions.correctOption: Both of the above
questions.explanation: Twelve points in twelve months starts suspension proceedings for an adult driver, and unlawful use of a license — including altering one — is its own separate ground for revocation.

citations.quote: Adult drivers (18 years of age or older) who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.
Allowing unlawful use of a driver license, including fraudulently altering a driver license or allowing another individual to use your license or identification.

questions.stem: Unless a different limit is posted, the speed limit on Tennessee's primary and secondary state and federal highways is:
questions.explanation: Fifty-five is the statewide default. A posted sign always wins, but where there is no sign, this is the number.

citations.quote: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 m.p.h.

questions.stem: The maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways is:
questions.explanation: Seventy is the statutory ceiling. Urban stretches are often posted lower, and the posted number is the one that binds you.

citations.quote: The maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways is 70 m.p.h.

questions.stem: On congested urban or metropolitan stretches of Tennessee interstate, the limit is typically:
questions.explanation: Traffic volume, merging and exits are all denser in the cities, so the posted limit typically drops to 55.

citations.quote: In the more congested urban or metropolitan areas of Tennessee interstates, the limit is typically 55 m.p.h.

questions.stem: Driving slower than 55 m.p.h. in the left-most lane of an interstate is:

options.text: Unlawful unless congestion prevents driving safely at that speed
Always permitted
Permitted whenever you are signaling

questions.correctOption: Unlawful unless congestion prevents driving safely at that speed
questions.explanation: The left lane is for passing and for moving traffic. If congestion makes 55 unsafe, the rule gives way; otherwise, move right.

citations.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle less than 55 m.p.h. in the left most lane of any Interstate highway, unless traffic congestion and flow prevent safe driving at such speed.

questions.stem: The minimum speed limit in the right lane or lanes of a Tennessee interstate is:
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions everything on the interstate must move at 45 or better, including in the right lanes.

citations.quote: On the interstates, the minimum speed limit in the right lane(s) is 45 m.p.h., and under normal driving conditions, all vehicles must travel at least this fast

questions.stem: Where no minimum speed is posted, driving so slowly that you block traffic is:

options.text: Against the law
Legal only on two-lane roads
Legal, since no minimum is posted

questions.correctOption: Against the law
questions.explanation: Obstructing the flow is an offense in its own right — a posted minimum is not what makes it illegal.

citations.quote: If there is noposted minimum speed, it is still against the law to drive so slowly that you block traffic.

questions.stem: You are considered to be driving a slow-moving vehicle when your speed is:

options.text: More than 25 m.p.h. below the limit
10 m.p.h. or more below the lawful maximum
Any speed under 45 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: 10 m.p.h. or more below the lawful maximum
questions.explanation: Ten under the lawful maximum is the line. Below it you are an obstruction other drivers have to work around.

citations.quote: You are considered to be driving a slow-moving vehicle if you are traveling at a rate of speed that is 10 miles per hour or more below the lawful maximum speed.

questions.stem: If five or more vehicles are lined up behind you on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Maintain your speed and let them wait
Turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely
Speed up to the posted limit even if conditions do not allow it

questions.correctOption: Turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely
questions.explanation: A queue behind you invites risky passing. Letting it clear is safer for everyone, including you.

citations.quote: If five or more vehicles are lined up behind you, turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely.

questions.stem: Exceeding the speed limit in a school zone is by law considered:

options.text: An equipment violation
A warning-only offense for a first occurrence
Reckless driving, with an automatic six points

questions.correctOption: Reckless driving, with an automatic six points
questions.explanation: It is not treated as ordinary speeding. The charge is reckless driving and six points land on your record automatically.

citations.quote: Exceeding the school zone speed limit is by law considered to be reckless driving. The penalty includes an automatic six points added to your driving record

questions.stem: Tennessee law mandates what fine range for violating a posted speed limit in an active work zone?

options.text: A flat $25
No fine, only points
A minimum of $250 and a maximum of $500

questions.correctOption: A minimum of $250 and a maximum of $500
questions.explanation: The minimum is a floor a judge cannot go under, because work zones put people on foot a few feet from moving traffic.

citations.quote: TENNESSEE LAW MANDATES A MINIMUM FINE OF $250 DOLLARS AND UP TO A MAXIMUM FINE OF $500 DOLLARS FOR VIOLATIONS OF THE SPEED LIMIT POSTED IN ACTIVE WORK ZONES.

questions.stem: If a work zone has no reduced speed limit posted, drivers should:

options.text: Obey the normal posted speed limit
Automatically reduce speed by 20 m.p.h.
Stop and wait for a flagger

questions.correctOption: Obey the normal posted speed limit
questions.explanation: No reduced posting means the normal limit still applies — though conditions may call for less.

citations.quote: if there are no reduced speed limit postings, drivers should obey the normal posted speed limit.

questions.stem: While passing another vehicle, exceeding the posted speed limit is:

options.text: Permitted if it shortens the pass
Illegal
Permitted only on the interstate

questions.correctOption: Illegal
questions.explanation: There is no passing exemption. If the pass needs more speed than the limit allows, it is not a pass you can legally make.

citations.quote: Remember, it is illegal to exceed the speed posted speed limit even when passing other vehicles.

questions.stem: The Basic Speed Rule described in the manual is:

options.text: A federal interstate regulation
A Tennessee law with its own fine
A general safety principle, not a Tennessee law

questions.correctOption: A general safety principle, not a Tennessee law
questions.explanation: The principle — that conditions, not the sign, set your real safe speed — is guidance rather than a statute in Tennessee.

citations.quote: The Basic Speed Rule (BSR) is not a Tennessee law, but it is a general safety principle.

questions.stem: When you meet a properly identified funeral procession on a two-lane roadway you may not:

options.text: Sound your horn
Pass the procession, or drive between its vehicles unless a traffic officer directs you to
Stop your vehicle

questions.correctOption: Pass the procession, or drive between its vehicles unless a traffic officer directs you to
questions.explanation: Cutting into a procession breaks it up and puts the vehicles behind into a gap they did not expect.

citations.quote: Vehicles following a funeral procession on a two-lane roadway may not attempt to pass such procession; and • No operator of a vehicle shall drive between vehicles in a properly identified funeral procession except when directed to do so by a traffic officer.

questions.stem: Tennessee's right-of-way law:

options.text: Gives certain drivers the right-of-way
Only says who must yield the right-of-way
Gives the right-of-way to whoever signals first

questions.correctOption: Only says who must yield the right-of-way
questions.explanation: Nobody is granted the right-of-way — the law only assigns the duty to give it up. You can be legally right and still be responsible for a crash.

citations.quote: The law does not really give anyone the right-of-way. It only says who must yield the right-of-way.

questions.stem: The Left-Right-Left rule at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Look left first, then right, and look both ways again before moving
Always turn left before turning right
Yield to the left, then to the right

questions.correctOption: Look left first, then right, and look both ways again before moving
questions.explanation: Traffic from the left reaches you first, so it gets the first look — and the last look happens right before you move.

citations.quote: The Left-Right-Left Rule: Look first to the left to make sure cross traffic is yielding the right-of-way. Then look for traffic from the right. If stopped, look both left and right just before you start moving.

questions.stem: Blocking an intersection is:

options.text: Legal if the light was green when you entered
Illegal only where a sign says so
Always illegal, whether the intersection is marked or not

questions.correctOption: Always illegal, whether the intersection is marked or not
questions.explanation: If your exit is not clear, stay out of the box. A green light is permission to proceed, not permission to trap yourself.

citations.quote: It is always illegal to block an intersection, whether it is marked or not.

questions.stem: You must yield to a pedestrian who is:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk only
In a marked or unmarked crosswalk, or on your half of the road, or approaching closely enough to be in danger
Only at signalized intersections

questions.correctOption: In a marked or unmarked crosswalk, or on your half of the road, or approaching closely enough to be in danger
questions.explanation: There is a crosswalk at every intersection whether or not it is painted, and the duty extends to pedestrians close enough to be at risk.

citations.quote: When pedestrians are in a crosswalk (marked or unmarked) or when the pedestrian is upon the half of the roadway upon which your vehicle is traveling or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the roadway as to be in danger

questions.stem: In a marked school zone with the warning flasher operating, a driver approaching a pedestrian in a crosswalk must:

options.text: Sound the horn to warn the child
Slow to 15 m.p.h. and continue
Stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway the vehicle is on

questions.correctOption: Stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway the vehicle is on
questions.explanation: In a flashing school zone the duty rises from yield to stop, and you stay stopped until they are clear of your side of the road.

citations.quote: the driver of a vehicle shall stop to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing the roadway within a marked or unmarked crosswalk. The driver shall remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway on which the vehicle is stopped.

questions.stem: When your vehicle crosses a sidewalk to enter or leave a driveway or parking lot, you must:

options.text: Take the right-of-way, since you are leaving private property
Yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk
Sound your horn and proceed

questions.correctOption: Yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk
questions.explanation: The sidewalk belongs to people on foot. Driving on one at all is illegal except to cross it.

citations.quote: When your vehicle crosses a sidewalk while entering or exiting a driveway, alley or parking lot. It is illegal to drive on a sidewalk except to cross it

questions.stem: When approaching a pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog you must stop:

options.text: Directly beside them and offer help
Only if they step into the roadway
At least 10 feet away and without sounding your horn

questions.correctOption: At least 10 feet away and without sounding your horn
questions.explanation: Ten feet of space and silence. A horn is disorienting to someone navigating by sound.

citations.quote: Stop at least 10 feet away until the person is off the roadway. Do not use your horn, as it could startle the blind pedestrian

questions.stem: When you pull out from a parked position you must:

options.text: Take the right-of-way from traffic behind you
Wait for all moving traffic to pass
Proceed as soon as you signal

questions.correctOption: Wait for all moving traffic to pass
questions.explanation: Traffic already moving has the road. Signal, look and wait for a real gap.

citations.quote: When starting from a parked position, wait for all moving traffic to pass.

questions.stem: When you are turning left at an intersection, you must yield to:

options.text: Only oncoming traffic that is signaling
Nobody, if you arrived at the intersection first
Oncoming traffic going straight ahead or turning right

questions.correctOption: Oncoming traffic going straight ahead or turning right
questions.explanation: A left turn crosses the path of everyone coming the other way, so the turn waits.

citations.quote: When turning left, you must wait for oncoming traffic going straight ahead or turning right.

questions.stem: Entering a main road from a driveway, alley or parking lot, you must yield to:

options.text: All vehicles already on the main road
Only vehicles approaching from the left
Nobody, once you have signaled

questions.correctOption: All vehicles already on the main road
questions.explanation: You are joining their road. Everything already on it goes first.

citations.quote: When entering a main road from a driveway, alley, parking lot or roadside, you must yield to all vehicles already on the main road.

questions.stem: When entering a roundabout you must yield to:

options.text: Traffic waiting to enter behind you
Nobody — roundabout entries are uncontrolled
Traffic already circulating in the roundabout

questions.correctOption: Traffic already circulating in the roundabout
questions.explanation: Circulating traffic has the right-of-way; you enter on a gap and then keep moving.

citations.quote: When entering a roundabout, traffic circle or rotary (also known as "town squares"), you must yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.stem: Approaching a fire station, you should yield to an emergency vehicle that is:

options.text: Parked inside the bay
Being washed in the driveway
About to back into, or already backing into, the station driveway

questions.correctOption: About to back into, or already backing into, the station driveway
questions.explanation: A backing fire truck has almost no view behind it, and it needs the road to finish the manoeuvre.

citations.quote: When approaching a fire station, you should yield to any emergency vehicle that is about to back into, or is already in the process of backing into, the driveway entrance to the station.

questions.stem: At an ALL-WAY stop where two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time:

options.text: The larger vehicle goes first
The vehicle on the right goes first
The vehicle on the left goes first

questions.correctOption: The vehicle on the right goes first
questions.explanation: First to arrive goes first; on a tie, yield to the driver on your right.

citations.quote: At intersections marked as ALL-WAY stops, the vehicle reaching the intersection first gets to go first (of course, ALL vehicles must stop). If more than one vehicle arrives at the same time, yield the right of way to the vehicle on the right

questions.stem: Where two roads cross and there are no stop signs or signals at all, you must yield to:

options.text: Any vehicle arriving at the same time on your left
Nobody — the faster vehicle has priority
Any vehicle arriving at the same time on your right

questions.correctOption: Any vehicle arriving at the same time on your right
questions.explanation: The same tie-breaker applies at uncontrolled crossings: the driver on the right wins.

citations.quote: Where roads cross and there are no stop signs or signals, yield to any vehicle coming at the same time on your right

questions.stem: At a "T" intersection, the vehicles on the road that ends must:

options.text: Yield only to traffic from the left
Yield to traffic from both directions on the through road
Go first, since they cannot continue straight

questions.correctOption: Yield to traffic from both directions on the through road
questions.explanation: Your road is ending, so everything on the through road has priority in both directions.

citations.quote: At "T" intersections where one road dead-ends into another main crossing roadway, the vehicles on the road ending must yield to oncoming traffic from both directions on the main road

questions.stem: You have a green light but a vehicle is still in the intersection. You must:

options.text: Sound your horn and go around it
Yield to it, even if you have the green light
Proceed, because your light is green

questions.correctOption: Yield to it, even if you have the green light
questions.explanation: Green means go if it is clear. Vehicles and pedestrians still in the box at the change keep the right-of-way.

citations.quote: To any vehicles already in the intersection, even if you have the green traffic light; (The red vehicle in the diagram at right must yield to the green vehicle.)

questions.stem: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren, air horn or red or blue flashing light, all traffic meeting or being overtaken must:

options.text: Drive to a position as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb and stop
Speed up to clear the area
Stop where they are, in the travel lane

questions.correctOption: Drive to a position as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb and stop
questions.explanation: Pull right and stop, and stay stopped until it has passed or an officer waves you on.

citations.quote: all traffic meeting or being overtaken must yield the right-of-way and immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as close as possible to the right hand edge or curb of the roadway stop. You must remain in that stopped position until the emergency vehicle has passed or until you are directed to move by a police officer.

questions.stem: You are stopped at a red light when an emergency vehicle approaches from behind and the light turns green. You should:

options.text: Stay where you are until the emergency vehicle has passed
Reverse out of the intersection
Proceed immediately on the green

questions.correctOption: Stay where you are until the emergency vehicle has passed
questions.explanation: Moving on the green would pull you straight into its path. Hold position and let it clear.

citations.quote: If the traffic light is red, stay where you are. If the light turns green before the emergency vehicle has passed, do NOT proceed on green.

questions.stem: Following a fire truck that is responding to an alarm is:

options.text: Permitted if you keep your headlights on
Against the law
Permitted at a two-second interval

questions.correctOption: Against the law
questions.explanation: It is illegal to follow a responding emergency vehicle, and illegal to bring your vehicle within the block where it has stopped.

citations.quote: It is against the law to follow a fire truck or other emergency vehicle responding to a fire alarm or other emergency. It is also illegal to take your vehicle within the block of where the emergency vehicle has stopped

questions.stem: An unprotected fire department hose lies across the road. You should:

options.text: Not drive over it unless the fire official in command says it is okay
Drive over it only if it appears empty
Drive over it slowly

questions.correctOption: Not drive over it unless the fire official in command says it is okay
questions.explanation: A charged hose is a lifeline for the crew inside the building, and driving over it can burst it.

citations.quote: do not drive over any unprotected fire department hose unless the fire department official in command says it is okay.

questions.stem: A transit bus has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway from a bus stop. You must:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to it
Maintain speed and pass on the left
Sound your horn to claim the lane

questions.correctOption: Yield the right-of-way to it
questions.explanation: Transit buses get the merge. That is different from a school bus, which you must stop for.

citations.quote: You must yield the right-of-way to any transit vehicle (metro bus) that has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway from a bus stop.

questions.stem: At a railroad crossing, drivers must yield to trains:

options.text: Only when signals are flashing
Only when the train sounds its horn
Always — it is the law

questions.correctOption: Always — it is the law
questions.explanation: A train needs a mile or more to stop and cannot swerve. The duty to yield is unconditional.

citations.quote: Drivers must ALWAYS yield the right of way to trains because IT'S THE LAW.

questions.stem: The manual states that a crosswalk exists:

options.text: Only where lines are painted
At every intersection, even if it is not marked
Only in school zones

questions.correctOption: At every intersection, even if it is not marked
questions.explanation: Unmarked crosswalks carry the same duty as painted ones. Look for the person, not the paint.

citations.quote: Generally, pedestrians have the right-of-way at all intersections. There is a crosswalk at every intersection, even if painted lines and boundaries do not mark the crossing.

questions.stem: Regardless of who has the right-of-way, the law requires a driver to:

options.text: Yield only to pedestrians in marked crosswalks
Exercise great care and extreme caution to avoid striking pedestrians
Sound the horn before every intersection

questions.correctOption: Exercise great care and extreme caution to avoid striking pedestrians
questions.explanation: The duty of care survives the right-of-way rules entirely. Being in the right is no defense for hitting someone.

citations.quote: Regardless of the rules of the road or right-of-way, the law specifically requires YOU, as a driver, to exercise great care and extreme caution to avoid striking pedestrians.

questions.stem: The first rule of turning is to turn from:

options.text: The center lane into the far lane
The closest lane in your direction into the closest legal lane in the new direction
Any lane, as long as you signal

questions.correctOption: The closest lane in your direction into the closest legal lane in the new direction
questions.explanation: Closest lane to closest lane keeps your path predictable and stops you sweeping across someone else's lane.

citations.quote: The first rule of turning is to turn from the closest lane in the direction you are traveling to the closest legal lane in the direction you want to go.

questions.stem: You must switch on your turn signal at least how far before the turn?
