options.text: 200 feet
50 feet
10 feet

questions.correctOption: 50 feet
questions.explanation: Fifty feet, for a turn or a lane change — enough warning for the drivers around you to react.

citations.quote: At least 50 feet before the turn, you must turn on your turn signal lights.

questions.stem: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, you should:

options.text: Not signal until you are in the intersection
Use your hazard lights instead
Signal well before the intersection

questions.correctOption: Not signal until you are in the intersection
questions.explanation: Signaling early tells drivers you are turning at the intersection, and someone waiting to pull out may move into your path.

citations.quote: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not signal until you are in the intersection.

questions.stem: Which of these is a misuse of your turn signals?

options.text: Signaling 50 feet before a lane change
Signaling before turning into a driveway
Signaling a driver behind you to come around and pass

questions.correctOption: Signaling a driver behind you to come around and pass
questions.explanation: Waving someone into a pass takes on responsibility for a gap you cannot properly see. Signals state your own intentions, nothing else.

citations.quote: To signal a driver behind you to come around to pass your vehicle. • To relay the turn intentions of vehicles ahead of you to those drivers behind your vehicle.

questions.stem: When you use hand and arm signals, you should:

options.text: Keep the arm out through the whole turn
Bring your arm in during the actual turn to keep control of the wheel
Signal only for left turns

questions.correctOption: Bring your arm in during the actual turn to keep control of the wheel
questions.explanation: Signal, then get both hands back on the wheel before the steering starts.

citations.quote: When you use hand signals, bring your arm in during the actual turn to keep control of the steering wheel.

questions.stem: While waiting to turn left across oncoming traffic, your front wheels should be:

options.text: Turned in the direction of the turn, ready to go
Kept straight until you begin the turn
Turned toward the curb

questions.correctOption: Kept straight until you begin the turn
questions.explanation: If someone hits you from behind with the wheels turned, the impact launches you into oncoming traffic.

citations.quote: Don't turn your wheels in the direction of the turn while waiting for oncoming traffic to pass. If you are hit from the rear while your wheels are turned, the impact can push you into oncoming traffic.
Keep your vehicles wheels straight until you begin the turn.

questions.stem: Turning left from a two-way street onto another two-way street, you should approach:

options.text: Straddling the center line
With the left side of your vehicle as close to the center line as possible
From the right-hand lane

questions.correctOption: With the left side of your vehicle as close to the center line as possible
questions.explanation: Approach near the center, then finish in the first lane past the center line — never wide into the right lane.

citations.quote: approach the turn with the left side of the vehicle as close to the center line as possible.

questions.stem: If an intersection has a lane marked for left turns, you:

options.text: Must turn from the lane to its right
May turn left from any lane if traffic is light
Must not make the turn from any other lane

questions.correctOption: Must not make the turn from any other lane
questions.explanation: A marked turn lane is mandatory, not a suggestion.

citations.quote: If the intersection has a lane signed or marked for making left turns, do not make this turn from any other lane.

questions.stem: Turning left onto a one-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn wide into whichever lane is empty
Turn into the lane nearest the right curb
Turn sharply into the first lane closest to the left curb

questions.correctOption: Turn sharply into the first lane closest to the left curb
questions.explanation: One-way streets take a sharp turn into the leftmost lane, not a lazy sweep across the street.

citations.quote: You should turn into the first lane closest to the left curb.

questions.stem: A left turn on a red light is permitted in Tennessee, after a complete stop, when you are turning:

options.text: From a two-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way street onto a two-way street
From a one-way street onto a one-way street

questions.correctOption: From a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: One-way to one-way only, at intersections not signed against turns on red — and only after a full stop.

citations.quote: you may make a left turn on red when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. You must come to a complete stop at the light prior to making the turn, the same as right turns on red.

questions.stem: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street at a red light:

options.text: Is permitted between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m.
Is permitted after a complete stop
Is not permitted

questions.correctOption: Is not permitted
questions.explanation: That turn would cross oncoming traffic that has a green, so the red light means wait.

citations.quote: You CANNOT make this left turn on a red light.

questions.stem: Before making a right turn you should position your vehicle:

options.text: Just left of the center line
As close as is practical to the right curb or road edge
In the center of the roadway

questions.correctOption: As close as is practical to the right curb or road edge
questions.explanation: Hugging the curb closes the gap a cyclist or another driver could try to squeeze into — without crowding pedestrians or parked cars.

citations.quote: Get as close as is practical to the right curb or road edge without interfering with pedestrians, bicyclists or parked vehicles.

questions.stem: A vehicle in the second lane may make the same turn as a vehicle in the first lane:

options.text: Whenever traffic allows
Only when a lane use control sign or marking permits it
Never

questions.correctOption: Only when a lane use control sign or marking permits it
questions.explanation: Dual turn lanes exist, but only where the signs and pavement markings say so.

citations.quote: A vehicle in the second lane can make the same turn as a vehicle in the first lane only when a lane use control sign or marking permits it.

questions.stem: Travel through a roundabout always goes:

options.text: To the right, counter-clockwise
To the left, clockwise
In whichever direction traffic is lighter

questions.correctOption: To the right, counter-clockwise
questions.explanation: Keep right and circulate counter-clockwise, staying right of the splitter island as you enter.

citations.quote: Always travel around a roundabout to the right, in a counter-clockwise direction.

questions.stem: Once you are inside a roundabout you should:

options.text: Not stop unless directed by signs, signals or a traffic officer
Stop at each exit
Stop to let entering vehicles in

questions.correctOption: Not stop unless directed by signs, signals or a traffic officer
questions.explanation: Stopping inside the circle backs traffic up all the way around it. Yield on entry, then keep moving.

citations.quote: Enter the roundabout when there is a gap in traffic and once inside do not stop unless directed to do so by signs, signals or a traffic officer.

questions.stem: The speed posted inside a roundabout is usually:

options.text: 35 to 45 m.p.h.
The same as the approach road
15 to 25 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: 15 to 25 m.p.h.
questions.explanation: Roundabouts work because everyone is going slowly enough to merge and to see pedestrians at the crossings.

citations.quote: Within the roundabout, proceed at a slower speed (usually posted at 15 to 25 m.p.h.).

questions.stem: In a multi-lane roundabout you should:

options.text: Change lanes freely to reach your exit
Pass slower vehicles on the inside
Not overtake or pass any vehicles

questions.correctOption: Not overtake or pass any vehicles
questions.explanation: Vehicles cross lanes to reach exits, so passing inside a roundabout puts you exactly where someone is about to be.

citations.quote: In a multi-lane roundabout, do not overtake or pass any vehicles.

questions.stem: When leaving a roundabout you should:

options.text: Not signal at all
Signal your exit with your right turn signal and watch for pedestrians
Signal left

questions.correctOption: Signal your exit with your right turn signal and watch for pedestrians
questions.explanation: The right signal tells the driver waiting to enter that the gap is theirs — and the crosswalk on the exit leg needs your attention.

citations.quote: Always indicate your exit using your right turn signal. Watch for pedestrians in or approaching the crosswalk on the street you are exiting and yield the right-of-way if necessary.

questions.stem: A U-turn is prohibited at any location where you cannot see traffic coming from both directions for at least:

options.text: 500 feet in each direction
100 feet in each direction
1,000 feet in each direction

questions.correctOption: 500 feet in each direction
questions.explanation: A U-turn takes time and blocks the whole road while it happens, so you need a long clear view both ways.

citations.quote: At any rural or urban location where you cannot see traffic coming from both directions for at least 500 feet in each direction.

questions.stem: Large trucks and buses turning right often leave an open space on their right. You should:

options.text: Stay out of it, because they must make wide turns
Sound your horn and pass on the left
Use the space to pass them

questions.correctOption: Stay out of it, because they must make wide turns
questions.explanation: That gap is the truck's turning room, not a lane. Moving into it puts you where the trailer is about to sweep.

citations.quote: Large trucks and buses MUST make wide turns. Sometimes they must leave an open space to the right just before the turn. To avoid an accident, do not pass a truck on the right if there is a possibility that it might make a right turn.

questions.stem: On a road with no center line markings where traffic comes from both directions, drivers must:

options.text: Claim the center until someone approaches
Drive on the left to see farther ahead
Give oncoming drivers at least half the road

questions.correctOption: Give oncoming drivers at least half the road
questions.explanation: No paint does not mean no rule — half the road belongs to whoever is coming the other way.

citations.quote: drivers must give others going in the opposite direction at least half the road.

questions.stem: You may legally drive to the left of the center of the roadway when:

options.text: Only between midnight and 6 a.m.
Passing a vehicle going the same direction, passing an obstruction, on a one-way road, or turning left
Any time the road ahead is clear

questions.correctOption: Passing a vehicle going the same direction, passing an obstruction, on a one-way road, or turning left
questions.explanation: Those four situations are the whole list. Everything else belongs on the right.

citations.quote: Drive on the right of the road except when: • Passing another vehicle going in the same direction as your vehicle; • Driving to the left of center to pass an obstruction in the road

questions.stem: The center lane of a two-way, three-lane or five-lane highway is used only for:

options.text: Turning left
Passing
Emergency parking

questions.correctOption: Turning left
questions.explanation: It is a shared turn lane. Traffic from both directions uses it to wait for a left turn, so nobody can travel in it.

citations.quote: The center lane of a two-way, three-lane or five-lane highway is used only for turning left.

questions.stem: A shared center turn lane may be used for travel of no more than:

options.text: One mile
Half a block
300 feet

questions.correctOption: 300 feet
questions.explanation: You may enter it to set up a left turn, not to drive down it — 300 feet is the limit, and passing in it is never allowed.

citations.quote: These lanes cannot be used for passing and cannot be used for travel farther than 300 feet.

questions.stem: When two vehicles enter a shared center turn lane from opposite directions:

options.text: Both must reverse out
The first vehicle to enter the lane has the right-of-way
The larger vehicle has the right-of-way

questions.correctOption: The first vehicle to enter the lane has the right-of-way
questions.explanation: First in, first served. The second driver waits for the lane to clear.

citations.quote: When vehicles enter the turn lane from opposite directions, the first vehicle to enter the lane has the right-of-way.

questions.stem: Using the center turn lane to reach a left turn lane at an intersection is:

options.text: Encouraged, because it keeps you out of through traffic
Not permitted
Permitted below 25 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: Not permitted
questions.explanation: Running the center lane up to an intersection turns it into a travel lane, and drivers pulling out of side streets do not expect traffic there.

citations.quote: Do NOT travel in the center turn lane to access a left turn lane at an intersection.

questions.stem: On a divided highway you may cross the median strip or barrier:

options.text: Only at an authorized crossover or intersection, or when officially directed
Only at night
Any time no traffic is in sight

questions.correctOption: Only at an authorized crossover or intersection, or when officially directed
questions.explanation: The median is not a road. Crossings happen at built openings or at an officer's direction.

citations.quote: Do not drive within, across or over any median strip or barrier separating these roadways. It is only allowed at an authorized crossover or intersection, or when you are officially directed to do so.

questions.stem: Crossovers for traffic on the interstate:

options.text: Are provided only near cities
Are provided every few miles
Are not provided at all — paved crossovers exist only on four-lane highways

questions.correctOption: Are not provided at all — paved crossovers exist only on four-lane highways
questions.explanation: Any gap you see in an interstate median is an emergency crossover for official use, not a place to turn around.

citations.quote: such a crossover is PERMITTED ONLY at paved openings provided on four-lane highways. There are NO crossovers provided for traffic on interstates.

questions.stem: You should not travel in a reserved lane unless:

options.text: You are operating the type of vehicle indicated, or must turn across it within the next half block
Your own lane is congested
You are running late

questions.correctOption: You are operating the type of vehicle indicated, or must turn across it within the next half block
questions.explanation: Reserved lanes belong to the vehicles named on the sign. Crossing one to make an imminent turn is the only other use.

citations.quote: Do NOT travel in one of these lanes unless operating the type of vehicle indicated, or unless you must turn across the reserved lane in the next half block distance.

questions.stem: During high inbound and outbound traffic hours, an HOV lane is reserved for vehicles carrying:

options.text: Three or more adults only
Any vehicle with its headlights on
Two or more persons, including a baby in a car seat

questions.correctOption: Two or more persons, including a baby in a car seat
questions.explanation: Buses with two or more occupants, motorcycles, and emergency vehicles also qualify. A baby in a car seat counts as a passenger.

citations.quote: During high inbound traffic hours (7–9 a.m.) and high outbound traffic (4–6 p.m.), the HOV lane is reserved for the exclusive use of: • Vehicles with two or more persons. (A baby in a car seat qualifies just like any other passenger.) • Buses with 2 or more occupants • Motorcycles occupied by 1 person • Emergency Vehicles

questions.stem: A driver found in violation of the HOV lane restriction is subject to:

options.text: A $50 fine and court costs
A 30-day suspension
No penalty, only a warning

questions.correctOption: A $50 fine and court costs
questions.explanation: Fifty dollars plus costs — the restriction is enforceable, not advisory.

citations.quote: Drivers found in violation of the HOV lane are subject to a $50 fine and court costs.

questions.stem: Which step belongs in a safe lane change?

options.text: Change lanes first and signal afterward
Look over your shoulder in the direction you will be moving
Rely on the mirrors alone

questions.correctOption: Look over your shoulder in the direction you will be moving
questions.explanation: Mirrors do not cover the blind spot. Check mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder, check again, then move gradually.

citations.quote: Check your rear view mirrors. • Signal your intention to change lanes. • Look over your shoulder in the direction you will be moving. • Look behind you to both sides again. • Check your blind spots.

questions.stem: On a two-lane road in the United States, you overtake and pass another vehicle:

options.text: On whichever side has more room
On the right if the other driver is slow
Only on the left

questions.correctOption: Only on the left
questions.explanation: Passing on the left is the rule; passing on the right is allowed only in the narrow situations the manual lists.

citations.quote: When overtaking and passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction on a two-lane road in the USA, you should pass only to the left of the vehicle.

questions.stem: After passing a vehicle you should return to the right lane:

options.text: Only after passing two more vehicles
As soon as you are safely clear of the vehicle you passed
Immediately after drawing level with it

questions.correctOption: As soon as you are safely clear of the vehicle you passed
questions.explanation: Cutting back in early clips the front of the car you just passed. Wait until you can see it in your mirror.

citations.quote: Pass on the left at a safe distance and do not return to the right lane until safely clear of the overtaken vehicle.

questions.stem: Passing more than one vehicle at a time in Tennessee is:

options.text: Not illegal, but not considered safe
Legal only on interstates
Illegal

questions.correctOption: Not illegal, but not considered safe
questions.explanation: You need to complete the whole pass and be back in the right lane before you are within 100 feet of the no-passing markings or an oncoming vehicle.

citations.quote: it is NOT SAFE to pass more than one vehicle at a time, although it is not illegal in Tennessee to pass multiple vehicles.
Can complete the pass of all vehicles and be safely returned to the right lane before coming within 100 feet of the no passing markings

questions.stem: Passing on the right by driving off the pavement of the roadway is:

options.text: Permitted when the shoulder is paved
Never permitted
Permitted below 30 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: Never permitted
questions.explanation: Never — not on the shoulder, not on the grass, not to get around a left-turning car.

citations.quote: Passing on the right is never permitted by driving off the pavement of the roadway.

questions.stem: Using a bike lane or parking lane to pass on the right is:

options.text: Allowed if you signal first
Allowed in slow traffic
Not allowed at any location

questions.correctOption: Not allowed at any location
questions.explanation: Those lanes hold exactly the road users least able to survive being hit, and the emergency lane near a signal or stop sign is off limits too.

citations.quote: Do NOT pass on the right using a bike lane or parking lane at any location, nor in the emergency lane within sight of a traffic light or stop sign.

questions.stem: You should not pass when approaching:

options.text: An intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel
A gas station
A milepost marker

questions.correctOption: An intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel
questions.explanation: All of them are places where something can appear with no room for you to get back in. Hills and curves are on the same list.

citations.quote: Do not pass when approaching any road-way intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

questions.stem: The end of a no-passing zone means:

options.text: Passing is now required
It is now safe to pass
There is increased visibility ahead

questions.correctOption: There is increased visibility ahead
questions.explanation: Better sight distance is not the same as a safe pass. You still have to judge the gap yourself.

citations.quote: The end of a "no-passing zone" does not mean it is safe to pass. It means there is increased visibility ahead.

questions.stem: When another driver is passing you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to shorten their time alongside
Move onto the shoulder
Maintain your speed and stay in your lane

questions.correctOption: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane
questions.explanation: Speeding up strands them in the oncoming lane. Hold your speed and let the pass finish.

citations.quote: Maintaining your speed. DO NOT speed up to keep the other driver from passing.

questions.stem: Passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road when oncoming vehicles are present is:

options.text: Required if the cyclist is slow
Fine if you sound your horn
Something you should never attempt

questions.correctOption: Something you should never attempt
questions.explanation: Squeezing between a cyclist and oncoming traffic leaves nowhere for anyone to go. Wait for a real gap.

citations.quote: As a driver you should never attempt passing between a bicyclist and oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road.

questions.stem: On the roadway, slower traffic must:

options.text: Use the shoulder
Drive in the right-hand lane
Drive in the center lane

questions.correctOption: Drive in the right-hand lane
questions.explanation: The left lane is for passing and turning; slower traffic belongs on the right.

citations.quote: Slower traffic must drive in the right-hand lane. The left lane is for passing and turning.

questions.stem: Reversible lanes are usually marked by:

options.text: Double-broken yellow lines
Solid white lines
Red reflectors

questions.correctOption: Double-broken yellow lines
questions.explanation: Double-broken yellow warns that the lane carries traffic one way at some hours and the other way at others — check the overhead lane signals.

citations.quote: These lanes are called "reversible lanes" and are usually marked by double-broken yellow lines.

questions.stem: You may turn left across the center line into a driveway or alley while inside a no-passing zone:

options.text: Only if a sign permits it
Yes — turning across the line is allowed there
No, never

questions.correctOption: Yes — turning across the line is allowed there
questions.explanation: A no-passing zone forbids passing, not turning. You may cross the line to enter or leave a driveway, alley, private road or intersection.

citations.quote: You are allowed to turn across the center line if you are making a left turn into or coming out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway while in the "no-passing zone".

questions.stem: Whose responsibility is it to yield when you are merging onto an interstate?

options.text: Whichever vehicle is travelling faster
The drivers already on the interstate
Yours — it is your responsibility to yield

questions.correctOption: Yours — it is your responsibility to yield
questions.explanation: Drivers on the interstate should make allowance for you, but the legal duty to yield is on the vehicle entering.

citations.quote: It is your responsibility to yield the right-of-way to other cars on the interstate.

questions.stem: A "lane added" sign at an on-ramp means:

options.text: The right lane is closing ahead
Entering traffic must merge immediately
The on-ramp becomes a new lane and entering traffic does not need to merge immediately

questions.correctOption: The on-ramp becomes a new lane and entering traffic does not need to merge immediately
questions.explanation: With a lane added, traffic already on the interstate should avoid moving right there — the entering driver is not expecting company.

citations.quote: The "lane added" sign means that there is a new right lane added to the interstate/roadway for the incoming traffic. The on-ramp becomes a new lane and the entering traffic does not need to merge immediately.

questions.stem: You are travelling in the left lane of an interstate and a faster vehicle comes up behind you. You should:

options.text: Move one lane to your right
Maintain your speed to enforce the limit
Brake to signal the driver behind

questions.correctOption: Move one lane to your right
questions.explanation: The left lane is for passing. Move over and let the faster traffic through rather than policing it.

citations.quote: If you are traveling in the left lane and someone comes up behind you at a faster speed, move one lane to your right.

questions.stem: Interstate exit signs are usually placed:

options.text: At least one mile ahead of the exit turn-off
At the exit itself
Exactly a quarter mile ahead

questions.correctOption: At least one mile ahead of the exit turn-off
questions.explanation: A mile of warning gives you time to move right in stages instead of cutting across at the last second.

citations.quote: Exit signs are usually placed at least one mile ahead of the exit turn-off.

questions.stem: The paved shoulder of an interstate may be used:

options.text: For deceleration where marked for that purpose, or in an emergency
For passing on the right
For travel when traffic is heavy

questions.correctOption: For deceleration where marked for that purpose, or in an emergency
questions.explanation: It is not a travel lane. Parking there is prohibited except for an emergency.

citations.quote: The paved shoulder of the interstate should not be used for vehicular travel except for deceleration when marked for this purpose or for an emergency.

questions.stem: Parking on the paved or unpaved portion of an interstate entrance or exit ramp is:

options.text: Legal for up to fifteen minutes
Legal if you switch on your hazard lights
Illegal unless the vehicle is disabled

questions.correctOption: Illegal unless the vehicle is disabled
questions.explanation: Attended or unattended, it is illegal. A disabled vehicle is the only exception.

citations.quote: It is illegal to park a motor vehicle, whether attended or unattended upon the paved or unpaved portions of any entrance or exit ramp of any highway unless the vehicle is disabled.

questions.stem: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you must:

options.text: Use the nearest median crossover
Back up along the shoulder
Proceed to the next exit

questions.correctOption: Proceed to the next exit
questions.explanation: Backing up, U-turns and crossing the median are all illegal on the interstate. The next exit is the only legal option.

citations.quote: It is also illegal to back up or make a U-turn on interstate highways. If you miss your exit, you must proceed to the next exit. It is illegal to cross the median on the interstate.

questions.stem: At a diamond interchange, the left turn entrance ramp is always encountered:

options.text: Only from the frontage road
Before crossing over or under the interstate
After crossing over or under the interstate

questions.correctOption: After crossing over or under the interstate
questions.explanation: Right-turn entrance first, then the crossing, then the left-turn entrance. Knowing the pattern keeps you out of a last-second lane change.

citations.quote: (1) The RIGHT TURN entrance ramp will always be encountered BEFORE crossing over or under the interstate. (2) The LEFT TURN entrance ramp will always be encountered AFTER crossing over or under the interstate.

questions.stem: At a cloverleaf interchange, to turn left you actually:

options.text: Take a right turn just after the overpass
Take a left turn before the overpass
Stop and wait for a signal

questions.correctOption: Take a right turn just after the overpass
questions.explanation: Every movement at a cloverleaf is a right turn; the loop does the turning for you.

citations.quote: At a cloverleaf interchange, all turns are right turns. To turn right, take the right turn before you get to the overpass. To turn left, take the right turn just after the overpass.

questions.stem: Your vehicle breaks down on the interstate. The manual says that, except in extreme emergencies, you should:

options.text: Stand behind the vehicle to flag traffic
Walk to the nearest exit for help
Remain in your disabled vehicle until help arrives

questions.correctOption: Remain in your disabled vehicle until help arrives
questions.explanation: Walking on the interstate is both illegal and dangerous. Stay with the car, flashers on, and wait for a trooper or a good Samaritan.

citations.quote: Walking on the interstate is both illegal and dangerous. Except for extreme emergency cases, remain in your disabled vehicle until a State Trooper, other police officer, emergency service vehicle or a good Samaritan stops to offer assistance.

questions.stem: After a crash on the interstate with no serious injuries and a still-drivable vehicle, Tennessee law allows you to:

options.text: Leave the scene once information is exchanged
Leave the vehicles exactly where they stopped in every case
Pull the vehicle to the emergency lane and wait for an officer

questions.correctOption: Pull the vehicle to the emergency lane and wait for an officer
questions.explanation: Clearing the travel lanes prevents the second crash. You still may not leave the scene.

citations.quote: If the vehicle is still drivable and there are NO SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURIES or deaths, you may pull the vehicle(s) to the emergency lane and await the arrival of a trooper or police officer to the crash scene.

questions.stem: Dialing *THP (*847) from a wireless phone connects you to:

options.text: A toll-paid roadside assistance service
The Department of Transportation billing office
The nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol dispatcher, at no charge

questions.correctOption: The nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol dispatcher, at no charge
questions.explanation: It is free and it routes to the nearest dispatch center — useful when you cannot describe where you are.

citations.quote: you may use your wireless phone at no charge to directly connect with the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol Dispatch Center. Dial: * T H P (*847)

questions.stem: Tennessee's Move Over Law now also applies to:

options.text: Any stationary motor vehicle with its emergency flasher lights on
Only police and fire vehicles
Only vehicles stopped at night

questions.correctOption: Any stationary motor vehicle with its emergency flasher lights on
questions.explanation: An ordinary car stopped on the shoulder with its hazards on gets the same protection as a patrol car.

citations.quote: this law now applies to all stationary motor vehicles, such as your car or truck, with their emergency flasher lights on.

questions.stem: The requirement to move over for a stopped emergency vehicle applies:

options.text: Only when the vehicle is on the right-hand side
Regardless of which side of the road the vehicle is on
Only during daylight

questions.correctOption: Regardless of which side of the road the vehicle is on
questions.explanation: Left shoulder or right, the duty is the same.

citations.quote: This requirement to move over applies, regardless of whether the emergency vehicle is on the right or left-hand side of the road.

questions.stem: Under the Move Over Law, a motorist may stay in the same lane and simply slow down:

options.text: Only at night
Whenever they prefer to
Only when traffic conditions make changing lanes unsafe

questions.correctOption: Only when traffic conditions make changing lanes unsafe
questions.explanation: Changing lanes is the default response. Slowing in place is the fallback when the change cannot be made safely.

citations.quote: ONLY when traffic conditions make it unsafe to make such lane change is the motorist allowed to respond to this situation by simply slowing down and remaining in the same lane.

questions.stem: Which vehicles does the manual list as covered by the Move Over Law?

options.text: Any vehicle displaying a green light
Police, ambulance and fire, utility and sanitation, tow trucks and TDOT HELP, and highway maintenance vehicles
Police vehicles only

questions.correctOption: Police, ambulance and fire, utility and sanitation, tow trucks and TDOT HELP, and highway maintenance vehicles
questions.explanation: The list is broad, and it now reaches ordinary vehicles showing hazard lights as well.

citations.quote: Police or Highway Patrol vehicles; • Ambulance or Fire Fighting vehicles; • Utility vehicles that provide your electric, phone, natural gas and water services as well as solid waste "sanitation" vehicles; • Tow Trucks or TDOT HELP vehicles; • TDOT maintenance vehicles or private contractors involved in road construction or repair work.

questions.stem: On the interstate, the manual advises scanning ahead:

options.text: Two car lengths ahead
Only as far as your headlights reach
15 to 20 seconds in front of your vehicle

questions.correctOption: 15 to 20 seconds in front of your vehicle
questions.explanation: At interstate speed you cover ground fast; looking well ahead is what turns a sudden brake light into a gentle lift off the accelerator.

citations.quote: Scan the roadway ahead and try to watch 15-20 seconds in front of your vehicle for cars braking, entering or exiting.

questions.stem: On a long interstate trip, the manual recommends taking a break:

options.text: Every six hours
Only when you feel sleepy
At least every two hours or every 100 miles

questions.correctOption: At least every two hours or every 100 miles
questions.explanation: And no more than eight hours of driving in a day. Fatigue builds long before you notice it.

citations.quote: Take a break and get out of the car at least every two hours, or every 100 miles or so.

questions.stem: Backing a vehicle into a travel lane is:

options.text: Allowed on residential streets
Never allowed, except when backing into a parallel parking space
Allowed if you use your hazard lights

questions.correctOption: Never allowed, except when backing into a parallel parking space
questions.explanation: Parallel parking is the single exception, and even then you back from a stopped position beside the space.

citations.quote: Never back a vehicle into any travel lane with the exception of backing into a parallel parking space.

questions.stem: Backing into an intersection from a driveway is:

options.text: Illegal
Legal if no traffic is in sight
Legal below 5 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: Illegal
questions.explanation: You cannot see cross traffic, and cross traffic cannot see a reversing car. It is prohibited outright.

citations.quote: It is illegal to back into an intersection from a driveway.

questions.stem: Backing up on the interstate is:

options.text: Legal on the shoulder only
Legal if you missed your exit
Illegal

questions.correctOption: Illegal
questions.explanation: It is flatly illegal, along with U-turns and crossing the median.

citations.quote: It is illegal to back up on the interstate.

questions.stem: When you stop at a curb, your vehicle should be within:

options.text: 18 inches of the curb
3 feet of the curb
6 inches of the curb

questions.correctOption: 18 inches of the curb
questions.explanation: Eighteen inches, both when you stop at a curb and when you finish a parallel park.

citations.quote: If stopping at a curb, move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.

questions.stem: Parking beside a roadway outside city limits requires that you leave at least:

options.text: 10 feet of road width
One full lane on each side
18 feet of road width for other traffic

questions.correctOption: 18 feet of road width for other traffic
questions.explanation: Eighteen feet of clear roadway, all four wheels off the pavement if possible, and your vehicle visible for 200 feet in either direction.

citations.quote: you must ensure that you leave at least 18 feet of road width for other traffic to pass your parked vehicle. Plus, your vehicle must be visible for at least 200 feet in either direction

questions.stem: Leaving the engine running in a parked, unattended vehicle is:

options.text: Allowed in cold weather
Against the law
Allowed for up to ten minutes

questions.correctOption: Against the law
questions.explanation: It is illegal, and the manual pairs it with removing the ignition keys.

citations.quote: It is against the law to leave the engine running in a parked unattended vehicle.

questions.stem: When pulling out of any type of parking space, including a parallel space, a driver must:

options.text: Look, signal and yield the right-of-way
Sound the horn and proceed
Reverse into the nearest gap

questions.correctOption: Look, signal and yield the right-of-way
questions.explanation: Traffic already moving keeps the right-of-way, so the parked car waits.

citations.quote: A driver must look, signal and yield the right-of-way when coming out of any type of parking space, including parallel spaces.

questions.stem: Parking on a downhill with a curb, you should turn the front wheels:

options.text: Straight ahead
Toward the curb, and set the parking brake
Away from the curb

questions.correctOption: Toward the curb, and set the parking brake
questions.explanation: If the brakes let go, the front wheel catches the curb instead of the car rolling into traffic.

citations.quote: On a downhill with a curb: Turn the front wheels toward the curb (right) and set the parking brake.

questions.stem: Parking on an uphill with a curb, you should turn the front wheels:

options.text: Away from the curb (to the left)
Toward the curb (to the right)
Straight ahead

questions.correctOption: Away from the curb (to the left)
questions.explanation: Rolling backward, the car settles back against the curb.

citations.quote: On an uphill with a curb: Turn the front wheels away from curb (left).

questions.stem: Parking on a hill where there is no curb, you should turn the front wheels:

options.text: Straight ahead
Toward the edge of the roadway
Toward the center of the road

questions.correctOption: Toward the edge of the roadway
questions.explanation: With no curb to catch the wheel, you point the car off the road rather than into it — uphill or down.

citations.quote: On a downhill without a curb: Turn the front wheels toward the edge of the roadway (right).
On an uphill without a curb: Turn the front wheels toward the edge of the roadway (right).

questions.stem: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or other traffic control device?

options.text: 10 feet
75 feet
30 feet

questions.correctOption: 30 feet
questions.explanation: Thirty feet, so the device stays visible to approaching drivers.

citations.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant • Within a fire lane • Within 20 feet of a crosswalk or in the crosswalk marked area • Within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street or on the other side of the street within 75 feet of the fire station driveway • Within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or any other traffic control device • Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing

questions.stem: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a crosswalk?

options.text: 20 feet
5 feet
50 feet

questions.correctOption: 20 feet
questions.explanation: Twenty feet of clearance keeps the crossing visible — a car parked on top of it hides the person stepping out.

citations.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant • Within a fire lane • Within 20 feet of a crosswalk or in the crosswalk marked area • Within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street or on the other side of the street within 75 feet of the fire station driveway • Within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or any other traffic control device • Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing

questions.stem: Starting a parallel park, your vehicle should be:

options.text: Rear bumper even with the other car's bumper, no closer than two feet
Touching the other car's bumper
Six feet out from the other car

questions.correctOption: Rear bumper even with the other car's bumper, no closer than two feet
questions.explanation: Line up the bumpers, leave two feet of side clearance, then back slowly with the wheel turned sharply right.

citations.quote: Your rear bumper should be even with the bumper of the other parked car. Your vehicle should not be any closer than two feet from the other vehicle.

questions.stem: During a parallel park you back slowly, turning the wheel sharply right until the car reaches an angle of about:

options.text: 15 degrees to the street
45 degrees to the street
90 degrees to the street

questions.correctOption: 45 degrees to the street
questions.explanation: Forty-five degrees is the pivot point; from there you straighten and bring the front in.

citations.quote: turning the steering wheel sharply to the right until the car is at about a 45-degree angle with the street.

questions.stem: Improperly parking in a space marked with the handicap symbol is:

options.text: A warning-only offense
Permitted for under five minutes
A misdemeanor punishable by a $100 fine, and the vehicle may be towed

questions.correctOption: A misdemeanor punishable by a $100 fine, and the vehicle may be towed
questions.explanation: The space may only be used by a vehicle displaying a valid placard or plate, and only when transporting the person it was issued to.

citations.quote: you will be committing a misdemeanor punishable by a $100 dollar fine, and your vehicle could be subject to being towed.

questions.stem: If you must leave your vehicle on a highway and cannot move it off the road, you should:

options.text: Raise the hood or tie a cloth to the left door handle or antenna
Leave the headlights on high beam
Leave the driver's door open as a warning

questions.correctOption: Raise the hood or tie a cloth to the left door handle or antenna
questions.explanation: A raised hood is a recognized breakdown signal. Add the four-way flashers and set the parking brake.

citations.quote: If you cannot move the vehicle off the highway, raise the hood or tie a handkerchief on the left door handle or antenna to warn other motorists of your stopped vehicle.

questions.stem: Double parking is:

options.text: Allowed if the hazard lights are on
Prohibited by law
Allowed while making a delivery

questions.correctOption: Prohibited by law
questions.explanation: It forces everyone else into the oncoming lane. The law prohibits it outright.

citations.quote: Double parking is prohibited by law.

questions.stem: Whenever you park, the manual says you should:

options.text: Set the parking brake, and leave the vehicle in gear or in park
Leave the transmission in neutral
Leave the engine running to keep the battery charged

questions.correctOption: Set the parking brake, and leave the vehicle in gear or in park
questions.explanation: Parking brake every time, plus gear or park — two independent things holding the car.

citations.quote: Always set the parking brake when you park. Leave the vehicle in gear if it has a manual transmission, or in park if it has an automatic transmission.

questions.stem: Stopping in a travel lane because you are lost or letting out a passenger is:

options.text: Permitted briefly with hazard lights
Permitted on residential streets
Not permitted — keep moving until you can pull off the roadway

questions.correctOption: Not permitted — keep moving until you can pull off the roadway
questions.explanation: A stopped car in a travel lane is what following drivers least expect. Keep going until you can get off the road.

citations.quote: Do not stop in the travel lanes for any reason (lost or confused about directions, vehicle breakdown, or letting out a passenger). Keep moving until you can safely pull your vehicle off the roadway.

questions.stem: Tennessee Code defines "stop" as:

options.text: Complete cessation of movement
Slowing to under 5 m.p.h.
Any pause of two seconds or more

questions.correctOption: Complete cessation of movement
questions.explanation: Rolling through is not stopping. It is grounds for a ticket and for failing the road test.

citations.quote: Tennessee Code defines "stop" as "complete cessation of movement."

questions.stem: At a stop sign with no crosswalk and no stop line, you must stop:

options.text: At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic, and again before entering the intersection
Anywhere within 50 feet of the sign
Only if another vehicle is visible

questions.correctOption: At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic, and again before entering the intersection
questions.explanation: The law names the sequence: stop where you can see, then stop before entering the intersection itself.

citations.quote: Tennessee law states: Every driver approaching a stop sign shall stop before entering the nearest side of a crosswalk, or stop at a clearly marked stop line. If neither is present, then (1) stop at a point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting roadway, and (2) stop before entering the actual intersection.

questions.stem: If no pavement markings are present at a stop sign, you should stop when:

options.text: Your rear bumper passes the sign
You are one car length past the sign
The front of your vehicle is even with the sign's placement at the roadside

questions.correctOption: The front of your vehicle is even with the sign's placement at the roadside
questions.explanation: The sign marks the stopping point when nothing is painted on the road.

citations.quote: If no pavement markings are present, stop when the front of your vehicle is even with the stop sign's placement on the roadside.

questions.stem: A flashing red traffic light requires:

options.text: Slowing and proceeding with caution
No action if the way is clear
A complete stop, just as at a stop sign

questions.correctOption: A complete stop, just as at a stop sign
questions.explanation: Flashing red is a stop sign in light form. Flashing yellow is the one that means slow down and proceed with care.

citations.quote: A complete stop is required at a flashing red traffic light, just as with a stop sign.

questions.stem: When a flag person at a construction site directs you to stop, you must:

options.text: Continue if the road looks clear
Stop completely
Slow to 10 m.p.h. and continue

questions.correctOption: Stop completely
questions.explanation: A flagger's directions carry the force of a traffic control device, and so do a police officer's.

citations.quote: You must stop completely when directed to stop by a flag person at a road construction site or by a police officer directing you to stop in any situation.

questions.stem: When a train is coming, you must stop within what distance of the nearest rail?

options.text: At least 100 feet
Between 15 and 50 feet
Between 5 and 10 feet

questions.correctOption: Between 15 and 50 feet
questions.explanation: No closer than 15 feet, no farther than 50 — and never on the tracks themselves.

citations.quote: you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the railroad tracks. Never stop on the railroad crossing tracks.

questions.stem: At a railroad crossing equipped with electric or mechanical signal devices, a driver must stop:

options.text: Within 50 feet but no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail
At least 100 feet back
Only when the gate is down

questions.correctOption: Within 50 feet but no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail
questions.explanation: Same window as any other crossing, and you do not move until it is safe.

citations.quote: Railroad crossings equipped with electric or mechanical signal devices require the operator to bring the vehicle to a complete stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and shall not proceed until it is safe.

questions.stem: Which of these must stop at every railroad grade crossing, whether or not signals are activated?

options.text: All passenger cars
Only vehicles pulling trailers
Church or school buses, common carriers, and vehicles carrying flammables or explosives

questions.correctOption: Church or school buses, common carriers, and vehicles carrying flammables or explosives
questions.explanation: Buses, taxis and hazardous-cargo vehicles stop every time. Never try to pass one of them stopped at a crossing on a two-way road.

citations.quote: Church or school buses, regardless of whether such buses are carrying any passengers at the time of crossing; • Common carriers, such as taxis or other vehicles transporting passengers for hire; • Vehicles transporting flammables, explosives or other dangerous articles as cargo or part of a cargo.

questions.stem: Driving around a crossing gate that has come down is:

options.text: Against the law
Allowed if no train is visible
Allowed if the lights have stopped flashing

questions.correctOption: Against the law
questions.explanation: Stop and stay put. You do not move until the gates are fully raised and the lights have stopped.

citations.quote: Never drive around a crossing gate that has extended down. If the gates are down, stop and stay in place. It's against the law to drive through lowered gates.

questions.stem: You are meeting a school bus with its red stop warning lights flashing and its stop arm out. You must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves
Slow to 15 m.p.h. and pass carefully
Stop only if children are visible

questions.correctOption: Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves
questions.explanation: Complete stop, in both directions, until the arm folds and the bus starts moving again.

citations.quote: Any driver meeting a school bus or church bus on which the red stop warning signal lights are flashing should reduce his speed and bring the vehicle to a complete stop while the bus stop signal arm is extended. The vehicle must remain stopped until the stop arm is pulled back and the bus resumes motion.

questions.stem: Passing a school bus on its right side while it is stopped is:

options.text: Allowed on a four-lane road
Illegal, because that is where children get on and off
Allowed if you move slowly

questions.correctOption: Illegal, because that is where children get on and off
questions.explanation: The right side is the door side. Passing there is illegal and is how children get killed.

citations.quote: Never pass on the right side of the bus, as this is where the children enter or exit. This is illegal and can have tragic results.

questions.stem: A school bus is stopped at an intersection to load or unload children. Drivers from which directions must stop?

options.text: Only the oncoming direction
All directions
Only the direction behind the bus

questions.correctOption: All directions
questions.explanation: Children may cross from any approach at an intersection, so every direction stops until the bus moves.

citations.quote: When a school bus is stopped at an intersection to load and unload children, drivers from ALL directions are required to stop until the bus resumes motion

questions.stem: Failing to stop for a stopped school bus in Tennessee is:

options.text: A non-moving violation
An infraction with no points
A Class A misdemeanor carrying a fine between $250 and $1,000

questions.correctOption: A Class A misdemeanor carrying a fine between $250 and $1,000
questions.explanation: It also carries eight points — the same as failing to stop at a railroad crossing.

citations.quote: It is a Class A misdemeanor and the driver can be fined between $250 and $1,000 for not stopping for a stopped school bus.

questions.stem: You need not stop for a school bus loading children on the opposite roadway when the road:

options.text: Has a posted limit above 45 m.p.h.
Has separate roadways divided by a median or barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic
Has four or more lanes

questions.correctOption: Has separate roadways divided by a median or barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic
questions.explanation: A real median or barrier separates you from the bus. Even then, proceed with caution.

citations.quote: When driving on a highway with separate roadways for traffic in opposite directions, divided by median space or a barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic, the driver need not stop, but should proceed with caution.

questions.stem: On a four-lane road with a center turn lane, drivers meeting a stopped school bus:

options.text: Need not stop in either direction
Must stop only in the bus's direction
Must stop in both directions, because a turn lane is not a barrier

questions.correctOption: Must stop in both directions, because a turn lane is not a barrier
questions.explanation: A fifth lane suitable for traffic is not a divider — it is just more road for a child to cross.

citations.quote: A turn lane in the middle of a four-lane highway is NOT considered a barrier, but a fifth lane that is suitable for vehicular traffic. Drivers meeting a stopped school bus on this type of road would be required to stop in both directions.

questions.stem: Flashing yellow lights on the front and back of a school bus mean:

options.text: The bus has broken down
The bus is about to turn
The bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children

questions.correctOption: The bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children
questions.explanation: Yellow is the warning to slow down and get ready to stop. Red with the arm out means stop now.

citations.quote: When the yellow lights on the front and back of the bus are flashing the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children. Motorists should slow down and prepare to stop their vehicles.

questions.stem: When a police officer signals you to pull over, you should:

options.text: Drive as close as is safely practical to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop
Stop immediately in the travel lane
Continue to the next parking lot regardless of distance

questions.correctOption: Drive as close as is safely practical to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop
questions.explanation: Get out of the traffic lanes, keep your hands on the wheel and stay in the vehicle unless you are asked to get out.

citations.quote: Drive as closely as is safely practical to the right-hand edge or curb of the road, clear of any intersection, stop and park.

questions.stem: During a traffic stop, a driver who has a handgun permit should:

options.text: Say nothing about it
Hand the weapon to the officer
Advise the officer of the permit and whether they are armed

questions.correctOption: Advise the officer of the permit and whether they are armed
questions.explanation: Tell the officer up front, and keep your hands visible while you do.

citations.quote: Drivers should advise officers if they have a handgun permit and if they are armed.

questions.stem: If an unmarked car signals you to pull over, you may:

options.text: Drive slowly a short distance to the nearest area where there are other people
Ignore it entirely
Accelerate away to a police station

questions.correctOption: Drive slowly a short distance to the nearest area where there are other people
questions.explanation: Slow down, put on your flashers to show you are complying, and stop somewhere populated.

citations.quote: If you find yourself being directed to pull over and stop by someone in an UNMARKED police car, you may drive slowly a short distance to the nearest area where there are other people

questions.stem: Your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks. You should:

options.text: Push the vehicle backward off the tracks first
Get everyone out immediately and away from the tracks, then call the number on the ENS sign or 911
Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it

questions.correctOption: Get everyone out immediately and away from the tracks, then call the number on the ENS sign or 911
questions.explanation: People first, even if you cannot see a train. The Emergency Notification System sign carries the number that stops trains.

citations.quote: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, all occupants should exit the vehicle immediately and get away from the tracks even if you do not see a train. Locate the Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign and call the emergency number provided

questions.stem: If a train is approaching your stalled vehicle on the tracks, you should run:

options.text: Toward the train at a 45 degree angle
Directly away from the tracks in line with the car
Alongside the tracks in the direction the train is going

questions.correctOption: Toward the train at a 45 degree angle
questions.explanation: Running toward the train at an angle takes you away from and behind the point of impact, where the debris is thrown.

citations.quote: If a train is approaching, run toward the train at a 45 degree angle. This allows you to be away from and behind the point of impact, to prevent injury.

questions.stem: You are already crossing the tracks when the warning lights start flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and reverse clear of the crossing
Stop where you are and wait
Keep moving and never try to back up

questions.correctOption: Keep moving and never try to back up
questions.explanation: Keep going. Gates are designed to break, and reversing puts you back into the path of the train.

citations.quote: If you are crossing the tracks and the warning lights begin flashing or the gates start coming down, don't stop. KEEP MOVING!

questions.stem: Where a crossing has more than one track, a driver waiting for a train to pass must:

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front closely to clear the crossing
Make sure another train is not approaching from the opposite direction
Cross as soon as the last car passes

questions.correctOption: Make sure another train is not approaching from the opposite direction
questions.explanation: The passing train hides the second one until it is on top of you.

citations.quote: Where there is more than one track, a driver waiting for one train to pass must make sure another train is not approaching from the opposite direction.

questions.stem: Headlights must be turned on:

options.text: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
Only after full darkness
One hour after sunset until sunrise

questions.correctOption: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
questions.explanation: The half-hour margins cover dusk and dawn, when the light is worst for spotting pedestrians.

citations.quote: Your car headlights must be turned on 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

questions.stem: Headlights are also required any time daylight is not good enough to see people or vehicles clearly at:

options.text: 200 feet ahead
50 feet ahead
1,000 feet ahead

questions.correctOption: 200 feet ahead
questions.explanation: Two hundred feet is also the distance your headlights must let you see a person at night.

citations.quote: At any time when daylight is not good enough for you to see persons or vehicles clearly at a distance of 200 feet ahead

questions.stem: In Tennessee, when precipitation requires constant use of your windshield wipers, headlights are:

options.text: Optional but recommended
Required only on interstates
Required by law

questions.correctOption: Required by law
questions.explanation: Wipers on means lights on — that is the law, not just a courtesy.

citations.quote: using headlights when wipers are in use is not just a good safety precaution — it's Tennessee law!

questions.stem: You must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:

options.text: 100 feet
1,000 feet
500 feet

questions.correctOption: 500 feet
questions.explanation: Five hundred feet — roughly a city block — whether you are meeting the vehicle or following it.

citations.quote: you must dim or lower the beam when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet (approximately the distance of one city block) or when you are following another vehicle within 500 feet.

questions.stem: Driving on parking lights alone when visibility is limited is:

options.text: Permitted below 30 m.p.h.
Against the law
Permitted in town

questions.correctOption: Against the law
questions.explanation: Parking lights mark a stopped car. They are not enough to drive by, and the law says so.

citations.quote: When there is limited visibility, the use of parking lights alone is not only unsafe, it is against the law.

questions.stem: Using fog lights or auxiliary lights by themselves is:

options.text: Legal when it is raining
Illegal
Legal in rural areas

questions.correctOption: Illegal
questions.explanation: They are also illegal at any time you are required to dim your high beams.

citations.quote: It is also illegal to have auxiliary lights or fog lights on by themselves or on at times when you are required to dim high beam headlights.

questions.stem: Steady-burning lights displayed to the front of a vehicle in Tennessee may only be:

options.text: White or amber
Any color except red
Blue, on any vehicle

questions.correctOption: White or amber
questions.explanation: White or amber only, with narrow exceptions for certain vehicles. Colored forward lighting is a violation.

citations.quote: Effective January 1, 2018, no vehicle operated in Tennessee shall be equipped with any steady-burning lights that display to the front of the vehicle in any color other than white or amber or in any combination of colors other than white and amber.

questions.stem: An unauthorized private vehicle equipped with a blue flashing light is:

options.text: Legal if it is only used off-road
Legal with a permit from any county
In violation of the law, even if the light is never switched on visibly

questions.correctOption: In violation of the law, even if the light is never switched on visibly
questions.explanation: The law reaches installing, maintaining or visibly showing blue — or blue and red — emergency lights on a private vehicle.

citations.quote: It is against the law for an unauthorized private vehicle to have a blue flashing emergency light or combination of blue and red flashing emergency lights installed, maintained or visibly shown on the vehicle in any manner.

questions.stem: Driving through dense fog, heavy rain or snow in the daytime, Tennessee law requires you to:

options.text: Use hazard lights instead of headlights
Turn on your low beam headlights
Use your high beams

questions.correctOption: Turn on your low beam headlights
questions.explanation: Low beams put light where you need it and make you visible to oncoming drivers.

citations.quote: WHEN DRIVING THROUGH DENSE FOG, HEAVY RAIN OR SNOW DURING THE DAYTIME, TURN ON YOU LOW BEAM HEADLIGHTS

questions.stem: When you park on or along a highway at night, you should:

options.text: Leave your emergency and parking lights on, but never your headlights
Leave your headlights on so you can be seen
Switch off all lights to save the battery

questions.correctOption: Leave your emergency and parking lights on, but never your headlights
questions.explanation: Headlights left on blind approaching drivers and confuse them about where the road goes.

citations.quote: Whenever you park on or along a highway at night, leave your emergency and parking lights on.
When parking at night, never leave your headlights on, even if

questions.stem: Hazard (four-way) flashers may be displayed during hours of darkness when:

options.text: You are looking for an address
The vehicle is disabled or otherwise presents a traffic hazard
You are driving faster than traffic

questions.correctOption: The vehicle is disabled or otherwise presents a traffic hazard
questions.explanation: They mark a hazard, which is why they belong on a disabled vehicle rather than a moving one.

citations.quote: The "hazard" or four-way flashing directional lights may be displayed during the hours of darkness when a vehicle is disabled or otherwise presents a traffic hazard.

questions.stem: In normal daylight, a vehicle with its headlights on is visible:

options.text: At half the distance
At twice the distance
At about the same distance

questions.correctOption: At twice the distance
questions.explanation: Daytime headlights double the distance at which other drivers pick you out — cheap insurance.

citations.quote: In normal daylight, vehicles are visible at twice the distance when headlights are on.

questions.stem: Tennessee law prohibits a driver from using a hand-held telephone or personal digital assistant to:

options.text: Make any call at all, even hands-free
Carry it in the vehicle
Transmit or read a written message while the vehicle is in motion

questions.correctOption: Transmit or read a written message while the vehicle is in motion
questions.explanation: Reading counts, not just typing. The offense is complete the moment the vehicle is moving.

citations.quote: hand-held personal digital assistant to transmit or read a written message while the driver's motor vehicle is in motion

questions.stem: Who is exempt from Tennessee's texting-while-driving law?

options.text: Law enforcement, firefighters, emergency medical persons and emergency management officers in the discharge of official duties
Anyone using a phone mount
Drivers over 65

questions.correctOption: Law enforcement, firefighters, emergency medical persons and emergency management officers in the discharge of official duties
questions.explanation: The exemption is narrow: on-duty emergency personnel only, while actually discharging their duties.

citations.quote: Law enforcement officers, firefighters, emergency medical persons and emergency management agency officers when in the actual discharge of their official duties, are exempt from the provisions of the law.

questions.stem: For a driver 18 or older, using a hand-held mobile phone in a marked school zone while the warning flasher is operating is:

options.text: An offense only if children are present
An offense, unless the phone is in hands-free mode
Always permitted

questions.correctOption: An offense, unless the phone is in hands-free mode
questions.explanation: The flasher is the trigger. Hands-free mode is the only way an adult driver may use the phone there.

citations.quote: Effective January 1, 2018, it is an offense for persons 18 years or older to use a hand-held mobile phone while a motor vehicle is in motion in any marked school zone in this state, when a warning flasher or flashers are in operation. There is an exception if the phone is being used in hands free mode.

questions.stem: The hands-free exception for phone use in a marked school zone:

options.text: Does not apply to drivers under 18, and creates a delinquent act for them
Applies to everyone
Applies only to drivers over 21

questions.correctOption: Does not apply to drivers under 18, and creates a delinquent act for them
questions.explanation: A driver under 18 has no hands-free workaround in a flashing school zone.

citations.quote: This exception also does not apply to persons under eighteen (18) years of age and creates a delinquent act for these individuals.

questions.stem: State law prohibits installing a video monitor or screen in a vehicle when it is:

options.text: Mounted anywhere on the dashboard
Capable of displaying a television broadcast or video signal visible to the driver while the vehicle is in motion
Larger than eight inches

questions.correctOption: Capable of displaying a television broadcast or video signal visible to the driver while the vehicle is in motion
questions.explanation: The test is whether the driver can see moving video while driving.

citations.quote: State law prohibits the installation of a video monitor or video screen capable of displaying a television broadcast or video signal that is intended to display an image visible to the driver of a vehicle while in motion.

questions.stem: Which in-vehicle display is NOT prohibited by the video device law?

options.text: A television tuner visible to the driver
A movie player visible to the driver
A navigation or GPS device

questions.correctOption: A navigation or GPS device
questions.explanation: Navigation, vehicle information displays and camera views forward, behind and to the sides are all allowed.

citations.quote: A navigation or global positioning device, a vehicle information system display, visual displays for the driver's view forward, behind and the sides of the vehicle are not prohibited.

questions.stem: Where should video equipment be placed in a vehicle?

options.text: Where it creates no visual obstruction
Directly in the center of the windshield
Anywhere the driver can reach it easily

questions.correctOption: Where it creates no visual obstruction
questions.explanation: Even a legal display becomes a hazard if it blocks your view of the road.

citations.quote: Careful consideration should be given to the placement of this equipment to insure no visual obstructions.

questions.stem: An adult driver receives a notice of proposed suspension after accumulating how many points in a 12-month period?

options.text: 6 or more
20 or more
12 or more

questions.correctOption: 12 or more
questions.explanation: Twelve for an adult. A driver under 18 gets the same notice at six.

citations.quote: Adult drivers (18 years of age or older) who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

questions.stem: A driver under 18 receives a notice of proposed suspension after accumulating how many points in 12 months?

options.text: 6 or more
12 or more
3 or more

questions.correctOption: 6 or more
questions.explanation: Half the adult threshold — and an advisory letter goes out at just one point.

citations.quote: Juvenile drivers (less than 18 years of age) who accumulate 6 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

questions.stem: An advisory letter is mailed to an adult licensee who has how many points within 12 months?

options.text: 6 to 11
1 to 5

questions.correctOption: 6 to 11
questions.explanation: It is a warning shot before the suspension threshold at twelve.

citations.quote: an advisory letter is mailed to any licensee having 6 to 11 points on his/her driving record within any 12 months.

questions.stem: How many points does contributing to a crash that causes bodily injury add to your record?

options.text: 4 points
1 point
8 points

questions.correctOption: 4 points
questions.explanation: Three for property damage, four for injury, eight for a death.

citations.quote: 4 Contributing to a crash resulting in bodily injury

questions.stem: Passing a stopped school, church or youth bus that is loading or discharging passengers is worth:

options.text: 1 point
8 points
3 points

questions.correctOption: 8 points
questions.explanation: Eight points — the same as failing to stop at a railroad crossing, and enough to suspend a teen driver on its own.

citations.quote: 8 Passing stopped school, church or youth bus taking on or discharging passengers

questions.stem: Reckless driving carries how many points?

options.text: 2 points
8 points
6 points

questions.correctOption: 6 points
questions.explanation: Six for reckless driving; reckless endangerment by vehicle is eight.

citations.quote: 6 Reckless driving

questions.stem: Operating a vehicle without your driver license in your possession carries:

options.text: 2 points
6 points
No points

questions.correctOption: 2 points
questions.explanation: Small compared with the moving violations, but it still goes on the record.

citations.quote: 2 Operating without driver license in possession

questions.stem: The Defensive Driving Course option for avoiding or reducing a suspension is available:

options.text: Once per calendar year
Any number of times
Once in any five-year period

questions.correctOption: Once in any five-year period
questions.explanation: Once every five years. It is a second chance, not a subscription.

citations.quote: the Defensive Driving Course option is only available once in any five-year period.

questions.stem: A suspended or revoked license must be surrendered to the Department of Safety within:

options.text: 20 days
48 hours
90 days

questions.correctOption: 20 days
questions.explanation: Twenty days, and failing to hand it in costs a $75 fine on top of everything else.

citations.quote: Whenever a driver license is suspended or revoked, it must be turned in to the Department of Safety within 20 days of the suspension or revocation.

questions.stem: Driving while your license is suspended will:

options.text: Restart the suspension at zero
Have no effect on the suspension
Extend the suspension period and could bring criminal prosecution

questions.correctOption: Extend the suspension period and could bring criminal prosecution
questions.explanation: The clock stretches, and you may face prosecution as well.

citations.quote: DRIVING WHILE YOUR LICENSE IS SUSPENDED WILL RESULT IN THE EXTENSION OF THE SUSPENSION PERIOD AND COULD ALSO RESULT IN CRIMINAL PROSECUTION.

questions.stem: Tennessee's Financial Responsibility Law requires a driver to produce evidence of financial responsibility:

options.text: Only when renewing a registration
When charged with any violation or involved in a crash, without regard to fault
Only when found at fault in a crash

questions.correctOption: When charged with any violation or involved in a crash, without regard to fault
questions.explanation: Fault is irrelevant to the requirement — you have to be able to show it either way.

citations.quote: the Financial Responsibility Law requires drivers to produce evidence of financial responsibility. This is required when charged with any violation or when involved in a motor vehicle crash without regard to apparent or actual fault.

questions.stem: Which type of insurance is NOT required by Tennessee law?

options.text: Collision insurance
Liability coverage or other evidence of financial responsibility
None — all coverage types are required

questions.correctOption: Collision insurance
questions.explanation: Collision covers your own car and is optional. What the law demands is proof you can answer for damage you cause.

citations.quote: Although collision insurance is not required by Tennessee law, the Financial Responsibility Law requires drivers to produce evidence of financial responsibility.

questions.stem: Which of these covers damages you cause to other people?

options.text: Collision insurance
Uninsured motorist insurance
Liability insurance

questions.correctOption: Liability insurance
questions.explanation: Liability pays others; collision repairs your vehicle; uninsured motorist covers what an uninsured driver does to you.

citations.quote: Liability insurance provides coverage for damages you cause to other persons.

questions.stem: A crash must be reported immediately to police when it involves death, injury or property damage over:
questions.explanation: Fifty dollars triggers the duty to notify police. A written Owner/Driver Report is required when damage to any one person's property exceeds $400.

citations.quote: Drivers must immediately notify the local police department if the crash occurs within a municipality, otherwise to the County Sheriff's office or the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol, of any crash involving death, injury or property damage over fifty dollars ($50).

questions.stem: A crash is "reportable" in Tennessee when someone is killed or injured, or when property damage to any one person exceeds:
questions.explanation: Over four hundred dollars — including damage to your own property — makes it reportable.

citations.quote: These include any crash within this state in which any person is killed or injured, or in which damage to the property of any one person, including oneself, is in excess of four hundred dollars ($400).

questions.stem: The law requires a driver involved in a crash to:

options.text: Drive to the nearest police station
Continue if the damage looks minor
Stop immediately at the scene, or as close as possible without obstructing traffic

questions.correctOption: Stop immediately at the scene, or as close as possible without obstructing traffic
questions.explanation: Leaving the scene of any crash is its own offense, and it is a ground for revocation.

citations.quote: The law requires drivers of vehicles involved in a crash to stop immediately at the scene, or as close to the scene as possible without obstructing traffic.

questions.stem: At a crash scene, you should not move an injured person from a wrecked vehicle unless:

options.text: The vehicle is blocking traffic
You have medical or rescue training, or there is an immediate danger such as fire
They ask you to

questions.correctOption: You have medical or rescue training, or there is an immediate danger such as fire
questions.explanation: Moving someone with a spinal injury can do permanent damage. Fire is the exception that overrides that risk.

citations.quote: Do not attempt to move an injured person from a wrecked vehicle unless you have the necessary medical or rescue training or there is an immediate danger such as fire.

questions.stem: After a crash you must exchange:

options.text: Names, addresses, driver license numbers, plate numbers and insurance policy numbers
Only your phone number
Nothing, if police were called

questions.correctOption: Names, addresses, driver license numbers, plate numbers and insurance policy numbers
questions.explanation: Take the witnesses' details too — memories fade and stories change.

citations.quote: Exchange information with other persons involved in the crash as soon as possible. Be sure to get the following information:
name, address and driver's license number of other drivers; • license plate numbers of other vehicles; • name and address of anyone who was injured; • name and address of each witness;
name, address and insurance policy number of other vehicle owners.

questions.stem: Failing to report a reportable crash may result in:

options.text: A written warning only
No consequence if no one was hurt
Suspension of driving and registration privileges

questions.correctOption: Suspension of driving and registration privileges
questions.explanation: Both your license and your plates can be suspended over a missing report.

citations.quote: Failure to report a crash may result in suspension of driving and registration privileges.

questions.stem: Tennessee is a member of the Non-Resident Violator Compact, which means that ignoring a traffic citation from another member state will:

options.text: Get your Tennessee driving privileges suspended, revoked or canceled
Have no effect in Tennessee
Only affect you if you return to that state

questions.correctOption: Get your Tennessee driving privileges suspended, revoked or canceled
questions.explanation: The suspension stays until that court tells Tennessee the citation has been dealt with.
