citations.quote: If you ignore the citation — whether it was issued for a traffic violation here or in another member state, your driving privileges will be suspended, revoked or canceled.

questions.stem: Two reckless driving violations within 12 months are:

options.text: Erased after one year
A ground for revoking or suspending a Tennessee driver license
Worth a warning letter only

questions.correctOption: A ground for revoking or suspending a Tennessee driver license
questions.explanation: It is item 9 on the manual's list of grounds for losing the privilege to drive.

citations.quote: In Tennessee, a driver license may be revoked or suspended for the following situations:
9. Two reckless driving violations within 12 months.

questions.stem: A driver whose ability to drive is affected by a physical or mental disorder must submit a medical report from a doctor within:

options.text: One year of notification
30 days of notification
6 months of notification

questions.correctOption: 30 days of notification
questions.explanation: Thirty days from the notice. The department can also require re-examination.

citations.quote: the driver will be required to submit (within thirty (30) days of notification) a medical report from a medical doctor.

questions.stem: A driver who loses consciousness due to epilepsy, cardiac syncope or diabetes must remain lapse-free for how long before reinstatement is possible?

options.text: Thirty days
Two years
At least six months

questions.correctOption: At least six months
questions.explanation: Six months clear, under a doctor's care, before driving privileges can come back.

citations.quote: Drivers who lose consciousness or control due to epilepsy, cardiac syncope, diabetes or other conditions must be suspended and remain lapse free for a minimum of six (6) months before being eligible for license reinstatement.

questions.stem: You must notify the Department of Safety of a change of residence address within:

options.text: 60 days
10 days
30 days

questions.correctOption: 10 days
questions.explanation: Ten days — even if the address changed without you moving. Notices about your license go to the address on file.

citations.quote: If you have a new address, you must report it to the Department of Safety within ten (10) days of the change.

questions.stem: The manual calls concentration:

options.text: One of the most important elements of safe and defensive driving
A skill only new drivers need
Less important than fast reflexes

questions.correctOption: One of the most important elements of safe and defensive driving
questions.explanation: Keeping your mind on driving is a habit you build deliberately, the same way you built the habit of checking your mirrors.

citations.quote: Concentration is one of the most important elements of safe and defensive driving. You must develop the habit of keeping your mind on driving.

questions.stem: According to the manual, the driver’s seat is no place for:

options.text: Checking your blind spot
Daydreaming, sightseeing or distracting conversations
Adjusting your mirrors before you set off

questions.correctOption: Daydreaming, sightseeing or distracting conversations
questions.explanation: A conversation that pulls your attention off the road is a distraction whether or not a phone is involved.

citations.quote: The driver’s safety is no place for daydreaming, site-seeing or distracting conversations.

questions.stem: Which does the manual list among the leading factors in crashes?

options.text: Vehicle colour
Low tyre pressure
Lack of concentration

questions.correctOption: Lack of concentration
questions.explanation: Excessive speed, lack of concentration and improper evasive action are the three it names — and human error is the single most common cause.

citations.quote: The leading factors in crashes are:
Excessive Speed • Lack of Concentration • Improper Evasive Action

questions.stem: When checking the traffic behind you, the manual warns that you should not:

options.text: Check behind before changing lanes
Keep your eyes off the road ahead for more than a brief look behind
Use your mirrors at all while moving

questions.correctOption: Keep your eyes off the road ahead for more than a brief look behind
questions.explanation: Mirror checks are quick glances. Anything longer and the road ahead has changed without you.

citations.quote: But don’t keep you eyes off the road ahead for more than a brief look behind.

questions.stem: Driving with your seat in a reclined or semi-reclined position:

options.text: Improves your view of the mirrors
Reduces both your vision and your ability to react
Is safer on long trips

questions.correctOption: Reduces both your vision and your ability to react
questions.explanation: Reclined, you cannot see the road properly and the safety belt no longer lies against your body where it can hold you.

citations.quote: DO NOT DRIVE WITH THE SEAT IN A RECLINED OR SEMI-RECLINED POSITION. This is dangerous and reduces both your vision and your ability to react to emergency situations.

questions.stem: Turning the ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is still moving will:

options.text: Lock the steering wheel and cost you control of the vehicle
Bring the vehicle to a controlled stop
Do nothing until the vehicle stops

questions.correctOption: Lock the steering wheel and cost you control of the vehicle
questions.explanation: The wheel locks as soon as you try to turn it, and there is no steering left at all.

citations.quote: never turn the ignition to the lock position when the vehicle is in motion The steering wheel will lock when trying to turn and the control of the vehicle will be lost.

questions.stem: The manual recommends the Push-Pull steering method because it:

options.text: Lets you steer with one hand
Turns the wheel faster than hand-over-hand
Slows the turning movement and keeps both hands on the wheel through the manoeuvre

questions.correctOption: Slows the turning movement and keeps both hands on the wheel through the manoeuvre
questions.explanation: Smoother inputs are easier to correct, and both hands stay where an emergency will need them.

citations.quote: The Push-Pull method is recommended because it slows down turning movements making for a smoother, safer turn. It also keeps both hands on the steering wheel through the entire maneuver.

questions.stem: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning you should never:

options.text: Let the engine run in a closed garage
Drive with a window cracked open
Use the defroster in winter

questions.correctOption: Let the engine run in a closed garage
questions.explanation: The manual also warns against running the heater or air conditioner in a parked car with the windows closed.

citations.quote: Never let the engine run in a closed garage • Do not use a heater/air conditioner in a parked car with the windows closed.

questions.stem: In normal daylight, switching your headlights on makes your vehicle visible:

options.text: At the same distance
Only to vehicles behind you
At twice the distance

questions.correctOption: At twice the distance
questions.explanation: Being seen sooner gives every other driver more time to make room for you.

citations.quote: In normal daylight, vehicles are visible at twice the distance when headlights are on.

questions.stem: Using the penny test, a tire is illegal and unsafe when the tread does not reach:

options.text: 1/2 inch
Lincoln's head, about 2/32 of an inch
The edge of the coin

questions.correctOption: Lincoln's head, about 2/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Below 2/32 of an inch the tire cannot clear water, and it must be replaced.

citations.quote: If the tread does not come at least to Lincoln's head (2/32 inch), the tire is illegal and unsafe and you need it replaced.

questions.stem: If your license carries Restriction Code 01 for corrective lenses you must wear them:

options.text: At all times when driving
Only at night
Only when driving on the interstate

questions.correctOption: At all times when driving
questions.explanation: Driving without them can bring a ticket and a fine — and the manual advises keeping a spare pair in the vehicle.

citations.quote: If your driver license indicates you must wear corrective lenses (Restriction Code 01) you must wear them at all times when driving. You could be fined and receive a ticket if stopped while driving without your glasses or contacts.

questions.stem: The manual advises drivers to have their eyes checked by a specialist:

options.text: Only after a crash
Every year or two
Once every ten years

questions.correctOption: Every year or two
questions.explanation: You drive on what you see, and vision degrades slowly enough that you will not notice it yourself.

citations.quote: you should have your eyes checked every year or two by an eye specialist

questions.stem: At night, dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses should be:

options.text: Avoided, because they cut down the light you need to see clearly
Worn to reduce headlight glare
Worn only on the interstate

questions.correctOption: Avoided, because they cut down the light you need to see clearly
questions.explanation: They take away light you cannot spare after dark. Clean glass and properly aimed headlights are the real answer to glare.

citations.quote: Avoid using dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night, they cut down the light you need to see clearly.

questions.stem: The manual says drivers with a hearing impairment:

options.text: Cannot be licensed in Tennessee
Must have a special vehicle
Have driving records statistically just as good as drivers with good hearing

questions.correctOption: Have driving records statistically just as good as drivers with good hearing
questions.explanation: They compensate by relying more on vision, and the records bear it out.

citations.quote: Statistically the driving records of hearing-impaired drivers are just as good as those drivers with good hearing.

questions.stem: Which temporary condition does the manual list as something that can make you an unsafe driver?

options.text: Anger, worry, frustration, fatigue or a minor illness such as a cold
Driving a car you are unfamiliar with
Carrying passengers

questions.correctOption: Anger, worry, frustration, fatigue or a minor illness such as a cold
questions.explanation: Being in shape to drive is mental and emotional as well as physical.

citations.quote: Anger, worry, frustration, fatigue and minor illnesses such as a cold are a few of the temporary conditions that can make you an unsafe driver.

questions.stem: Peripheral (side) vision is important because it lets you:

options.text: Judge your following distance
Spot vehicles and trouble to either side while you look ahead
Read road signs at a distance

questions.correctOption: Spot vehicles and trouble to either side while you look ahead
questions.explanation: You cannot focus on what is beside you, so side mirrors and the occasional glance fill the gap.

citations.quote: This lets you spot vehicle and other potential trouble on either side of you while you look ahead.

questions.stem: In Tennessee, an officer:

options.text: Can stop and ticket a driver solely for a safety belt or child restraint violation
Can only cite a belt violation after stopping you for something else
Cannot cite belt violations at all

questions.correctOption: Can stop and ticket a driver solely for a safety belt or child restraint violation
questions.explanation: The belt law is primary enforcement — the violation itself is reason enough for the stop.

citations.quote: Officers can stop and ticket drivers solely for disobeying Safety belt and Child Restraint Device (CRD) laws.

questions.stem: Safety belts are required for the driver and all front-seat passengers:

options.text: Only on highways
Any time the vehicle is in motion
Only above 30 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: Any time the vehicle is in motion
questions.explanation: In motion is the test — most crashes happen close to home at low speed.

citations.quote: Safety belts are required for ALL drivers and all passengers in the FRONT seat, any time the vehicle is in motion.

questions.stem: A child under one year old, or any child weighing less than 20 pounds, must ride in:

options.text: A forward-facing car seat
A booster seat with the lap belt only
A rear-facing child passenger restraint system

questions.correctOption: A rear-facing child passenger restraint system
questions.explanation: Rear-facing spreads crash forces across the whole back and supports the head and neck.

citations.quote: A child under one year old, or any child weighing less than 20 pounds, must be in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) that is facing the rear of the car.

questions.stem: A child aged one through three who weighs more than 20 pounds must ride in:

options.text: A forward-facing child passenger restraint system
A rear-facing car seat
An ordinary lap belt

questions.correctOption: A forward-facing child passenger restraint system
questions.explanation: Forward-facing with a harness is the next step up from rear-facing.

citations.quote: Children who are one through three years old, and who weigh more than 20 pounds, must be in a child passenger restraint system that is facing forward.

questions.stem: A passenger four through eight years old and shorter than four feet nine inches must be:

options.text: Held on an adult's lap
In a belt-positioning booster seat and wearing a seatbelt
In an ordinary seat with a lap belt

questions.correctOption: In a belt-positioning booster seat and wearing a seatbelt
questions.explanation: The booster lifts the child so the adult belt crosses the hips and the chest instead of the abdomen and the neck.

citations.quote: Children who are four through eight years old and whose height is under four feet, nine inches, must be in a belt positioning booster seat system (child booster car seat) and wearing a seatbelt.

questions.stem: Children in booster seats must ride:

options.text: In the front seat, where the driver can see them
Wherever there is room
In the back seat, if the vehicle has one

questions.correctOption: In the back seat, if the vehicle has one
questions.explanation: The back seat is out of reach of the passenger air bag.

citations.quote: If the passenger is four through eight years old and is shorter than four feet, nine inches in height. These passengers must be in a child booster seat at all times. Children in booster seats must be in the back seat of a vehicle, if the vehicle has a back seat.

questions.stem: The driver is responsible for the proper restraint of children up to what age?

options.text: Sixteen
Twelve
Eighteen

questions.correctOption: Sixteen
questions.explanation: Up to sixteen, and an unrestrained child under 16 can bring the driver a $50 fine.

citations.quote: which makes the driver responsible for their protection up to the age of sixteen (16). If children under age 16 are not properly restrained, the driver may be charged and fined $50.00 for violation of the law.

questions.stem: If a child's parent or legal guardian is in the car but not driving:

options.text: Nobody can be cited
The parent or guardian is responsible for the child being properly transported and may be fined
Only the driver can be cited

questions.correctOption: The parent or guardian is responsible for the child being properly transported and may be fined
questions.explanation: The responsibility follows the parent into the passenger seat.

citations.quote: If the child's parent or legal guardian is present in the car but not driving, then the parent or legal guardian is responsible for making sure that the child is properly transported and may be fined for non-compliance.

questions.stem: Failing to use a car seat or booster for a child under nine can be charged as:

options.text: A parking violation
A civil matter only
A Class C misdemeanor, with a required class on safely transporting children

questions.correctOption: A Class C misdemeanor, with a required class on safely transporting children
questions.explanation: The class is part of the penalty — the state would rather teach the seat than collect the fine.

citations.quote: The driver can be charged with a Class C misdemeanor, required to attend a class on safely transporting children and required to pay possible fees and fines.

questions.stem: Where on the body should the lap belt sit?

options.text: Low over the pelvis, with the bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs
Across the soft part of the abdomen
Above the hip bones at the waist

questions.correctOption: Low over the pelvis, with the bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs
questions.explanation: The pelvis is bone and can take the load. The abdomen cannot.

citations.quote: The lap belt should be worn low over the pelvis with the bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs snugly.

questions.stem: The shoulder belt should be worn:

options.text: Under the arm
Behind the back for comfort
Over the shoulder and across the chest

questions.correctOption: Over the shoulder and across the chest
questions.explanation: Under the arm puts the belt across the ribs and abdomen, which is where the injuries come from.

citations.quote: The shoulder belt should be worn over the shoulder and across the chest, not under the arm and over the abdomen.

questions.stem: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recommends how much space between your chest and the air bag module?

options.text: Twenty-four inches
Ten to twelve inches
Two to four inches

questions.correctOption: Ten to twelve inches
questions.explanation: The bag needs room to inflate before it meets you.

citations.quote: Ten (10) to twelve (12) inches between the chest and the air bag module is recommended by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

questions.stem: In Tennessee it is illegal to let a child under what age ride in the bed of a pickup truck?
questions.explanation: Under 6 is banned outright, and children between 6 and 12 may not ride in the bed on any state or interstate highway.

citations.quote: It is illegal in Tennessee to allow any child under the age of 6 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck.

questions.stem: Children between 6 and 12 may not ride in the bed of a pickup truck:

options.text: Only after dark
On any state or interstate highway
Anywhere at any time

questions.correctOption: On any state or interstate highway
questions.explanation: There are narrow exceptions for parades under 20 m.p.h. and for agricultural work.

citations.quote: It is also against the law to allow any child between the ages of 6 and 12 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck on any state or interstate highway.

questions.stem: Leaving a child younger than 7 unattended in a motor vehicle, with no one at least 13 years old supervising, is:

options.text: An offense
Permitted for up to fifteen minutes
Permitted if the doors are locked

questions.correctOption: An offense
questions.explanation: The offense is complete where conditions present a risk, the engine is running or the keys are in the passenger compartment.

citations.quote: It is an offense for a person responsible for a child younger than 7 years of age to knowingly leave that child in a motor vehicle

questions.stem: A first offense of leaving a child unattended in a vehicle is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by a fine of:
questions.explanation: Two hundred dollars for the first offense, five hundred for a second or subsequent one.

citations.quote: (b) A violation of this section is a Class B misdemeanor punishable only by a fine of two hundred dollars ($200) for the first offense. (c) A second or subsequent violation of this section is a Class B misdemeanor punishable only by a fine of five hundred dollars ($500).

questions.stem: When a medically prescribed modified child restraint device is used, the vehicle must carry:

options.text: Nothing extra
A copy of the doctor's prescription at all times
A note from the school

questions.correctOption: A copy of the doctor's prescription at all times
questions.explanation: The prescription is what makes the non-standard device lawful, so it travels with the child.

citations.quote: A copy of a doctor's prescription should be carried in the vehicle utilizing the modified child restraint device (CRD) at all times.

questions.stem: In a 15-passenger van in Tennessee, safety belts must be worn by:

options.text: The driver only
The driver and front passenger only
All occupants, at all times

questions.correctOption: All occupants, at all times
questions.explanation: It is the law here, and these vans are unusually prone to rollover when loaded.

citations.quote: All occupants in 15-passenger vans must wear safety belts at all times. This is the law in Tennessee, as well as many other states.

questions.stem: Operating a 15-passenger van in Tennessee requires:

options.text: A For-Hire endorsement in every case
No special endorsement or license
A Class A commercial license

questions.correctOption: No special endorsement or license
questions.explanation: No special credential — which is exactly why the manual spends a page on how differently they handle.

citations.quote: There are no special endorsements or licenses needed to operate a 15-passenger van in the State of Tennessee.

questions.stem: Tennessee law states that a driver shall not follow another vehicle:

options.text: Closer than 100 feet at any speed
More closely than is reasonable and prudent for the speed, traffic and road condition
Closer than exactly two car lengths

questions.correctOption: More closely than is reasonable and prudent for the speed, traffic and road condition
questions.explanation: The standard is judgment-based, which is why the manual gives you the two-second rule as a way to measure it.

citations.quote: Tennessee law states: "The driver of a motor vehicle shall not follow another vehicle more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway."

questions.stem: To use the two-second rule you pick a fixed object ahead and:

options.text: Count the car lengths between you
Count "one-thousand and one, one-thousand and two" after the vehicle ahead passes it
Time how long the vehicle ahead takes to reach it

questions.correctOption: Count "one-thousand and one, one-thousand and two" after the vehicle ahead passes it
questions.explanation: If you reach the object before you finish the count, you are too close and need to drop back.

citations.quote: Count to yourself "one-thousand and one, one-thousand and two," etc.

questions.stem: In inclement weather, at interstate speeds, at night, or when following a motorcycle, the following interval should be increased to a minimum of:

options.text: Four seconds
Three seconds
Two and a half seconds

questions.correctOption: Four seconds
questions.explanation: More time to react is the only thing that compensates for less grip and less visibility.

citations.quote: A minimum of four seconds should allow for better reaction time and a safer space cushion under these conditions including following a motorcycle.

questions.stem: The three steps in stopping a vehicle are:

options.text: Coasting, braking and steering
Perception time, reaction time and braking time
Seeing, signaling and stopping

questions.correctOption: Perception time, reaction time and braking time
questions.explanation: Two of the three happen before the brakes are even touched, which is why speed hurts stopping distance so badly.

citations.quote: There are three steps in stopping a vehicle: • Perception time: The length of time it takes a driver to see and recognize a dangerous situation. • Reaction time: The time from perception of danger to the start of braking.

questions.stem: Average reaction time — from perceiving danger to starting to brake — is about:

options.text: About 2/3 of a second
Two seconds
A tenth of a second

questions.correctOption: About 2/3 of a second
questions.explanation: At 55 m.p.h. that fraction of a second is already several car lengths of road.

citations.quote: • Reaction time: The time from perception of danger to the start of braking. The average is 2/3 of a second, as noted in blue section of charts on the next page.

questions.stem: With anti-lock brakes, you should:

options.text: Apply firm, steady pressure and never pump the pedal
Pump the pedal rapidly
Apply the parking brake as well

questions.correctOption: Apply firm, steady pressure and never pump the pedal
questions.explanation: The system does the pumping for you — far faster than a foot can — and pumping defeats it.

citations.quote: When slowing or stopping, apply firm, steady pressure to the brake pedal. Never pump the pedal with ABS.

questions.stem: When you stop behind another vehicle at an intersection, a good rule of thumb is that you should be able to see:

options.text: Only its rear bumper
The driver's mirrors
Its license plate and back tire where it meets the pavement

questions.correctOption: Its license plate and back tire where it meets the pavement
questions.explanation: That gap gives you room to pull around a stalled car, and room to absorb being hit from behind.

citations.quote: A basic rule of thumb is that you should be able to see the license plate and/or the other vehicle's back tire where it meets the pavement.

questions.stem: Stopping for a crosswalk on a multi-lane road, you should stop about how far back?

options.text: 30 feet before the crosswalk
Right at the crosswalk line
100 feet before the crosswalk

questions.correctOption: 30 feet before the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Stopping short keeps the crossing pedestrian visible to drivers in the other lanes instead of hidden behind your car.

citations.quote: When stopping for a crosswalk on a multi-lane road, you should stop about 30 feet before the crosswalk so you do not block visibility of the crossing pedestrians to drivers in the other lane(s).

questions.stem: Changing lanes, entering a roadway, or merging requires a gap of at least:

options.text: One second
Ten seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctOption: Four seconds
questions.explanation: Four seconds is the minimum gap for joining traffic; passing a single vehicle at 55 m.p.h. needs ten.

citations.quote: A minimum four-second gap is needed whenever you change lanes, enter a roadway or when your lane merges with another traffic lane.

questions.stem: At 55 m.p.h., completing a pass of a single vehicle takes about:

options.text: Twenty-five seconds
Ten seconds
Three seconds

questions.correctOption: Ten seconds
questions.explanation: So you need a ten-second gap in oncoming traffic — and the sight distance to see it.

citations.quote: At 55 M.P.H. you will need about ten (10) seconds to complete the pass of a single vehicle.

questions.stem: Every motor vehicle should approach a railroad crossing at a speed that:

options.text: Matches the posted highway limit
Clears the tracks as fast as possible
Permits stopping before the nearest rail

questions.correctOption: Permits stopping before the nearest rail
questions.explanation: If you cannot stop short of the rail, you are going too fast for the crossing.

citations.quote: Every motor vehicle should be driven at a rate of speed that will permit the vehicle to be stopped before reaching the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

questions.stem: Rolling stops are:

options.text: Acceptable when no traffic is present
Legal at flashing yellow lights
Dangerous, illegal, and grounds for failing the road test

questions.correctOption: Dangerous, illegal, and grounds for failing the road test
questions.explanation: A stop means complete cessation of movement — anything less is a ticket and a failed road test.

citations.quote: Rolling stops are grounds for receiving a traffic ticket AND for failing the driver examination road test.

questions.stem: The basic rule for safe night driving is:

options.text: Never outrun your headlights
Always use high beams
Follow the car ahead closely to use its lights

questions.correctOption: Never outrun your headlights
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance has to fit inside the distance your lights let you see.

citations.quote: The basic rule for safe night driving is this: NEVER OUTRUN YOUR HEADLIGHTS.

questions.stem: After dark, which abilities does the manual say are impaired?

options.text: Depth perception, color recognition and peripheral vision
Hearing and balance
Grip and reaction speed only

questions.correctOption: Depth perception, color recognition and peripheral vision
questions.explanation: Most of your reaction time depends on vision, and after dark vision is working with far less to go on.

citations.quote: Depth perception, color recognition, and peripheral vision are impaired after dark.

questions.stem: To cope with oncoming traffic at night, you should:

options.text: Increase speed to pass oncoming lights quickly
Switch to high beams as they approach
Make sure your stopping distance is less than your sight distance

questions.correctOption: Make sure your stopping distance is less than your sight distance
questions.explanation: It is the same idea as never outrunning your headlights, stated as a measurement you can check.

citations.quote: Make sure your stopping distance is less than your sight distance.

questions.stem: The best way to handle the glare of oncoming headlights is to:

options.text: Watch the right edge of the road and use the white line as a steering guide
Look straight at the oncoming lights
Close one eye

questions.correctOption: Watch the right edge of the road and use the white line as a steering guide
questions.explanation: Looking into the lights causes momentary blindness; looking right keeps you tracking your lane.

citations.quote: Avoid the glare of oncoming lights by watching the right edge of the road and using the white line or road edge as a steering guide.

questions.stem: Glare recovery time is:

options.text: The time it takes headlights to warm up
A measure of how bright your high beams are
The interval while the pupil readjusts after a vehicle passes, during which you are virtually driving blind

questions.correctOption: The interval while the pupil readjusts after a vehicle passes, during which you are virtually driving blind
questions.explanation: It varies from person to person and is generally worse for older drivers — another reason to slow down at night.

citations.quote: This is called glare recovery time. During this recovery period you are virtually driving blind.

questions.stem: Flashing your high beams to warn another driver:

options.text: Is the recommended way to communicate at night
Is required when passing
Should be avoided, because it may distract them and cause a collision

questions.correctOption: Should be avoided, because it may distract them and cause a collision
questions.explanation: You cannot control how the other driver reacts to being dazzled.

citations.quote: Avoid flashing your high beams to warn the other driver as it might serve as a distraction and interfere with their driving resulting in a collision.

questions.stem: Tennessee law requires headlights that let you see a person on the highway at least:

options.text: 500 feet ahead
200 feet ahead
50 feet ahead

questions.correctOption: 200 feet ahead
questions.explanation: Which means clean lenses, correct aim and working bulbs — headlights lose effectiveness fast with distance.

citations.quote: The law requires headlights that will enable you to see clearly any person on the highway at least two hundred (200) feet ahead of your car.

questions.stem: Headlights that shine up or out excessively:

options.text: Do not help you see, and they blind drivers you meet or follow
Improve your view of overhead signs
Are required for rural driving

questions.correctOption: Do not help you see, and they blind drivers you meet or follow
questions.explanation: Badly aimed lights are all cost and no benefit. Have them aligned.

citations.quote: Lights that shine up or out excessively do NOT help you see objects in the roadway. They do however contribute to glare and blinding the vision of drivers in vehicles you are meeting or following.

questions.stem: When are more fatal crashes recorded, according to the manual?

options.text: On Monday mornings
On weekday afternoons
On Friday and Saturday nights

questions.correctOption: On Friday and Saturday nights
questions.explanation: Night driving carries a much higher risk of a serious crash even though the roads are emptier.

citations.quote: More fatal crashes take place on Friday and Saturday nights than on any other day.

questions.stem: Parking at night, you should:

options.text: Never leave your headlights on, even briefly
Leave your headlights on so others can see you
Leave your high beams on if you are off the pavement

questions.correctOption: Never leave your headlights on, even briefly
questions.explanation: Parked headlights blind approaching drivers and confuse them about where the road runs.

citations.quote: When parking at night, never leave your headlights on, even if
you plan on being parked for a brief period of time. They are just as likely to blind approaching drivers when your car is stationary as they are when it is moving.

questions.stem: Wet pavement:

options.text: Can be as treacherous as icy pavement, so reduce speed in wet weather
Is only a problem above 60 m.p.h.
Improves tire grip slightly

questions.correctOption: Can be as treacherous as icy pavement, so reduce speed in wet weather
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop and you can skid on turns that would be routine when dry.

citations.quote: Wet pavement can be as treacherous as icy pavement, so always reduce your speed in wet weather.

questions.stem: Pavement is at its most treacherous:

options.text: After several hours of steady rain
Only when standing water is visible
When it first begins to rain, as dirt and oil mix with water

questions.correctOption: When it first begins to rain, as dirt and oil mix with water
questions.explanation: That greasy film takes a while to wash off, and it is exactly when drivers have not yet adjusted their speed.

citations.quote: The pavement is particularly treacherous when it first begins to rain. Accumulations of dirt and oil will mix with the water, and create a greasy film on the roadway.

questions.stem: Bridges and overpasses:

options.text: Are salted automatically
Tend to freeze before the rest of the road does
Stay warmer than the roadway

questions.correctOption: Tend to freeze before the rest of the road does
questions.explanation: Cold air circulates underneath them. Shade from trees and buildings hides ice for the same reason.

citations.quote: Bridges and overpasses can also hide spots of ice. They tend to freeze before the rest of the road does.

questions.stem: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually by letting up on the gas, and not slam on the brakes
Brake hard immediately
Accelerate to regain traction

questions.correctOption: Slow down gradually by letting up on the gas, and not slam on the brakes
questions.explanation: The tires are riding on water. Anything abrupt — brakes or steering — arrives as a shove when they touch down again.

citations.quote: a. If you vehicle starts to hydroplane, slow down gradually by letting up on the gas. b. Don't slam on the brakes.

questions.stem: When hydroplaning occurs, stopping distances may be:

options.text: Unchanged
Shortened
Tripled, with steering control reduced or lost

questions.correctOption: Tripled, with steering control reduced or lost
questions.explanation: You lose the traction needed both to steer and to brake at the same moment.

citations.quote: When hydroplaning occurs there is a loss of the traction needed to steer and brake safely. d. Stopping distances may be tripled and steering control may be reduced or lost.

questions.stem: Hydroplaning is:

options.text: Only a risk for heavy vehicles
More common at higher speeds, but possible at any speed
Impossible below 45 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: More common at higher speeds, but possible at any speed
questions.explanation: Worn tires and standing water can lift a car at surprisingly low speeds.

citations.quote: Hydroplaning is more common at higher speeds, although tires can hydroplane under certain conditions at ANY speed.

questions.stem: In fog or mist, you should never use high beams because:

options.text: The light is reflected back into your eyes
They drain the battery
They are illegal in Tennessee

questions.correctOption: The light is reflected back into your eyes
questions.explanation: Low beams put light on the road under the fog instead of bouncing it back at you.

citations.quote: In fog or mist, never put your headlights on high beam because the light will be reflected back into your eyes.

questions.stem: If you must drive in fog or smoke, the manual advises you to:

options.text: Follow the tail lights of the vehicle ahead closely
Reduce speed, stay to the right, be patient and avoid passing
Use high beams and maintain speed

questions.correctOption: Reduce speed, stay to the right, be patient and avoid passing
questions.explanation: It also says to keep the radio down so you can hear traffic, and to avoid crossing traffic unless you must.

citations.quote: Be patient! Stay to the right. Avoid passing.

questions.stem: Skids happen when:

options.text: The tires can no longer grip the road, usually because the driver is going too fast for conditions
The brakes are too new
The road is perfectly dry

questions.correctOption: The tires can no longer grip the road, usually because the driver is going too fast for conditions
questions.explanation: The manual is blunt about the cause: drivers travelling too fast for the conditions.

citations.quote: Skids are caused when the tires can no longer grip the road. Skids are caused by drivers traveling too fast for conditions.

questions.stem: As little as six to twelve inches of moving water may:

options.text: Improve braking by cooling the brakes
Cause you to lose control of your vehicle
Be safely driven through at speed

questions.correctOption: Cause you to lose control of your vehicle
questions.explanation: Two feet will carry most cars downstream. Turn around rather than test it.

citations.quote: As little as six to twelve inches of water may cause you to lose control of your vehicle and two feet of water will carry most cars downstream.

questions.stem: A driver who ignores visible flood warning signs or barricades and drives into a flooded road can be:

options.text: Given a written warning only
Ticketed for littering
Charged with reckless driving and made to pay the cost of the rescue

questions.correctOption: Charged with reckless driving and made to pay the cost of the rescue
questions.explanation: The rescue restitution is the part people forget — someone has to come and get you.

citations.quote: the driver can be charged with reckless driving. The driver can also be responsible for the restitution of funds for the cost of your rescue.

questions.stem: If your vehicle stalls in floodwater you should:

options.text: Leave it immediately and seek higher ground
Stay inside and wait for the water to drop
Try to restart the engine

questions.correctOption: Leave it immediately and seek higher ground
questions.explanation: Water rises faster than people expect and a stalled car floats sooner than they think.

citations.quote: NEVER drive through floodwaters or on flooded roads. If your vehicle stalls, leave it immediately and seek higher ground.

questions.stem: If you spot a tornado while driving you should:

options.text: Park under an overpass and stay in the vehicle
Get out of the car and lie face down in a ditch or low-lying area
Try to outrun it

questions.correctOption: Get out of the car and lie face down in a ditch or low-lying area
questions.explanation: A car is no shelter, and outrunning a tornado assumes you know where it is going.

citations.quote: If you spot a tornado, DON'T try to outrun it. Get out of the car, find shelter in a ditch or low-lying area and lie face down to protect yourself from flying debris.

questions.stem: In hail or sleet, the manual advises you to:

options.text: Find shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge
Drive faster to get through it
Pull into the left lane

questions.correctOption: Find shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge
questions.explanation: Shelter protects the glass, and hail on a windshield can take your visibility instantly.

citations.quote: Hailstorms/Sleet – find shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge.

questions.stem: The three big errors drivers make on snow and ice are to:

options.text: Use low gear, use the defroster and use snow tires
Over-power and spin the wheels, over-brake and slide, over-steer and skid
Drive too slowly, brake too gently, and steer too little

questions.correctOption: Over-power and spin the wheels, over-brake and slide, over-steer and skid
questions.explanation: Every one of them is an input that is too big for the grip available.

citations.quote: To over-power and spin the wheels • To over-brake and slide the wheels • To over-steer and skid the wheels

questions.stem: Before driving in winter conditions, you should:

options.text: Clear only the driver's side of the windshield
Rely on the defroster while driving
Clear snow, ice or frost from all windows

questions.correctOption: Clear snow, ice or frost from all windows
questions.explanation: A porthole in the frost is not a view of the road.

citations.quote: Clear snow, ice or frost from ALL windows before driving.

questions.stem: To gain more control of your vehicle in a strong wind you should:

options.text: Slow down
Speed up to reduce the time exposed
Steer with one hand to feel the gusts

questions.correctOption: Slow down
questions.explanation: And when a truck or bus passes you on the left, move as far right in your lane as you can and slow down.

citations.quote: a. To gain more control over vehicles in a strong wind, slow down.

questions.stem: If your vehicle begins to skid you should:

options.text: Accelerate through the skid
Stay off the brake and steer in the direction you want the car to go
Brake hard and hold the wheel straight

questions.correctOption: Stay off the brake and steer in the direction you want the car to go
questions.explanation: As the car straightens, be ready to correct back the other way — a skid usually tries to swing twice.

citations.quote: If your vehicle begins to skid: a. Stay off the brake. Until the vehicle slows, your brakes will not work and could cause you to skid more. b. Steer. Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want your car to go.

questions.stem: In a vehicle without anti-lock brakes that starts to skid, the general rule is to:

options.text: Take your foot off the brake and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid
Press the brake harder
Pull the parking brake

questions.correctOption: Take your foot off the brake and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid
questions.explanation: Locked wheels cannot steer. Releasing the brake gives the tires their grip back.

citations.quote: if the car starts to skid, take your foot off the brake and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid

questions.stem: If your wheels drop off the paved roadway you should:

options.text: Jerk the wheel back immediately
Brake hard and stop where you are
Not steer back onto the pavement until there are no cars in your immediate vicinity

questions.correctOption: Not steer back onto the pavement until there are no cars in your immediate vicinity
questions.explanation: Come off the gas, hold the wheel firmly, brake lightly, then come back onto the pavement when it is clear.

citations.quote: 5. Do NOT attempt to steer back onto the pavement until there are no cars in your immediate vicinity.

questions.stem: In avoiding a collision, a driver has three options:

options.text: Signal, stop, or reverse
Stop, turn, or speed up
Stop, brake, or coast

questions.correctOption: Stop, turn, or speed up
questions.explanation: Speeding up is a real option — sometimes the gap is in front of you, not behind.

citations.quote: In avoiding a collision, drivers have three options: 1. Stop 2. Turn 3. Speed Up

questions.stem: To stop quickly in a vehicle with anti-lock brakes you should:

options.text: Press the pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing firmly
Pump the pedal
Press and release repeatedly

questions.correctOption: Press the pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing firmly
questions.explanation: The pedal may buzz and push back. Do not let up — that is the system working.

citations.quote: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing on it firmly.

questions.stem: To stop quickly without anti-lock brakes you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as possible and hold
Use the parking brake
Brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels, releasing briefly if they lock

questions.correctOption: Brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels, releasing briefly if they lock
questions.explanation: If the wheels lock and the car starts to skid, ease off the pedal and press again once the skid stops.

citations.quote: Without ABS - If you must stop quickly and you do NOT have an antilock braking system: Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking them.
If the brakes lock-up, you will feel the vehicle start to skid. Quickly let up on the brake pedal.

questions.stem: With anti-lock brakes, the manual says the second thing you should do after stamping on the brake is:

options.text: Shift into neutral
Steer around the obstacle, because ABS leaves you steering
Take your hands off the wheel

questions.correctOption: Steer around the obstacle, because ABS leaves you steering
questions.explanation: The point of ABS is not a shorter stop — it is that you can still steer while stopping.

citations.quote: Use the nonskid feature of ABS to steer around the obstacle that made you slam the brakes on in the first place.

questions.stem: An ABS-equipped vehicle should be driven:

options.text: No more aggressively than a vehicle without ABS
Faster through curves, since it cannot skid
With abrupt lane changes to test the system

questions.correctOption: No more aggressively than a vehicle without ABS
questions.explanation: ABS shortens nothing about physics. It only keeps the wheels turning while you brake.

citations.quote: Never drive an ABS-equipped vehicle more aggressively than vehicle without ABS.

questions.stem: If a collision with a deer or other large animal seems inevitable, you should:

options.text: Swerve hard to miss it
Brake and steer into the shoulder
Not swerve — keep the vehicle under control and on the roadway

questions.correctOption: Not swerve — keep the vehicle under control and on the roadway
questions.explanation: Swerving is how a survivable animal strike becomes a head-on or a rollover.

citations.quote: If a collision seems inevitable, don't swerve to avoid the animal; your risk of personal injury may be greater if you do. Keep your vehicle under control and on the roadway when you hit the animal.

questions.stem: After hitting a large animal such as a deer or a farm animal you should:

options.text: Continue driving if the vehicle is undamaged
Report the crash to the police
Move the animal off the road yourself

questions.correctOption: Report the crash to the police
questions.explanation: It is a reportable event, and an injured animal in the road is a hazard for the next driver.

citations.quote: Report the crash to the police if it involves a large animal such as a deer or farm animal.

questions.stem: The manual warns that jerking the steering wheel suddenly in an emergency can:

options.text: Improve your chance of avoiding the obstacle
Trigger the air bag safely
Send you into another object or off the road, risking a rollover

questions.correctOption: Send you into another object or off the road, risking a rollover
questions.explanation: Steer normally around the problem. Freezing at the wheel and jerking it are the two failure modes.

citations.quote: People sometimes get hurt, or killed, when they jerk the steering wheel suddenly. This can cause them to run into another object or veer off the road risking a rollover.

questions.stem: Rumble stripes along the edge line exist to:

options.text: Improve wet-night visibility of the edge line, with vibration and noise as a secondary effect
Slow traffic in work zones
Mark the boundary of a passing zone

questions.correctOption: Improve wet-night visibility of the edge line, with vibration and noise as a secondary effect
questions.explanation: The indentations under the paint do double duty — they let water drain off the markings so the line stays visible on a wet night, and they make noise and vibration under a tyre.

citations.quote: It has a secondary effect of the vibration and noise, however, its primary function is to improve wet-night visibility of the edge line.

questions.stem: The manual defines defensive driving as:

options.text: Being constantly aware of driving conditions, planning ahead, anticipating dangers and taking the right action
Driving below the speed limit at all times
Staying in the right lane

questions.correctOption: Being constantly aware of driving conditions, planning ahead, anticipating dangers and taking the right action
questions.explanation: It is an active habit — anticipating other people's errors and having an answer ready.

citations.quote: "Defensive Driving" means being constantly aware of the driving conditions, planning ahead, anticipating dangers and taking the right action so as not to come in contact with any obstacle or other vehicle.

questions.stem: Which attitudes does the manual call the key to safe driving?

options.text: Confidence and speed
Assertiveness and quick reflexes
Courtesy and consideration toward others

questions.correctOption: Courtesy and consideration toward others
questions.explanation: Most conflicts on the road start with someone insisting on being right.

citations.quote: Courtesy and consideration toward others are the most important driving attitudes you can develop.

questions.stem: One of the manual's Drive Alert rules is to:

options.text: Rely on your horn to prevent conflicts
Expect the other driver to do the wrong thing and have a plan ready
Assume other drivers will follow the rules

questions.correctOption: Expect the other driver to do the wrong thing and have a plan ready
questions.explanation: Planning for the error costs you nothing when it does not happen and saves you when it does.

citations.quote: Expect the other driver to do the WRONG thing, and have a plan of action prepared to counter his error.

questions.stem: Defensive drivers try to focus their eyes how far ahead?

options.text: Two car lengths
One second
10 to 15 seconds, about one city block

questions.correctOption: 10 to 15 seconds, about one city block
questions.explanation: Looking far ahead turns sudden events into things you saw coming.

citations.quote: Defensive drivers try to focus their eyes 10 to 15 seconds (about the distance of 1 city block) ahead.

questions.stem: How often does the manual suggest checking the traffic behind you in the rearview mirror?

options.text: Only before braking
About every 10 seconds
Once a mile

questions.correctOption: About every 10 seconds
questions.explanation: It tells you early if someone is closing fast or tailgating — but keep each glance brief.

citations.quote: Use your rearview mirror to check the traffic behind you frequently, about every 10 seconds.

questions.stem: About what share of the information a driver gathers comes through the eyes?

options.text: 90 percent
50 percent
25 percent

questions.correctOption: 90 percent
questions.explanation: Which is why scanning — rather than a fixed stare — is the core defensive skill.

citations.quote: When driving, we gather 90% of the information about the road and our surroundings through our eyes.

questions.stem: When scanning the road, you should:

options.text: Fix your eyes on the vehicle ahead
Watch the road surface just in front of the hood
Keep your eyes moving and avoid a fixed stare

questions.correctOption: Keep your eyes moving and avoid a fixed stare
questions.explanation: A fixed stare narrows what you notice to almost nothing.

citations.quote: As you scan the road, avoid a fixed stare.

questions.stem: Which of these are the "clues" the manual tells you to watch for on other vehicles?

options.text: Bumper stickers and licence plates
The make and model of the car
Exhaust smoke, brake or back-up lights, and turned wheels

questions.correctOption: Exhaust smoke, brake or back-up lights, and turned wheels
questions.explanation: Each one says the vehicle may be about to move into your path.

citations.quote: Look for exhaust smoke, brake or back-up lights and turned wheels on vehicles.

questions.stem: In rural areas, defensive drivers should watch particularly for:

options.text: Bus lanes
Hidden intersections and driveways, curves, hills and changing road conditions
Traffic signals

questions.correctOption: Hidden intersections and driveways, curves, hills and changing road conditions
questions.explanation: Pavement that turns to gravel or a road that narrows can change your grip and your margin without warning.

citations.quote: Watch for hidden intersections and driveways, curves, hills and different road conditions

questions.stem: Staying out of another driver's blind spot:

options.text: Prevents them from turning into you
Is only necessary near large trucks
Matters only at night

questions.correctOption: Prevents them from turning into you
questions.explanation: If they cannot see you, their lane change is going to happen anyway.

citations.quote: Stay out of another driver's blind spot(s) to prevent another vehicle from turning into you.

questions.stem: The manual says human error is:

options.text: Only a factor in bad weather
The single most common cause of traffic crashes
A rare contributor to crashes

questions.correctOption: The single most common cause of traffic crashes
questions.explanation: Excessive speed, lack of concentration and improper evasive action are the leading factors it names.

citations.quote: Human error is the single most common cause of traffic crashes.

questions.stem: Approaching any intersection, the manual says to look:

options.text: Right first, because that traffic is closer
Straight ahead only
Left first, then right, then quickly left again

questions.correctOption: Left first, then right, then quickly left again
questions.explanation: Traffic from the left is nearer to your side of the road, so it gets the first and the last look.

citations.quote: Check Left to Right Before Entering an Intersection - At any intersection, look to the left first, since cars coming from the left will be closer to you. Then look to the right and take one more quick look to the left before you drive through.

questions.stem: When you are stopped at a red light or waiting to turn, you should:

options.text: Stop with the front wheels on the crosswalk line
Move into the crosswalk to see better
Not block the crosswalk or stop with part of your vehicle over it

questions.correctOption: Not block the crosswalk or stop with part of your vehicle over it
questions.explanation: A car in the crosswalk forces people on foot out into the traffic lane to get around it.

citations.quote: Drivers should not block the crosswalk when stopped at a red light or waiting to make a turn. You also should not stop with a portion of your vehicle over the crosswalk area.

questions.stem: Even when you have the legal right-of-way, you should not:

options.text: Signal your intentions
Honk, rev your engine or do anything to rush or scare a pedestrian in front of your car
Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing

questions.correctOption: Honk, rev your engine or do anything to rush or scare a pedestrian in front of your car
questions.explanation: Startling someone in the middle of the road is how they end up in front of the next car.

citations.quote: Don't honk your horn, rev up your engine or do anything to rush or scare a pedestrian in front of your car, even if you have the legal right-of-way.

questions.stem: On most roadways, bicyclists:

options.text: Have the same rights and responsibilities as other roadway users
Have no legal right to the roadway
May use only the sidewalk

questions.correctOption: Have the same rights and responsibilities as other roadway users
questions.explanation: They are prohibited from limited-access highways and expressways, but elsewhere they are traffic like anyone else.

citations.quote: On most roadways, bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other roadway users and in most cases, they must share the lane. Bicyclists are prohibited on limited-access highways, expressways and certain other marked roadways.

questions.stem: Bicyclists are required to travel:

options.text: In the center of the lane at all times
On the right-hand side of the road, in the same direction as vehicles
Facing oncoming traffic

questions.correctOption: On the right-hand side of the road, in the same direction as vehicles
questions.explanation: As close to the right as is practical, while still avoiding drains, debris and car doors.

citations.quote: Bicyclists are required to travel on the right hand side of the road and travel in the same direction as vehicles. They must ride as close to the right side of the road as practical, while avoiding road hazards

questions.stem: A lane marked and signed for bicycle use only must never be used by drivers:

options.text: As a turning lane, a passing lane, or for parking
To cross into a driveway
In an emergency

questions.correctOption: As a turning lane, a passing lane, or for parking
questions.explanation: Those three uses are precisely what the marking exists to prevent.

citations.quote: If the lane is marked and signed (as shown at right) for bicycle use only, drivers must NEVER use this lane as a turning lane, passing lane or for parking.

questions.stem: When the lane is too narrow for a car and a bicycle to share safely, the safest thing is to:

options.text: Squeeze past within the lane
Sound your horn until the cyclist moves over
Let the bicycle take the full lane

questions.correctOption: Let the bicycle take the full lane
questions.explanation: A cyclist may also need the full lane to overtake another vehicle or to get around a hazard in the road.

citations.quote: The lane is too narrow for both a vehicle and a bicycle to safely share the lane. In this case it is safest to let the bicycle take the full lane.

questions.stem: Tennessee law requires a bicycle used at night to have:

options.text: Reflective clothing instead of lights
A white front lamp visible at 500 feet and a red rear reflector or lamp visible at 500 feet
Only a rear reflector

questions.correctOption: A white front lamp visible at 500 feet and a red rear reflector or lamp visible at 500 feet
questions.explanation: Front lamp, rear reflector or lamp — the same 500-foot standard both ways.

citations.quote: Tennessee law requires that a bicycle used at night must be equipped with a lamp on the front that emits a white light visible from a distance of at least 500 feet to the front and either a red reflector or lamp emitting a red light that is visible from distance of 500 feet to the rear

questions.stem: A bicyclist signaling a left turn:

options.text: Extends the left arm bent upward at the elbow
Points the left arm downward
Extends the left arm out sideways

questions.correctOption: Extends the left arm out sideways
questions.explanation: Arm out sideways is left; bent up at the elbow is right; bent down is stopping or slowing.

citations.quote: Left Turn Extend your left arm out sideways with all fingers extended or use your index finger to point left.

questions.stem: A bicyclist with the left arm bent 90 degrees at the elbow, hand pointing down and palm back, is signaling:

options.text: A right turn
Stopping or slowing
A left turn

questions.correctOption: Stopping or slowing
questions.explanation: Hand down means slowing. Hand up in the same bent position means a right turn.

citations.quote: Stopping or Slowing Extend your left arm or right arm sideways and bend your arm at a 90-degree angle at the elbow joint, hand pointing downwards and the palm of your hand facing backwards.

questions.stem: You are turning left and a bicyclist is entering the intersection from the opposite direction. You should:

options.text: Turn quickly in front of the bicyclist
Sound your horn and turn
Wait for the bicyclist to pass before turning

questions.correctOption: Wait for the bicyclist to pass before turning
questions.explanation: Bicycles are easy to under-estimate for both speed and distance. Let them through.

citations.quote: When your vehicle is turning left and there is a bicyclist entering the intersection from the opposite direction, you should wait for the bicyclist to pass before making the turn.

questions.stem: You are turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on your right. You should:

options.text: Let the bicyclist go through the intersection first
Turn ahead of them to clear the lane
Stop in the bike lane to block them

questions.correctOption: Let the bicyclist go through the intersection first
questions.explanation: Turning across a cyclist who is going straight is one of the most common ways they are hit.

citations.quote: If your vehicle is turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on the right, let the bicyclist go through the intersection first before making a right turn.

questions.stem: A bicyclist with a red or orange pennant flag on an antenna is commonly indicating:

options.text: The rider is a child
The rider has impaired hearing
The bicycle is for sale

questions.correctOption: The rider has impaired hearing
questions.explanation: They may not hear you coming, so slow down and give them room.

citations.quote: If you see a bicyclist with a red or orange pennant flag on the antennae attached to the bike, slow down: this is a common symbol to indicate the rider has impaired hearing.

questions.stem: At night, when you see an oncoming bicycle rider you should:

options.text: Flash your high beams as a warning
Leave your high beams on so you can see them
Not use your high beams

questions.correctOption: Not use your high beams
questions.explanation: A dazzled cyclist cannot see the pothole or the gravel that puts them under your wheels.

citations.quote: At night, do not use high beams when you see an oncoming bicycle rider.

questions.stem: Where there are no sidewalks, pedestrians should walk:

options.text: On the left side of the road, facing traffic, in single file
On the right side, with traffic
In the middle of the road

questions.correctOption: On the left side of the road, facing traffic, in single file
questions.explanation: Facing traffic means you can see what is coming and step clear of it.

citations.quote: When there are no sidewalks, always walk on the left side of the road facing traffic
Two or more pedestrians should walk in single file and never side by side of each other.

questions.stem: Where sidewalks are available, it is:

options.text: Lawful to walk in the road at night only
Unlawful for pedestrians to walk in the road
A matter of personal preference

questions.correctOption: Unlawful for pedestrians to walk in the road
questions.explanation: The sidewalk is the pedestrian's lane; the roadway is not.

citations.quote: Pedestrians must walk along sidewalks when available. It is unlawful for pedestrians to walk in the road where there are sidewalks.

questions.stem: Pedestrians must not:

options.text: Cross at an unmarked intersection
Use a crosswalk without a signal
Suddenly leave a curb and walk into the path of traffic that is close enough to be an immediate hazard

questions.correctOption: Suddenly leave a curb and walk into the path of traffic that is close enough to be an immediate hazard
questions.explanation: The right-of-way does not create stopping distance. Even a driver who is watching needs time.

citations.quote: pedestrians must not suddenly leave a curb or other safe waiting place and walk into the path of vehicle traffic if it so close that it is an immediate hazard.

questions.stem: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: Half a lane, shared with a car
The shoulder only
The use of a full lane

questions.correctOption: The use of a full lane
questions.explanation: Never try to share a lane with a motorcycle — the rider needs the whole width to swerve around road hazards.

citations.quote: Motorcycles have the right to the use of the full lane
You must never try to share a lane with a motorcycle, and you should always respect the cycle's space and position in traffic.

questions.stem: Following a motorcycle, you should allow at least:

options.text: A two-second following distance
One car length
A half-second gap

questions.correctOption: A two-second following distance
questions.explanation: Two seconds at minimum, and four in poor conditions — a motorcycle can stop far shorter than a car.

citations.quote: Following Distance - Allow at least a two-second following distance, so the motorcycle rider has enough time to maneuver or stop in an emergency.

questions.stem: A motorcyclist must never:

options.text: Ride two abreast in a lane
Ride between lanes in traffic or share a lane with another vehicle
Use the full lane

questions.correctOption: Ride between lanes in traffic or share a lane with another vehicle
questions.explanation: Riding between lanes is prohibited, and it puts the rider in exactly the space drivers do not check.

citations.quote: Never ride in between lanes in traffic or share a lane with another vehicle.

questions.stem: The simplest test of whether a truck driver can see you is:

options.text: If you cannot see the driver in the truck's mirror, the driver cannot see you
If you can see the trailer, you are visible
If your headlights are on, you are visible

questions.correctOption: If you cannot see the driver in the truck's mirror, the driver cannot see you
questions.explanation: Trucks have No-Zones at the front, the sides and a long way behind.

citations.quote: if you can't see the truck driver in the truck's mirror, the truck driver can't see you.

questions.stem: The No-Zone directly in front of a large vehicle extends approximately:

options.text: Two feet
Up to 20 feet
Up to 200 feet

questions.correctOption: Up to 20 feet
questions.explanation: Cutting in and braking inside those 20 feet leaves the truck no chance at all.

citations.quote: The area approximately up to 20 feet directly in front of a large vehicle is considered a NO-ZONE.

questions.stem: A truck's rear blind spot extends back about:

options.text: 20 feet
1,000 feet
200 feet

questions.correctOption: 200 feet
questions.explanation: Sit inside it and the driver has no idea you are there — and you cannot see around the trailer either.

citations.quote: A truck's blind spots are immediate in front, on either side of the car and up to 200 feet in the rear.

questions.stem: After passing a large truck, you should not pull back in front of it until:

options.text: You can see the whole front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror
You have cleared its front bumper
The truck signals you

questions.correctOption: You can see the whole front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: A loaded truck needs far more distance to stop than you do, and it cannot make up the gap you just took.

citations.quote: do NOT pull back over into the lane in front of the truck unless you can see the whole front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.stem: If a truck or bus driver blinks their headlights after you pass, it means:

options.text: They want you to slow down
There is a police officer ahead
You are clear to pull back in front of them

questions.correctOption: You are clear to pull back in front of them
questions.explanation: It is a courtesy signal — the driver can see your whole vehicle and is telling you so.

citations.quote: If the truck or bus driver blink their vehicle headlights after you pass, it's a signal that you are cleared to pull back in front of their vehicle.

questions.stem: Runaway truck ramps:

options.text: Must never be used for stopping or parking
Are rest areas for trucks
May be used by cars in an emergency

questions.correctOption: Must never be used for stopping or parking
questions.explanation: They exist for a truck that has lost its brakes on a long downgrade, and it will arrive at speed.

citations.quote: Runaway Truck Ramps: These ramps are designed to stop out-of-control trucks or buses going down step downgrades. Vehicles should never stop or park in these areas.

questions.stem: Near a commercial vehicle weigh station, you should:

options.text: Speed up to clear the area
Move into the right lane to keep the left clear
Avoid driving in the right lane so trucks can merge back on

questions.correctOption: Avoid driving in the right lane so trucks can merge back on
questions.explanation: Trucks rejoining traffic from a standstill need a long, clear run.

citations.quote: When you are near a Commercial Vehicle Weigh Station, avoid driving in the right lane so slow-moving trucks can easily merge back onto the roadway.

questions.stem: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

options.text: A red square
A fluorescent or reflective orange triangle displayed on the rear
A round yellow disc

questions.correctOption: A fluorescent or reflective orange triangle displayed on the rear
questions.explanation: It is required on animal-drawn vehicles and most farm and construction equipment, and it means the vehicle is doing well under the limit.

citations.quote: The "slow moving vehicle" emblem, a fluorescent or reflective orange triangle, must be displayed on the rear of vehicles drawn by animals, and most farm vehicles and construction equipment.

questions.stem: Farm machinery preparing to turn right may first:

options.text: Pull wide to the left, then turn right
Signal with a horn
Stop completely for one minute

questions.correctOption: Pull wide to the left, then turn right
questions.explanation: Most farm machinery has no turn signals at all, so never assume a wide swing left means it is turning left.

citations.quote: Farm machinery usually does not have turn signals and to make a right turn, operators of farm machinery may first pull wide to the left, then turn to the right.

questions.stem: Animal-drawn vehicles on the road:

options.text: Must yield to all motor vehicles
May not use public roads
Have the same rights as motor vehicles and must follow the same rules

questions.correctOption: Have the same rights as motor vehicles and must follow the same rules
questions.explanation: Warning signs are posted in areas where you are likely to meet them.

citations.quote: They have the same rights to use the road as a motor vehicle and must follow the same rules of the road.

questions.stem: Approaching a horse being ridden or led along the road, the law requires you to:

options.text: Pass as quickly as possible
Drive at a reasonable speed and distance, and not sound your horn or rev your engine
Sound your horn to warn the rider

questions.correctOption: Drive at a reasonable speed and distance, and not sound your horn or rev your engine
questions.explanation: Noise is what makes a horse bolt, and a bolting horse ends up in the road with you.

citations.quote: You must drive at a reasonable speed, and at a reasonable distance away from the horse. Do NOT sound your horn or "rev" your engine loudly when approaching or passing a horse.

questions.stem: Children waiting at a school bus stop should stay:

options.text: Ten feet away from the bus and never go behind it
Directly beside the bus door
Behind the bus, where the driver can see them

questions.correctOption: Ten feet away from the bus and never go behind it
questions.explanation: The area right around a bus is where the driver cannot see, and behind it is the worst of all.

citations.quote: Children should stay ten feet away from the school bus and NEVER go behind the bus.

questions.stem: Trucks making a right turn often leave an open space on the right. That space is:

options.text: A lane you may use
A safe place to wait
The truck's turning room — do not move into it or try to pass

questions.correctOption: The truck's turning room — do not move into it or try to pass
questions.explanation: The trailer sweeps through that space as the turn tightens.

citations.quote: Trucks make wide right turns and often must leave an open space on the right side. Do NOT move into that space or try to pass a truck if it might be making a right turn.

questions.stem: If a tractor has a long hood, the driver may not be able to see:

options.text: The road more than 100 feet ahead
The first 10 to 20 feet in front of the bumper
Anything in the left mirror

questions.correctOption: The first 10 to 20 feet in front of the bumper
questions.explanation: A car sitting in that space at a red light is invisible from the cab.

citations.quote: If the tractor has a long hood, the trucker may not be able to see the first 10-20 feet in front of the bumper

questions.stem: Red is used as a background color only for:

options.text: Any sign carrying a prohibition
Warning signs on curves
Stop signs, ALL WAY and FOUR-WAY plates, DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and interstate route markers

questions.correctOption: Stop signs, ALL WAY and FOUR-WAY plates, DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and interstate route markers
questions.explanation: Red is reserved. Most prohibition signs are white with a red circle and slash, not a red background.

citations.quote: RED is used only as a background color for STOP signs, multiple supplemental plates (FOUR-WAY or ALL WAY), DO-NOT-ENTER messages, WRONG WAY signs and on Interstate route markers.

questions.stem: Orange is used as a background color for:

options.text: Construction and maintenance signs, and nothing else
School zones
Motorist services

questions.correctOption: Construction and maintenance signs, and nothing else
questions.explanation: Orange always means road work. The manual says it shall not be used for any other purpose.

citations.quote: ORANGE is used as a background color for construction and maintenance signs and shall not be used for any other purpose.

questions.stem: Yellow is used as a background color for:

options.text: Regulatory signs
Warning signs, except where orange is specified, and school signs
Guide signs

questions.correctOption: Warning signs, except where orange is specified, and school signs
questions.explanation: Yellow is the general warning color; orange takes over inside work zones.

citations.quote: YELLOW is used as a background color for warning signs, except where orange is specified, and for school signs.

questions.stem: A brown background on a sign means the information relates to:

options.text: Points of recreational or cultural interest
Emergency services
Road construction

questions.correctOption: Points of recreational or cultural interest
questions.explanation: Parks, historic sites and campgrounds get brown; ordinary destinations get green.

citations.quote: BROWN is used as a background color for guide information signs related to points of recreational cultural interest.

questions.stem: Blue backgrounds are used for signs about:

options.text: Sharp curves
Motorist services, including police services and rest areas
Speed limits

questions.correctOption: Motorist services, including police services and rest areas
questions.explanation: Blue means services — fuel, food, lodging, hospitals, rest areas — and the Emergency Route Marker.

citations.quote: BLUE is used as a background color for information signs related to motorist services (including police services and rest areas) and the Emergency Route Marker.

questions.stem: Fluorescent yellow-green is the color used for:

options.text: Interstate exits
Work zones
School zones and other pedestrian areas such as crosswalks

questions.correctOption: School zones and other pedestrian areas such as crosswalks
questions.explanation: It reads much better in low light and rain, which is exactly where children and pedestrians are hardest to see.

citations.quote: FLUORESCENT YELLOW-GREEN is now in use for signage in school zones and other pedestrian traffic areas such as crosswalks.
FLUORESCENT YELLOW-GREEN IS THE COLOR FOR SCHOOL ZONES!

questions.stem: Fluorescent pink signage is used for:

options.text: Incident management — crashes, wildland fires, floods and hazardous material spills
School crossings
Permanent detours

questions.correctOption: Incident management — crashes, wildland fires, floods and hazardous material spills
questions.explanation: Pink marks a temporary emergency scene, not planned road work.

citations.quote: FLUORESCENT PINK (sometimes called "coral") is used for incident management traffic control signage when needed for incidents such as traffic accidents, wildland fires, floods, and hazardous material spills

questions.stem: The only eight-sided sign on the roadway is:

options.text: The stop sign
The yield sign
The railroad advance warning sign

questions.correctOption: The stop sign
questions.explanation: The shape alone identifies it, which matters when the face is dirty, snow-covered or backlit.

citations.quote: Octagon Shape - Stop This sign is the only eight-sided sign on the roadway.

questions.stem: A diamond-shaped sign tells you:

options.text: You are approaching a service area
There is a hazardous or unexpected condition ahead
A law or regulation applies

questions.correctOption: There is a hazardous or unexpected condition ahead
questions.explanation: Diamonds call for caution and usually a slower speed.

citations.quote: Diamond Shape — Hazardous Or Unexpected Condition Ahead These signs call for caution and usually for a slower speed.

questions.stem: A rectangular sign generally carries:

options.text: A warning about the road surface
A railroad crossing
Special laws, regulations or important information

questions.correctOption: Special laws, regulations or important information
questions.explanation: Speed limits, parking rules and many guide signs are rectangles.

citations.quote: Rectangular Shape - Special Laws, Regulations or Important Information, Some Guide Signs

questions.stem: A round sign on the roadside always means:

options.text: A rest area is ahead
A railroad grade crossing is ahead
A roundabout is ahead

questions.correctOption: A railroad grade crossing is ahead
questions.explanation: The yellow disc is the railroad advance warning: slow down and be ready to stop.

citations.quote: This circular sign always means that you are approaching a railroad grade crossing. You must slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.stem: Drivers must obey directions from a law enforcement officer, construction worker or school crossing guard:

options.text: Even when those directions differ from what the lights and signs indicate
Only when the signals agree with them
Only inside a work zone

questions.correctOption: Even when those directions differ from what the lights and signs indicate
