questions.explanation: A person directing traffic outranks the signal. They can see the reason the signal cannot.

citations.quote: Drivers must obey directions from these individuals, even if the directions are different than what the traffic lights and signs indicate.

questions.stem: A white sign with a red circle and a diagonal line through it means:

options.text: A warning about the symbol shown
A service related to the symbol shown
"No" — according to whatever symbol is shown behind it

questions.correctOption: "No" — according to whatever symbol is shown behind it
questions.explanation: One convention covers a dozen signs: no left turn, no U-turn, no trucks, no bicycles, no hitchhiking.

citations.quote: Signs having a white background and a red circle and a line diagonally through them mean "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.

questions.stem: An ALL WAY plate below a stop sign means:

options.text: All traffic approaching the intersection must stop
Only your direction must stop
Traffic may proceed without stopping when clear

questions.correctOption: All traffic approaching the intersection must stop
questions.explanation: It changes how you read the intersection: everyone stops, and order of arrival decides who goes.

citations.quote: ALL WAY: Red Rectangle –Added below a stop sign. It means all traffic approaching this intersection must stop.

questions.stem: The three-sided yield sign means:

options.text: You have the right-of-way over the other roadway
Slow down, enter with caution, and stop and wait when other vehicles are approaching
Always come to a complete stop

questions.correctOption: Slow down, enter with caution, and stop and wait when other vehicles are approaching
questions.explanation: The manual adds a plain instruction: always stop when traffic is heavy.

citations.quote: This three-sided sign means that you are approaching an intersection and must stop and wait when other vehicles are approaching from the right or left on the other roadway. If you are sure no other cars are coming you need not come to a complete stop but you must slow down and enter the intersection with caution. Always stop when traffic is heavy.

questions.stem: The KEEP RIGHT / SLOWER TRAFFIC sign on a multi-lane highway means you must:

options.text: Drive in the center lane
Straddle the lane line while passing
Drive in the extreme right lane unless passing or turning left

questions.correctOption: Drive in the extreme right lane unless passing or turning left
questions.explanation: The manual is explicit that you should never straddle lanes or sit in a center lane while moving slower than traffic.

citations.quote: It means that you must drive in the extreme right lane unless you want to pass a slower moving car or make a left turn.

questions.stem: No-passing signs mark passing restrictions that are based on:

options.text: How far ahead you can see
The posted speed limit
The width of the shoulder

questions.correctOption: How far ahead you can see
questions.explanation: Passing zones account for hills, curves, intersections and driveways — anywhere a vehicle could appear.

citations.quote: These signs tell you where passing is not permitted. Passing areas are based on how far you can see ahead.

questions.stem: The triangular NO PASSING ZONE sign is:

options.text: Blue and mounted overhead
Yellow or orange and placed on the left side of the roadway
Red and placed on the right

questions.correctOption: Yellow or orange and placed on the left side of the roadway
questions.explanation: Left side, pennant shaped — it is aimed at the driver who is thinking about pulling out.

citations.quote: A triangular No Passing Zone sign can also be used. These signs are yellow or orange and placed on the left side of the roadway.

questions.stem: A High Occupancy Vehicle sign indicates lanes reserved for:

options.text: Commercial vehicles only
Vehicles travelling above the speed limit
Buses and vehicles carrying at least the number of occupants shown on the sign

questions.correctOption: Buses and vehicles carrying at least the number of occupants shown on the sign
questions.explanation: The sign also carries the hours during which the restriction applies.

citations.quote: This sign (High Occupancy Vehicle) indicates lanes reserved for buses and vehicles with the minimum number of occupants specified on the sign.

questions.stem: The one-way sign on the approach to a street tells you:

options.text: Traffic may flow either way at off-peak times
The street ahead is closed
You must not enter from the direction you are traveling

questions.correctOption: You must not enter from the direction you are traveling
questions.explanation: Red DO NOT ENTER and WRONG WAY signs are the last warnings if you miss it.

citations.quote: This sign tells you that you are approaching a one-way street and that you must not enter from the direction you are traveling.

questions.stem: A blue sign with the international symbol of access marks a parking space that:

options.text: Is reserved for vehicles displaying a disabled plate or placard
Is reserved for hospital staff
Is free of charge for anyone

questions.correctOption: Is reserved for vehicles displaying a disabled plate or placard
questions.explanation: Using one without the plate or placard is a misdemeanor, and the vehicle may be towed.

citations.quote: Parking spaces displaying this blue sign are reserved for vehicles bearing disabled veteran or handicapped license plates, or a special handicapped decal.
The use of reserved handicapped spaces by others is prohibited by law.

questions.stem: The NO HITCHHIKING sign reflects that in Tennessee it is illegal to:

options.text: Give a ride to a stranger
Park on the shoulder
Stand on a roadway to solicit a ride

questions.correctOption: Stand on a roadway to solicit a ride
questions.explanation: The offense belongs to the person on foot, but the manual notes the risk runs both ways.

citations.quote: In Tennessee, it is illegal to stand on a roadway to solicit a ride.

questions.stem: Speed control signs show:

options.text: Advisory speeds for curves
The maximum speed allowed, the minimum speed required, or a change in the speed limit
Only the maximum speed

questions.correctOption: The maximum speed allowed, the minimum speed required, or a change in the speed limit
questions.explanation: Advisory speeds for curves come on a yellow plaque below a warning sign, not on a regulatory speed sign.

citations.quote: These signs show the maximum speed allowed, the minimum speed required or a change in speed limit.

questions.stem: A turn sign (a yellow diamond with a sharp bend) is used where the recommended speed is:

options.text: Between 30 and 55 m.p.h.
Above 55 m.p.h.
30 m.p.h. or less

questions.correctOption: 30 m.p.h. or less
questions.explanation: The gentler curve sign covers 30 to 55. The sharper the symbol, the slower the corner.

citations.quote: The turn sign is used to mark turns with a recommended speed of 30 m.p.h. or less.

questions.stem: The curve sign marks curves with recommended speeds:

options.text: Under 15 m.p.h.
Over 65 m.p.h.
Between 30 and 55 m.p.h.

questions.correctOption: Between 30 and 55 m.p.h.
questions.explanation: An advisory speed plaque below it gives the specific number when one is posted.

citations.quote: The curve sign is used to mark curves with recommended speeds in the range between 30 and 55 m.p.h.

questions.stem: The reverse turn sign warns of two turns in opposite directions that are:

options.text: Separated by a traffic signal
Less than 600 feet apart
More than a mile apart

questions.correctOption: Less than 600 feet apart
questions.explanation: There is no room to build speed between them, so take the first one at a speed that sets up the second.

citations.quote: The reverse turn sign is used to mark two turns in opposite directions that are less than 600 feet apart.

questions.stem: The advisory speed plate mounted below a warning sign gives:

options.text: The minimum speed
The recommended maximum safe speed for the condition ahead
The legal speed limit

questions.correctOption: The recommended maximum safe speed for the condition ahead
questions.explanation: It is advice, but the advice is calculated for the geometry ahead.

citations.quote: It gives you the recommended maximum safe speed.

questions.stem: The falling rocks sign warns of:

options.text: Rocks that may be lying in the road
Rocks that may strike your vehicle from above
Loose gravel on the shoulder

questions.correctOption: Rocks that may be lying in the road
questions.explanation: The manual's advice is blunt: watch the roadway, not the hill.

citations.quote: This sign warns of rocks that may be in the road, not of rocks which may strike you from overhead. Watch the roadway, not the hill.

questions.stem: A yellow diamond showing a stop sign symbol means:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead that you cannot see yet — start slowing down
You may stop here if you wish
Stop immediately

questions.correctOption: There is a stop sign ahead that you cannot see yet — start slowing down
questions.explanation: It exists for stop signs hidden by a curve, a crest or foliage.

citations.quote: This sign indicates that there is a STOP sign just ahead that you cannot yet see. At this point, start to slow down.

questions.stem: The merging traffic sign alerts you to:

options.text: A lane closing ahead of you
A merge you must make yourself
Traffic blending into your stream of travel, so you should move over if you can

questions.correctOption: Traffic blending into your stream of travel, so you should move over if you can
questions.explanation: Check behind first, then leave the merging driver a clear path.

citations.quote: This sign alerts you to the possibility of traffic blending into the main stream of travel.

questions.stem: A lane-ends sign means you should:

options.text: Speed up to get ahead of traffic
Merge in the direction shown, signaling your intentions
Stop and wait for a gap

questions.correctOption: Merge in the direction shown, signaling your intentions
questions.explanation: Merging early is safer and legal; being a last-chance merger can get you ticketed in a work zone.

citations.quote: This sign is warning of the lane ending and that drivers should merge left. Be sure to signal your intentions.

questions.stem: The narrow bridge sign tells you:

options.text: The bridge is narrow and may require passing vehicles to reduce speed
The bridge is closed to trucks
The bridge ices before the road

questions.correctOption: The bridge is narrow and may require passing vehicles to reduce speed
questions.explanation: Two vehicles meeting on a narrow bridge have no shoulder and no escape route.

citations.quote: This sign tells you that the bridge is narrow and may require passing cars to reduce speeds.

questions.stem: A yellow diamond near a school warns you to:

options.text: Stop at the school entrance
Sound your horn
Slow down, drive with caution and watch for children

questions.correctOption: Slow down, drive with caution and watch for children
questions.explanation: It is placed on the approach to the school, before the zone itself.

citations.quote: It warns you to slow down, drive with caution and watch for children.

questions.stem: The school bus stop ahead sign means:

options.text: Children are likely to be in the area with a bus loading and unloading during the school season
A bus stop shelter is ahead
School buses are prohibited beyond this point

questions.correctOption: Children are likely to be in the area with a bus loading and unloading during the school season
questions.explanation: The sign stays up year round; the children only appear in term time, which is when drivers stop expecting them.

citations.quote: This sign indicates that children are likely to be in the area with a school bus loading and unloading during the school season.

questions.stem: A T-INTERSECTION sign means:

options.text: You must turn right or left, and be prepared to yield
A side road joins from the right
The road ahead narrows

questions.correctOption: You must turn right or left, and be prepared to yield
questions.explanation: Your road ends. Traffic on the through road has the right-of-way in both directions.

citations.quote: You must turn right or left. Be prepared to yield.

questions.stem: Chevron signs are used to:

options.text: Show the distance to the next exit
Give extra emphasis and guidance for a change in horizontal alignment
Mark the end of a work zone

questions.correctOption: Give extra emphasis and guidance for a change in horizontal alignment
questions.explanation: A line of them traces the curve so you can see where the road goes at night.

citations.quote: These Chevron signs displayed below are used to provide additional emphasis and guidance for a change in horizontal alignment.

questions.stem: A LOW CLEARANCE sign shows:

options.text: The weight limit of the bridge
The distance from the road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass
The width of the lane ahead

questions.correctOption: The distance from the road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass
questions.explanation: It matters to anyone driving a truck, an RV or anything with something on the roof.

citations.quote: Shows the distance from road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass

questions.stem: Object markers warn you of:

options.text: Objects lying in the travel lane
The end of the pavement
Objects near the edge of the road, such as bridge ends and underpass abutments

questions.correctOption: Objects near the edge of the road, such as bridge ends and underpass abutments
questions.explanation: They mark hazards that are not in the roadway but are close enough to hit.

citations.quote: These markers warn you of objects, not actually in the roadway, but so close to the edge of the road that need marking.

questions.stem: Work area signs are:

options.text: Blue with white symbols
Diamond or rectangular, orange with black letters or symbols
Yellow with red letters

questions.correctOption: Diamond or rectangular, orange with black letters or symbols
questions.explanation: They warn that people are working on or near the roadway.

citations.quote: These construction, maintenance or emergency operations signs are generally diamond or rectangular shaped, orange with black letters or symbols and warn you that people are working on or near the roadway.

questions.stem: In a work area, a person holding a sign or flag:

options.text: Has authority only when a police officer is present
May control traffic, and you must obey their directions
May only advise, not direct

questions.correctOption: May control traffic, and you must obey their directions
questions.explanation: Flaggers use paddles reading STOP on one side and SLOW on the other, and red flags in emergencies.

citations.quote: In work areas, a person with a sign or flag may control traffic. You must obey the directions of these persons.

questions.stem: A flashing arrow panel in a work zone tells you to:

options.text: Begin merging into the remaining open lanes well in advance of the sign
Stop until the panel goes dark
Move onto the shoulder

questions.correctOption: Begin merging into the remaining open lanes well in advance of the sign
questions.explanation: Merging early keeps the queue moving; merging at the cones is how the queue turns into a crash.

citations.quote: Flashing arrow panels alert approaching drivers of lane closures. You must begin to merge into the remaining open lane(s) well in advance of this sign.

questions.stem: Driving among barricades, drums and cones in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed
Straddle the lane line for extra room
Change lanes whenever you find a gap

questions.correctOption: Keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane on the way out too — do not change lanes until you are completely clear of the zone.

citations.quote: When driving near these devices, keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed limit. As you leave the work zone, stay in your lane and maintain your speed. Don't change lanes until you are completely clear of the work zone.

questions.stem: The color orange on a roadway sign always means:

options.text: School zone
Emergency incident
Road work — slow down

questions.correctOption: Road work — slow down
questions.explanation: Every temporary sign in a work zone is orange with black legend.

citations.quote: Watch for the color orange
All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background and black letters or symbols.

questions.stem: A sign reading "Road Work 1500 Feet" means you will be in that construction zone in about:

options.text: Two minutes
Half a mile of driving
17 seconds

questions.correctOption: 17 seconds
questions.explanation: The manual uses the figure to make the point that a work zone arrives far faster than it feels.

citations.quote: If you see a sign that says "Road Work 1500 Feet", you'll be in that construction zone in 17 seconds!

questions.stem: You should keep observing work zone signs until you see:

options.text: A police vehicle
The END ROAD WORK sign
The first orange cone

questions.correctOption: The END ROAD WORK sign
questions.explanation: The zone is not over when the workers disappear from view — it is over at the sign.

citations.quote: Observe the posted signs until you see the one that says "End Road Work".

questions.stem: Before entering a work zone you should:

options.text: Switch to high beams
Turn on your headlights
Turn on your hazard flashers

questions.correctOption: Turn on your headlights
questions.explanation: Headlights make you visible to the workers on foot and to the traffic weaving around you.

citations.quote: Turn your lights on before you enter the zone! Turn on your vehicle's headlights to become more visible to workers and other motorists.

questions.stem: Inside a work zone you should change lanes:

options.text: Only when instructed to do so
Whenever the next lane is moving faster
Whenever a gap appears

questions.correctOption: Only when instructed to do so
questions.explanation: Lane positions are set by the traffic control plan; freelancing inside the zone is what causes the sideswipes.

citations.quote: Follow their signals, and don't change lanes within the work zone unless instructed to do so.

questions.stem: Flaggers, utility workers and other personnel directing traffic in work zones can be seen wearing:

options.text: Fluorescent yellow-green clothing, vests and hard hats
Plain white overalls
Blue reflective jackets

questions.correctOption: Fluorescent yellow-green clothing, vests and hard hats
questions.explanation: Law enforcement officers wear the same fluorescent yellow-green at traffic emergencies.

citations.quote: can also be seen wearing FLUORESCENT YELLOW-GREEN clothing, vests and hard helmets in these construction work zones

questions.stem: Electronic message and arrow signs in work zones are used to:

options.text: Show the current time and temperature only
Give advance warning of construction zones, traffic directions, closures and weather hazards
Display advertising

questions.correctOption: Give advance warning of construction zones, traffic directions, closures and weather hazards
questions.explanation: They are mobile, so they appear exactly where the hazard is on that day.

citations.quote: These are mobile devices that are often used on some roads to give advance warning of construction zones, special traffic directions, road closures or in some cases weather hazards.

questions.stem: The round yellow sign with a black X and two Rs means:

options.text: A crossing is closed ahead
Trains have stopped running on this line
You are approaching a railroad grade crossing — slow down and be ready to stop

questions.correctOption: You are approaching a railroad grade crossing — slow down and be ready to stop
questions.explanation: It is an advance warning: it is up to you to stop if a train is coming.

citations.quote: This circular sign always means that you are approaching a railroad grade crossing. You must slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.stem: The crossbuck sign:

options.text: Marks the end of the railroad property
Is only used where there are no gates
Is placed at all railroad grade crossings and shows exactly where the tracks are

questions.correctOption: Is placed at all railroad grade crossings and shows exactly where the tracks are
questions.explanation: It functions like a yield sign at the tracks themselves.

citations.quote: This is known as a crossbuck sign. It is placed at all railroad grade crossings and shows exactly where the tracks are located.

questions.stem: The small sign mounted below a crossbuck shows:

options.text: The number of tracks at that crossing
The speed of trains on the line
The distance to the next crossing

questions.correctOption: The number of tracks at that crossing
questions.explanation: More than one track means a second train may be hidden behind the first.

citations.quote: They show the number of tracks at a particular crossing.

questions.stem: Flashing lights on a crossbuck mean:

options.text: A train is coming — stop and remain stopped until it has passed
A train has just passed and you may proceed
The signal is being tested

questions.correctOption: A train is coming — stop and remain stopped until it has passed
questions.explanation: Always stop when the lights are flashing, gates or no gates.

citations.quote: Flashing lights on a crossbuck mean that a train is coming. Always stop when the lights are flashing. Remain stopped until the train has passed.

questions.stem: At a crossing with gates, you must remain stopped until:

options.text: The last car of the train passes
The gates are raised and the lights stop flashing
The gate begins to lift

questions.correctOption: The gates are raised and the lights stop flashing
questions.explanation: The gates staying down after a train passes usually means a second train is coming.

citations.quote: Stop when the lights begin flashing and before the gate comes down. Remain stopped until the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing.

questions.stem: A white crossbuck and the letters RR painted on the pavement are:

options.text: A sign that the tracks are abandoned
A warning marker for a railroad grade crossing ahead
A no-parking marking

questions.correctOption: A warning marker for a railroad grade crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing markings also include a no-passing stripe and a stop line.

citations.quote: A white crossbuck and the letters RR are painted on the pavement as a warning marker for many railroad/highway grade crossings.

questions.stem: The Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign at a crossing is:

options.text: Round and yellow
Painted on the pavement
Normally blue, and located on the crossbuck post or signal post

questions.correctOption: Normally blue, and located on the crossbuck post or signal post
questions.explanation: It carries the number to call if your vehicle stalls on the tracks — that call can stop the trains.

citations.quote: The Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign, normally blue in color and may be located on the crossbuck post or signal post.

questions.stem: A stop sign posted at a railroad crossing means you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed only after looking both ways
Slow down and proceed if no train is visible
Stop only if the lights are flashing

questions.correctOption: Come to a complete stop and proceed only after looking both ways
questions.explanation: It is a stop sign like any other, with a train instead of cross traffic.

citations.quote: If you approach a railroad crossing at which a stop sign is posted, you must come to a complete stop and proceed across the tracks only after looking both ways to make sure a train is not approaching.

questions.stem: A yellow diamond warning sign showing tracks crossing a road just beyond an intersection warns that:

options.text: The intersection is closed
Railroad tracks cross one of the roadways just past the intersection
A train station is ahead

questions.correctOption: Railroad tracks cross one of the roadways just past the intersection
questions.explanation: It warns you not to turn onto a road and find yourself stopped on the tracks.

citations.quote: will be posted prior to intersections or crossroads where railroad tracks cross one of the roadways

questions.stem: Trains are required to sound a horn when they are approximately how far from a crossing?

options.text: 100 feet
5 miles
1,500 feet

questions.correctOption: 1,500 feet
questions.explanation: The horn is a warning, not a guarantee — the manual still tells you to look both ways.

citations.quote: Trains are required to signal a horn when they are approximately 1,500 feet from passing through a railroad crossing.

questions.stem: Violations of railroad signals or signs carry:

options.text: Only a written warning
The same penalties as violations of other traffic control devices
No penalty unless a train was present

questions.correctOption: The same penalties as violations of other traffic control devices
questions.explanation: And failure to stop at a railroad crossing is worth eight points on your record.

citations.quote: Violations of railroad signals or signs carry the same penalties as violations of other traffic control devices.

questions.stem: On a standard traffic signal, the lights from top to bottom are:

options.text: Yellow, green, red
Red, yellow, green
Green, yellow, red

questions.correctOption: Red, yellow, green
questions.explanation: Position matters as much as color — it is what lets a color-blind driver read the signal.

citations.quote: Standard traffic lights are red, yellow and green, from top to bottom respectively.

questions.stem: At a steady red light, unless otherwise posted, you may:

options.text: Proceed straight if no traffic is coming
Turn right after a complete stop when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present
Turn right without stopping if the way is clear

questions.correctOption: Turn right after a complete stop when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present
questions.explanation: Stop first, behind the crosswalk or stop line, and yield to everyone already there.

citations.quote: Stop behind crosswalk or stop line. Unless otherwise posted, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

questions.stem: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Prepare to stop — you must stop if it is safe to do so
Speed up to clear the intersection
The light is about to turn green

questions.correctOption: Prepare to stop — you must stop if it is safe to do so
questions.explanation: The manual adds the rule people ignore: do not speed up to beat the light.

citations.quote: You must stop if it is safe to do so. Do not speed up to beat the light.

questions.stem: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow you should:

options.text: Reverse out of the intersection
Continue cautiously through the intersection
Stop immediately

questions.correctOption: Continue cautiously through the intersection
questions.explanation: Stopping in the box strands you where the cross traffic is about to move.

citations.quote: do not stop, but continue cautiously through the intersection

questions.stem: Tennessee law requires a yellow light to be displayed for a minimum of:

options.text: Three seconds
One second
Ten seconds

questions.correctOption: Three seconds
questions.explanation: Three seconds is a minimum, not a promise — and it is not a window to accelerate into.

citations.quote: Tennessee law only requires the yellow light to be exhibited for a minimum of three seconds before the red light.

questions.stem: A green light means:

options.text: Go if the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles still in it
Go, regardless of what is in the intersection
Proceed only if turning

questions.correctOption: Go if the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles still in it
questions.explanation: Green is permission subject to the right-of-way rules, not a guarantee the way is clear.

citations.quote: Go IF the intersection is clear. You must yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection at light change.

questions.stem: A flashing red signal means:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution
The signal is out of service — ignore it
Complete stop, the same as a stop sign, then proceed when safe

questions.correctOption: Complete stop, the same as a stop sign, then proceed when safe
questions.explanation: Look both ways, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.

citations.quote: FLASHING RED Complete stop. Same as stop sign. Look both ways, yield to traffic and pedestrians and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.stem: A flashing yellow signal means:

options.text: Stop only if traffic is approaching
Slow down and proceed with caution at the intersection
Stop and wait for a green

questions.correctOption: Slow down and proceed with caution at the intersection
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow gives you the intersection with a warning attached; flashing red takes it away.

citations.quote: FLASHING YELLOW Slow down and proceed with caution at the intersection.

questions.stem: A green protected arrow means you:

options.text: Have the right-of-way and may drive only in the direction of the arrow
May turn or go straight
Must yield to oncoming traffic

questions.correctOption: Have the right-of-way and may drive only in the direction of the arrow
questions.explanation: You still yield to anyone already in the intersection when the arrow comes on.

citations.quote: When the arrow is green, you have the right-of-way and may drive the vehicle only in the direction of the arrow, after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.stem: When your turn arrow is red, or your lane has a red light:

options.text: You may turn after stopping
All turns are prohibited, even if other lanes have a green signal
You may turn if the path looks clear

questions.correctOption: All turns are prohibited, even if other lanes have a green signal
questions.explanation: A green in another lane is not permission for your lane.

citations.quote: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, all turns are prohibited. This is true even if other lanes of traffic have a green signal and your path through the intersection appears to be clear.

questions.stem: A flashing yellow arrow means you may:

options.text: Turn left with the right-of-way
Not turn at all
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic, bicyclists and pedestrians

questions.correctOption: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic, bicyclists and pedestrians
questions.explanation: Permissive, not protected: you wait for a safe gap yourself.

citations.quote: If you see a flashing yellow arrow,youareallowedtoturn left after yielding to all oncoming traffic and to any bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalk.

questions.stem: When a traffic signal is not working at all, Tennessee law requires you to treat the intersection as:

options.text: A yield-controlled intersection
An uncontrolled intersection where the larger road has priority
An all-way stop

questions.correctOption: An all-way stop
questions.explanation: Stop as if there were stop signs on every approach, then go in order of arrival.

citations.quote: Tennessee state law requires that if a signal is not working, the intersection is to be treated as if it were a ll-way stop intersection.

questions.stem: A pedestrian signal showing a raised hand or the words DON'T WALK means:

options.text: It is not safe to begin crossing
You may cross if you hurry
The signal is broken

questions.correctOption: It is not safe to begin crossing
questions.explanation: The walking person symbol or WALK is the signal to start.

citations.quote: When the pedestrian signal shows the words "DON’T WALK," or a symbol of a raised hand appears, it is not safe to begin crossing a street or intersection.

questions.stem: Over a lane, a red X signal means:

options.text: The lane is for turning only
The lane direction is about to change
You cannot drive in the lane below it

questions.correctOption: You cannot drive in the lane below it
questions.explanation: Green arrow means the lane is yours; flashing yellow X means turning only; steady yellow X means get out of it safely.

citations.quote: A green arrow means you can drive in the lane beneath it. • A red "X" means you CANNOT drive in the lane below. • A flashing yellow "X" means the lane is only for turning. • A steady yellow "X" means that the use/direction of the lane is changing and you should move out of it as soon as it is safe to do so.

questions.stem: A solid white line at the edge of the road marks:

options.text: The left edge of traffic going your way
A no-passing zone
The right edge of the traffic lane

questions.correctOption: The right edge of the traffic lane
questions.explanation: Yellow marks the left edge of traffic going your direction; white marks the right.

citations.quote: A solid white line indicates the right edge of the traffic lane on a road. A solid or broken yellow line indicates the left edge of traffic lanes going in your direction.

questions.stem: If you find yourself with a yellow line on your right and a white line on your left, you are:

options.text: In a shared center turn lane
Going the wrong way
In a passing zone

questions.correctOption: Going the wrong way
questions.explanation: Pull over immediately — the lines are telling you that you are facing oncoming traffic.

citations.quote: If you ever find yourself with yellow to your right and white to your left, you are going the wrong way.

questions.stem: A broken yellow center line means:

options.text: You may cross to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe
You may never cross
Passing is required

questions.correctOption: You may cross to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe
questions.explanation: The broken line marks a passing zone; the judgment about the gap is still yours.

citations.quote: Broken yellow lines mean that you MAY cross the line to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

questions.stem: Two solid yellow lines between lanes mean:

options.text: The road ahead is one-way
You may not cross from either direction, though you may cross to turn into a driveway
Passing is permitted for the faster vehicle

questions.correctOption: You may not cross from either direction, though you may cross to turn into a driveway
questions.explanation: No passing, even with no oncoming vehicle in sight — but turning across them into a driveway is allowed when safe.

citations.quote: Two solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic mean you MAY NOT cross the lines from either direction, even if no oncoming traffic is in view. You may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road if it is safe to do so.

questions.stem: Broken white lines between lanes mean:

options.text: You may cross to pass or change lanes when it is safe
You must stay in your lane
The lanes carry traffic in opposite directions

questions.correctOption: You may cross to pass or change lanes when it is safe
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same way; broken means crossing is allowed.

citations.quote: Broken white lines between lanes of traffic mean you may cross the lines to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.stem: A single solid white line between lanes means:

options.text: You may pass freely
The lane to your right is closed
You should stay in your lane and not cross to pass

questions.correctOption: You should stay in your lane and not cross to pass
questions.explanation: And you should not cross a double solid white line at all.

citations.quote: One solid white line between lanes of traffic means that you should stay in your lane and should not cross the line to pass (unless an emergency situation requires you to change lanes). Also, you should not cross a double solid white line.

questions.stem: White crosswalk lines painted across a road:

options.text: Show where you must stop at a signal
Indicate a pedestrian crossing area, which may be mid-block as well as at an intersection
Mark the boundary of a school zone

questions.correctOption: Indicate a pedestrian crossing area, which may be mid-block as well as at an intersection
questions.explanation: Not every crosswalk is painted — you must yield at unmarked ones too.

citations.quote: White crosswalk lines are painted across a road to indicate pedestrian crossing areas.

questions.stem: Where a stop line is painted across your lane, you must:

options.text: Stop with the front wheels on the line
Stop level with the traffic signal
Stop the vehicle behind the line

questions.correctOption: Stop the vehicle behind the line
questions.explanation: If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk; if there is no crosswalk, stop before your bumper crosses the edge line of the cross street.

citations.quote: (A) If the motorist is required to stop at the intersection, the vehicle must be stopped behind this stop line.

questions.stem: A diamond-shaped marking painted in the middle of a lane indicates:

options.text: A bicycle lane
A High Occupancy Vehicle lane
A bus stop

questions.correctOption: A High Occupancy Vehicle lane
questions.explanation: Signs beside the lane tell you the minimum occupancy and the hours it applies.

citations.quote: High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lanes are designated on highways by a diamond-shaped marking in the center of the lane.

questions.stem: A lane marked with a curved arrow and the word ONLY means:

options.text: You may turn or continue straight
Only buses may use the lane
You must turn in the direction of the arrow

questions.correctOption: You must turn in the direction of the arrow
questions.explanation: A lane marked with both a curved and a straight arrow lets you choose.

citations.quote: If you are traveling in a lane marked with a curved arrow and the word ONLY, you must turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.stem: Red reflectors facing you on the lane lines always mean:

options.text: You are facing traffic the wrong way and risk a head-on collision
The lane is closed ahead
There is a toll booth ahead

questions.correctOption: You are facing traffic the wrong way and risk a head-on collision
questions.explanation: Wrong-way reflectors are a last-chance warning at night on divided highways and ramps.

citations.quote: Red reflectors always mean you are facing traffic the wrong way and could have a head-on collision.

questions.stem: Where the center line has a solid yellow line on your side and a broken yellow line on the other side:

options.text: Both directions may pass
You may not pass
You are in a passing zone

questions.correctOption: You may not pass
questions.explanation: Read the line nearest you. Solid on your side means stay put.

citations.quote: you may not pass if the solid yellow line is on your side

questions.stem: Green is used as a background color for:

options.text: Guide signs and mileposts
Warning signs
Regulatory signs

questions.correctOption: Guide signs and mileposts
questions.explanation: Green tells you where you are and where things are — it never states a law.

citations.quote: GREEN is used as a background color for guide signs (other than those using brown or white), mileposts and as a legend color with a white background for permissive parking regulations.

questions.stem: A blue and red shield route marker means the route is:

options.text: A scenic byway
Part of the national system of interstate and defense highways
A state secondary route

questions.correctOption: Part of the national system of interstate and defense highways
questions.explanation: U.S. routes use a black-and-white shield; state routes use their own marker.

citations.quote: Blue and red signs, like the one on the right, indicate that the route is part of the national system of interstate and defense highways.

questions.stem: U.S. route markers consist of:

options.text: White numerals on a blue shield
Black numerals on a yellow diamond
Black numerals on a white shield surrounded by a black background

questions.correctOption: Black numerals on a white shield surrounded by a black background
questions.explanation: Learning the shield shapes lets you navigate by route number without reading every word.

citations.quote: U.S. Route signs consists of black numerals on a white shield surrounded by a black background without a border.

questions.stem: Interstate guide signs have:

options.text: A brown background with white letters
A green background with white letters and numbers
A blue background with white letters

questions.correctOption: A green background with white letters and numbers
questions.explanation: They carry the information you need to choose a lane and an exit in time.

citations.quote: The background is green with white letters and/or numbers visible at some distance.

questions.stem: If an interstate guide sign is marked EXIT ONLY:

options.text: Only trucks must exit
Traffic may exit or continue straight
All traffic in the lanes directly below the arrows must exit

questions.correctOption: All traffic in the lanes directly below the arrows must exit
questions.explanation: The yellow EXIT ONLY panel is the warning that your lane is leaving the highway whether you meant it to or not.

citations.quote: If an interstate guide sign is marked with the above sign, all traffic in the lane(s) directly below the arrows MUST exit.

questions.stem: Blue service signs direct motorists to:

options.text: Service facilities such as service stations, restaurants and motels
State parks and historic sites
Detour routes

questions.correctOption: Service facilities such as service stations, restaurants and motels
questions.explanation: Brown is the color for recreational and cultural destinations.

citations.quote: The blue color of these signs directs motorists to service facilities. Word message signs will also be used to direct motorists to areas where service stations, restaurants and motels are available.

questions.stem: Green background signs pointing to bike and hiking trails are:

options.text: Regulatory signs
Directional signs
Warning signs

questions.correctOption: Directional signs
questions.explanation: Green means guidance in every context — routes, distances and directions.

citations.quote: The green background signs indicate that the message is providing directional information.

questions.stem: Interstate reference markers in Tennessee's urban areas are installed:

options.text: Every 1,000 feet along heavily traveled sections
Every mile
Only at exits

questions.correctOption: Every 1,000 feet along heavily traveled sections
questions.explanation: They give the route number, the direction of travel and the log mile in tenths — enough for an emergency operator to find you.

citations.quote: the state has installed interstate reference markers every 1,000 feet along heavily traveled sections.

questions.stem: Dynamic message signs on Tennessee interstates provide:

options.text: Permanent speed limits
Real-time information on incidents, weather-related road conditions and construction ahead
Advertising for nearby businesses

questions.correctOption: Real-time information on incidents, weather-related road conditions and construction ahead
questions.explanation: They are updated as conditions change, so what they say outranks what you expected.

citations.quote: The signs provide real-time information to motorists of traffic incidents, weather-related road conditions or road construction ahead

questions.stem: The slow-moving vehicle emblem — an orange triangle with red reflective borders — appears on:

options.text: Farm tractors, machinery, construction equipment and horse-drawn vehicles
Emergency vehicles
School buses

questions.correctOption: Farm tractors, machinery, construction equipment and horse-drawn vehicles
questions.explanation: It means the vehicle ahead is travelling well below the limit — often under 25 m.p.h.

citations.quote: You may see this emblem on slow-moving vehicles, such as farm tractors, machinery, construction equipment

questions.stem: Signs along Tennessee's interstates reminding motorists to move damaged vehicles to the shoulder apply when:

options.text: The vehicles are undrivable
A trooper has authorized it
No serious injury has occurred

questions.correctOption: No serious injury has occurred
questions.explanation: Clearing the lanes prevents the secondary crash that so often follows the first.

citations.quote: reminding motorists to move their damaged vehicles to the shoulder if no serious injury has occurred
